# Engineering decisions taken

Internal Windows choices with no product visibility, decided under PORT_CONTRACT section 8
("ENGINEERING DECISION: a necessary internal implementation choice, justified against the
contract"). Each is recorded so it can be challenged. None changes observable behaviour; where a
choice would be visible to a user it was classified an owner decision instead and appears in
porting/owner_decisions_pending.md.

## ED-001

[LAUNCH] Is the website/tour capture subsystem ported at all? :: DECIDED: do not port it, and do not port the CaptureRun indirection either. SOURCE FACT: CaptureRun.outputDirectory (Core/Support/CaptureRun.swift:10-19) is a `static let` parsed once from CommandLine.arguments by exact match against exactly ['--website-captures','--tour-captures'], each requiring a following argument; nothing in the checkout writes CommandLine.arguments. With no flag, isEnabled is false (:27), storageRoot is nil (:30-32) and defaults is nil (:35-37). I checked every one of the 30 consumers: each is either `guard !isEnabled else { return }` (AppModel.swift:276, :1159, :1241, :1249; UpdateChecker.swift:133; MCPKeychain.swift:12; APIKeychain.swift:14; ProviderRegistry.swift:162, :176, :210, :538, :669, :703) or `CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard` / `CaptureRun.storageRoot ??` (Library.swift:200, ProviderRegistry.swift:161, :698, TokenLedger.swift:87, WindowChrome.swift:288, Storage.swift:20, AppSettings.swift:183, :696, :856). Every one collapses to the non-capture branch in every launch reachable through the shipped UI, so dropping the subsystem is observationally identical. port_impacts.md entry 90 is therefore WRONG as written: AppModel.notify and threadNeedsAttention do not need the indirection to survive, because the flag they bail on is a compile-time-constant false in a shipped launch. Route AppSettings, SidebarLayout, ShortcutStore, TokenLedger, ProviderRegistry and Storage through one settings store and one storage root with no capture branch. Justification against the contract: dead_code.md 33/38/42 prove unreachability; the contract gives dead code no requirement.

## ED-002

[LAUNCH] The source contributes no single-instance lock; macOS gets that behavior from Launch Services. Doing nothing on Windows is itself a divergence. :: DECIDED: implement a single-instance lock, and on the second launch run exactly the reopen path the source already defines. SOURCE FACT: a whole-tree grep for NSRunningApplication, LSMultipleInstances, flock and O_EXLOCK over DroppyCode/ and project.yml returns nothing, so no lock exists in source. But the user-visible behavior is not undefined: App/AppDelegate.swift:30-33 `applicationShouldHandleReopen` calls `WindowManager.shared.showMain()` when there are no visible windows, and App/Window/WindowManager.swift:26-30, :57-60 make that `NSApp.activate()` plus `makeKeyAndOrderFront`. So the second-launch behavior the user sees is: bring the existing main window forward and activate the app. Reproduce that. Doing nothing is not a neutral option: two processes would share one unsynchronised store root (Storage.swift:20) with last-writer-wins on the library, which is a C1/C4 path this decision avoids rather than creates. Record the lock in COMPATIBILITY as a platform binding, not a feature.

## ED-003

[LAUNCH] /usr/bin/sample has no Windows counterpart; the two verbatim failure bodies name a macOS tool. PA-0005 also still defers the Windows log location. :: DECIDED, because none of these strings reaches the user through the app. SOURCE FACT: I grepped the whole tree for `reportsFolder`, `Logs/Droppy Code` and `hang-`; the only hits are HangWatchdog's own writer (Core/Support/HangWatchdog.swift:86, :89, :118-121, :125) and two comments. Nothing in the app reads, lists, opens or surfaces a hang report, so "sample could not run: <error>" (:111) and "sample exited with status <n>" (:108) are diagnostic file content, not UI text. DECISIONS: (1) the two bodies become the Windows capturer's own wording, with the same two failure cases and the same position (prepended to the body, and sole-body-plus-newline respectively); (2) the three header lines stay byte-identical in shape - "<AppInfo.name> main thread unresponsive for %.1fs", "Version <short> (<build>)", "Sampled at <Date()>", then a blank line (:91-93) - with the hardcoded "Droppy Code" at :91 following AppInfo.name under OD-0002; (3) keep every number exactly: 0.5 s ping (:52), 4 s stallThreshold (:24), 2 s sample window (:28), 10 kept reports (:32), one report per stall (:74-75), filename `hang-<ISO8601 with ':' replaced by '-'>.txt` (:88-89), oldest-first trim by sorted name (:124-128); (4) PA-0005 closes as %LOCALAPPDATA%\\<AppInfo.name>\\Logs, the per-user application log location, since ~/Library/Logs has no roaming counterpart.

## ED-004

[LAUNCH] The 4 minute quit deferral cannot be honoured under a Windows logoff or shutdown. :: DECIDED: reproduce the deferral exactly on the ordinary quit path, and request the OS grace on session end without claiming it. SOURCE FACT: App/AppDelegate.swift:38-48 returns .terminateNow unless model.isAnyHydraMergeRunning, otherwise .terminateLater with a 250 ms poll (:43) against a deadline of `Date.now.addingTimeInterval(4 * 60)` (:41); :50-55 then runs saveBeforeQuit(), TokenLedger.shared.flushLiveSpend() and MCPHub.terminateAll() in that order. DECISIONS: (1) on WM_CLOSE and on the app's own Exit, honour the full 250 ms / 4 minute contract and then run the three shutdown steps in that exact order; (2) on WM_QUERYENDSESSION call ShutdownBlockReasonCreate while a merge is running so the OS shows why, keep polling at 250 ms, and on WM_ENDSESSION run the three shutdown steps immediately regardless of the remaining deadline; (3) record in COMPATIBILITY that the cap is honoured for an ordinary quit and truncated to the OS grace period at session end. No product visibility beyond a shutdown the OS is already forcing.

## ED-005

[LAUNCH] SwitchLatency is shipped, non-#if-guarded code that is inert outside the dev bundle id; is the dev instrumentation kept? :: DECIDED: do not port it; replace the requirement with a recorded no-op. SOURCE FACT: Core/Support/SwitchLatency.swift:20-21 is `guard AppInfo.isDevelopment, observer == nil else { return }`, and Core/Support/Text.swift:5 makes isDevelopment `Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier == "iordv.droppycode.dev"`, which project.yml:56 shows is the separate Dev target. With observer nil, note(_:) (:43) and noteSwitch(to:) (:49) both return immediately, so in a release build the entire file's observable behavior is nothing at all: no UI, no file, no log line. Its only output even in the dev app is os_log on subsystem "iordv.droppycode" category "switch" plus a points-of-interest signpost - developer instrumentation, not product. Dropping it is invisible to every user of the shipped artifact. If the port later wants equivalent instrumentation it may add its own; that is not this requirement.

## ED-006

[WIN] The defaults key holding the main window frame is an AppKit convention, not a source fact; only the autosave NAME is in source. :: DECIDED: the port defines its own key; nothing migrates. SOURCE FACT: App/Window/WindowManager.swift:24 is the whole of it, `private static let mainFrameName = "DroppyCodeMainWindow"`, used at :67 `setFrameUsingName` and :70 `setFrameAutosaveName`; the defaults key AppKit derives from it is not in the tree. The user-visible contract IS in source and is what must be reproduced: on first run with no stored frame, the window opens at 1320x860 (:19) centered (:68); thereafter it restores its saved frame; the content minimum is 860x560 (:20, :66). Store that frame under one key of the port's own choosing in the single settings store, keyed to the main window only. No migration is possible or attempted: there is no macOS profile to read on a Windows machine, and the name carries the old product identity. Zero product visibility - the user sees the window come back where they left it either way.

## ED-007

[WIN] fitTitlebar and the titlebar frameDidChange observer reach into AppKit's private titlebar hierarchy; there is no Windows view to fit. :: DECIDED: implement the OUTCOME as a constant-height caption band and drop the AppKit plumbing. SOURCE FACT: the observable purpose is stated in the source's own words at UI/Chrome/WindowChrome.swift:140-147 - AppKit hands a click or hover to a caption button only inside the title bar's own bounds, its bar stops short of buttons levelled with the chrome, and the clicks fell through. fitTitlebar (:161-172) therefore grows the container to `titlebarHeight` keeping its top edge, where titlebarHeight = Chrome.sheetInset + Chrome.chromeTopPadding + Chrome.capsuleHeight = 0 + 12 + 32 = 44 (:148-150 with Chrome.swift:11, :32, :33-34, :38). DECISION: on Windows the WM_NCHITTEST caption band is a fixed 44 device-independent pixels from the window's top edge, recomputed on resize and on DPI change; every chrome control keeps a NoWindowDragArea equivalent so a press on a control never drags the window (:145-147). The private-hierarchy probe (:153-155), the frameDidChange observer (:62-66, :77-87) and its one-queued-fit coalescing (:80-84) do NOT port: they exist only because AppKit re-tiles the bar, which Windows does not do. Preserve the one part that IS observable: the unanimated re-place after a live resize ends (:91-95). No product visibility; re-examine only if the chosen stack draws its own non-client area differently.

## ED-008

[SIDEBAR] The reorder alignment haptic has no Windows desktop equivalent; does the owner want a substitute cue? :: DECIDED: omit it, add nothing. SOURCE FACT: App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:799 is the single site, `NSHapticFeedbackManager.defaultPerformer.perform(.alignment, performanceTime: .now)`, fired once per accepted swap. Windows has no desktop haptic channel: the API surface is limited to game controllers and pen/touch digitizers, neither of which a mouse-driven sidebar reorder goes through. The two options are omit, or invent a substitute cue (a click sound, a flash) that has no counterpart in the source. The contract's no-invention rule decides it: omit. Specify PR-SIDEBAR-053 as absent on Windows with this reasoning attached, and record it in COMPATIBILITY as a platform capability gap rather than a design choice. If the owner later wants a cue, that is a new feature request, not this requirement.

## ED-009

[SIDEBAR] Search uses Swift lowercased() and the picker uses localizedCaseInsensitiveContains; does a Windows ordinal-ignore-case comparison agree? :: DECIDED: they are two different comparisons and must be implemented as two different comparisons; ordinal-ignore-case is wrong for both. SOURCE FACT: the sidebar search folds with `lowercased()` then `contains` - query at App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:739, project name at :742, thread titles at :744 against the cache built at :2653. Swift's `lowercased()` is Unicode FULL, locale-INDEPENDENT default case conversion, which can change string length. The picker path uses `localizedCaseInsensitiveContains`, which is locale-SENSITIVE. DECISIONS: (1) implement `lowercased()` as Unicode Default Case Conversion with no locale tailoring - in a JS/TS stack that is exactly `String.prototype.toLowerCase()`; never ordinal case folding, never a locale-tailored ToLower, because Turkish dotless-i tailoring and simple-vs-full mapping of U+0130 both diverge from Swift; (2) implement `localizedCaseInsensitiveContains` as a locale-sensitive collator search at secondary strength in the user's current locale - in a JS/TS stack `Intl.Collator(undefined, {usage:'search', sensitivity:'accent'})`; (3) add the pinning fixture both requirements already call for, covering at minimum U+0130, U+0131, the final sigma pair, and a combining-mark case, and assert the two comparisons disagree where the source makes them disagree. Not a product choice: the user-visible contract is 'matches the same strings the source matches', and these are the implementations that satisfy it.

## ED-010

[SIDEBAR] The scroll freeze lifts immediately on an .idle scroll phase, but WM_MOUSEWHEEL has no scroll-end signal. :: DECIDED: the 150 ms debounce is the sole governor for wheel input; wire a scroll-end to the immediate lift only where the input stack actually reports one. SOURCE FACT: the freeze's only effect is `.allowsHitTesting(!isListScrolling)` on the list (App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:115). It is raised by noteListScroll() (:391-403), which sets the flag once per scroll and re-arms a 150 ms settle task on every movement (:397-402), and it is lifted either by that task or immediately by `.onScrollPhaseChange` when phase == .idle, which also cancels the task (:140-143). DECISION: on Windows, a raw wheel scroll lifts the freeze 150 ms after the last tick, exactly the debounce the source already runs for a scroll that has not reported idle; where the stack does surface a terminal scroll phase (precision touchpad through Direct Manipulation, or a pointer-event sequence with a terminal phase), route it to the immediate lift so that path matches the source exactly. Worst observable difference: up to 150 ms of ignored clicks after the last wheel tick, on wheel input only. Record in COMPATIBILITY.

## ED-011

[SIDEBAR] Chrome.glideSpring's settlingDuration drives the glide's handover; will a Windows spring solver compute the same value for response 0.6 / damping 0.86? :: DECIDED: derive the handover from the solver's own settle time, never hardcode a macOS-measured constant. SOURCE FACT: UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift:106 is `Spring(response: 0.6, dampingRatio: 0.86)`; App/Views/Sidebar/RowGlide.swift:18 aliases it, :225 drives the keyframes with it, and :228-236 is the whole contract - sleep for `max(spring.settlingDuration - 0.12, 0)`, then arrive(), then sleep 0.12, then finish(). The comments at :114-115 and :229-230 state the intent plainly: the real row comes back under the ghost's last frames so the handover never shows a gap, and the ghost goes once the keyframes have run their course. DECISION: (1) implement the spring with the same parameterisation, angular frequency omega0 = 2*pi/response = 10.472 rad/s and zeta = 0.86; (2) define settlingDuration analytically as the time the envelope decays to 1/1000 of the initial displacement, ln(1000)/(zeta*omega0), approximately 0.767 s for these values, and pin that in a unit test; (3) compute the 0.12 s handover FROM that value at runtime, so if the solver's settle time is ever retuned the ghost is still removed after the animation visually ends and never before. The failure the source is guarding against is a visible gap or a ghost outliving its motion; both are avoided by the derivation, not by matching Apple's number. AttachmentFlight.swift:102 uses the same property and takes the same treatment.

## ED-012

[CHAT] The drift, blank-repair, viewport-nudge and stack-generation machinery exists to correct a virtualized list built against a remembered viewport; is any of it needed on Windows? :: DECIDED: the timeline list derives its visible range from the LIVE scroll offset every frame, and these four are then recorded as NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_EVIDENCE rather than implemented. Justification: all four exist only to correct an artefact of SwiftUI's lazy stack building rows against a remembered viewport - PR-CHAT-056 tells the lazy list where the viewport is once accumulated drift passes a tolerance, PR-CHAT-167 rebuilds the list from scratch by bumping a generation identity. None of them is a product behavior a user asked for; the user-visible contract is 'the rows on screen are the rows at the current scroll offset, and none is blank'. A list whose visible range is computed from the live offset satisfies that contract directly and makes the corrections dead by construction. REQUIRED FORM OF THE RECORD, so this is not a quiet drop: each of the four keeps its requirement, states the tolerance, the nudge and the generation bump as specified from source, and carries an explicit note naming the design property that makes it a no-op. If the chosen stack turns out to virtualize against a remembered viewport after all, the four become live and must be implemented as specified. No product visibility either way.

## ED-013

[CHAT] Chrome tokens resolve from ThemeManager.spec, but SwiftUI's .primary/.secondary/.tertiary/.quaternary and the view tint resolve inside AppKit at draw time and are not numerically observable from source. :: DECIDED: resolve each hierarchical level as a fixed opacity over the theme's resolved foreground, pinned as four named tokens in one place, and ship the result labelled UNVERIFIED. The split the agent drew is right and needs no ruling for its first half: Chrome.accent, Chrome.warning, Chrome.danger, Chrome.success and Chrome.glassTint all resolve through ThemeManager.spec and are exact source facts. For the four hierarchical levels, OD-0001 has already closed the only branch that could have measured them on a Mac, so an owner ruling would produce nothing; what is needed is a method, and that is mine to set. DECISIONS: (1) define exactly four tokens, one per level, as opacity multipliers over the resolved foreground colour, defined once and referenced everywhere, so a later correction is a single edit rather than an audit of every pill and label; (2) seed their values by sampling the eight real macOS screenshots of the running app that OD-0004 found inside the pinned tree (tour-themes@2x.png in particular shows one chat in four themes with secondary labels, inline code and card fills visible), and record the sampling as the evidence; (3) resolve the SwiftUI view tint from ThemeTint (App/Window/WindowManager.swift:180-189), which sets `content.tint(theme.spec.accent)` with a nil tint meaning the system accent; (4) mark every affected requirement UNVERIFIED per UNK-0003 and name it in the final report. This affects rendered colour only, never structure.

## ED-014

[COMPOSER] PR-COMPOSER-084 carries upstream_defect "51, 52" because two defect entries describe one inseparable behavior; must the record be split? :: DECIDED: keep it as ONE requirement and make the schema carry the list. The agent's reasoning is right and splitting is the worse option: defects 51 and 52 - the reduce-motion early-return ordering and the take-before-fly consumption - are two descriptions of one code path with one failure scenario, so splitting would produce two requirements with identical failure scenarios, which is exactly the duplication the spec is supposed to avoid and which makes a later reviewer think one of them is redundant and drop it. If the schema currently types upstream_defect as a single scalar, widen it to a list of defect ids rather than fracturing the requirement; a spec schema is an internal artefact with no product visibility, so this is mine to settle. Requirement: PR-COMPOSER-084 stays single and references both ids; if the tooling cannot yet take a list, the record carries both ids in one string and a schema fix is filed, not a split.

## ED-015

[COMPOSER] COMPOSER.json:1905 contains one em dash inside a verbatim quotation of ModelOption.chipName's separator table; the Marrow repository forbids em dashes. :: DECIDED: no lint exception is needed, and the character must not be stripped. SOURCE FACT: Core/Models/Provider.swift:252-256 is `for separator in [" (", " · ", " — ", " – ", " - ", ": "]` and it takes the text BEFORE the first match - the separators are MATCHING INPUT applied to a model name the provider supplied, never text the app emits. So this is neither UI text nor prose; it is a lookup table whose bytes must match or the chip name comes out wrong for any model whose name contains an em dash. DECISIONS: (1) the six separators port byte for byte, in that exact order, and the order matters because " - " would otherwise never be reached for a name containing " — "; (2) in the Windows source, write the two dash separators as the escapes "—" and "–", which satisfies `npm run lint:text` literally while producing identical bytes at runtime, so no exception is filed; (3) the spec JSON under porting/ is not in lint:text's scope (it covers .ts, .tsx, .mts, .mjs and .css under src, scripts, tests and resources), so COMPOSER.json:1905 needs no change. Specify the vendor-prefix list at :258 in the same requirement, since it runs on the result.

## ED-016

[THEME] The file chooser's confirm-button caption "Use as Wallpaper" is settable on macOS; will the Windows common dialog honour a custom OK caption? :: DECIDED, and the platform does support it, so the caption stays verbatim. SOURCE FACT: App/Views/Settings/WallpaperCard.swift:168-182 configures an NSOpenPanel with allowedContentTypes = WallpaperStore.acceptedTypes (:171), allowsMultipleSelection false (:172), canChooseDirectories false (:173), `panel.message = "Choose a picture for the window"` (:174) and `panel.prompt = "Use as Wallpaper"` (:175), then runs it as a sheet on the key window when there is one (:176-181). DECISIONS: (1) the confirm button caption is set through IFileDialog::SetOkButtonLabel, which is available on every Windows version this port supports, so "Use as Wallpaper" ships verbatim with its exact casing; (2) the second string at :174 has no exact counterpart - map it to the dialog's title (IFileDialog::SetTitle) rather than dropping it, since that is where it is read; (3) keep single-selection, files-only and the same accepted type list; (4) present it modal to the window the card is in, matching the sheet-versus-modeless branch at :176-182. Only if a supported shell version were found to ignore the label would that become a recorded limitation - never a licence to reword.

## ED-017

[RUNTIME] Q45 [RUNTIME] The pinned checkout does not compile: four sessions emit .tokenSpend(TokenSpend(...)) but ProviderEvent declares 30 cases with no such member. Which side of the mid-refactor? :: SOURCE FACT, verified: ProviderSession.swift:82-118 is the only `enum ProviderEvent` in the tree (whole-tree grep) and declares 30 cases, none named tokenSpend. The four emit sites are AntigravitySession.swift:308, CommandCodeSession.swift:350, CopilotSession.swift:554, OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:494. `git show dec91b23a --stat` ('Add token spend tracking and Hydra metrics', the commit directly under the pinned merge) touches 14 files and does NOT touch ProviderSession.swift, so the case was never added. DECISION, and it is free of product visibility because the event has no consumer: a whole-tree grep for `case .tokenSpend` returns nothing, and TokenLedger.record(_ spend: TokenSpend, on:) at TokenLedger.swift:114 has no caller either. What actually feeds the user-visible token UI is the Int overload TokenLedger.record(spend:) at TokenLedger.swift:107, called on the line immediately above each broken emit (AntigravitySession.swift:307, CommandCodeSession.swift:348, CopilotSession.swift:550, OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:491) plus ClaudeSession.swift:574 and CodexSession.swift:608/:610/:619/:621, and read by TokenActivitySection.swift:38. Therefore: implement ProviderEvent with exactly the 30 committed cases; do NOT port the four `.tokenSpend(...)` emissions (never-built code, no consumer, no observable effect); DO port the adjacent TokenLedger.shared.record(spend:) Int calls verbatim. Adding a 31st case would be observationally identical but would put a member in the spec that the pinned enum does not have. Record a new UNK id noting the checkout does not compile, for the register's sake only.

## ED-018

[RUNTIME] Q46 [RUNTIME] TurnRecord.tokenSpends is declared and decoded but never assigned; its one reader always renders empty. Adopting the 31-case enum would start writing it. :: SOURCE FACT, verified: `tokenSpends` occurs exactly three times in the tree - declared at Timeline.swift:269, decoded at Timeline.swift:292, read at HydraRunMetricsView.swift:135. No assignment anywhere. DECISION, following Q45: keep the field declared and decoded (so a document written by a build that knew it still reads), never assign it, and let HydraRunMetricsView.swift:135 render empty exactly as the pinned build does. Since Q45 drops the four emissions, nothing can start writing it, so the behavior change the question fears cannot arise. No owner input needed: both branches are invisible, and this one is the pinned build's observable state.

## ED-019

[RUNTIME] Q50 [RUNTIME] ToolTitles.relativePath and TouchedPaths.relative do forward-slash, case-sensitive byte-prefix comparison; a literal port reports zero changed files on Windows. :: SOURCE FACT, verified: ToolTitles.relativePath at ProviderSession.swift:188-191 (`root.hasSuffix("/") ? root : root + "/"`, then `path.hasPrefix(normalizedRoot)`); TouchedPaths.relative at TouchedPaths.swift:19-28 (tilde expansion, `path.hasPrefix("/")` as the absoluteness test, standardizingPath, same slash-suffixed prefix compare). DECISION, one rule for the whole port, no product visibility because the observable contract ('a path inside the checkout is shown and attributed relative to the root') is preserved exactly: (1) COMPARE on a normalized form - convert both sides to forward slashes, resolve to an absolute path, and compare with a locale-invariant lowercase fold, because NTFS is case-insensitive; (2) treat absoluteness as drive-qualified (`X:\`, `X:/`) or UNC (`\\`), replacing the `hasPrefix("/")` test; (3) RETURN forward slashes from TouchedPaths.relative, because every consumer of its output uses forward slashes - TouchedPaths.isBuildOutput splits on "/" (:40), TouchedPaths.matches compares `"/" + path` against DiffFile paths (:55-58), and git's own diff output is forward-slash; (4) RETURN the untouched tail of the caller's original string from ToolTitles.relativePath, so a display title keeps whatever separators the provider emitted. Keep every literal (the trailing-slash normalization, the `://` refusal, the empty-string guards, buildOutputNames' 15 entries) verbatim.

## ED-020

[PROVCLI] Q54 [PROVCLI] Command Code's executableName is the bare `cmd`; on Windows PATH+PATHEXT finds C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe first. Which identity signal, and where does the CLI install? :: Source supplies more than the question credits. SOURCE FACT, verified: ProviderRegistry.swift:240 already knows the CLI by three names, in order - `for name in ["command-code", "commandcode", "cmd"] { if let found = LoginEnvironment.which(name) ... }` - under the comment at :236-237 calling `cmd` 'the documented alias' and `command-code`/`commandcode` 'the package's own' names. ProviderKind.executableName is `"cmd"` at Provider.swift:51. DECISION, no probe and no invention needed: on Windows, resolve Command Code by trying `command-code`, then `commandcode`, then `cmd`, in exactly the order and with exactly the names ProviderRegistry.swift:240 already uses, and reject any candidate whose resolved directory is under %SystemRoot% (System32 or SysWOW64), which is where the interpreter lives and where no npm-installed CLI ever lands. That is one Windows fact needing no probe plus three source-supplied names; it hard-codes no install directory and needs no version query or handshake. The user-visible contract - 'Command Code shows as installed exactly when the real CLI is present' - is preserved, which the literal `cmd` order cannot achieve on any Windows PC. Keep executableName = "cmd" as the declared value; the reorder lives in the Windows resolver, not in the model.

## ED-021

[PROVCLI] Q57 [PROVCLI] The shipped Command Code mod's orphan test is `process.ppid === 1`, a POSIX idiom with no Windows meaning; a stranded gate waits the full six hours. :: SOURCE FACT, verified at CommandCodeAPI.swift:428-431: `if (process.ppid === 1 || Date.now() - started > 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000) { try { fs.unlinkSync(request) } catch {}; return {block: true, additionalContext: 'Droppy Code did not answer.'} }`. DECISION, and it cannot widen the gate because BOTH disjuncts return the same `block: true`: replace only the predicate `process.ppid === 1` with a Windows-correct liveness test of the same parent - `(() => { try { process.kill(process.ppid, 0); return false } catch (e) { return e.code === 'ESRCH' } })()`. Under libuv on Windows process.ppid is captured at start and never becomes 1, so the literal test can never fire; the signal-0 probe expresses the identical intent ('the app is gone, give up now'). Keep the 6-hour cap, the unlink, the `block: true` and the additionalContext string byte-identical apart from the approved product-identity rename. The only failure mode is Windows pid reuse making a dead parent look alive, which degrades to the 6-hour cap - the current behavior - and never toward permitting. This is not a product change to the gate: the gate's decision, its strings and its fail-closed direction are untouched.

## ED-022

[PROVCLI] Q58 [PROVCLI] Four paths hand a Windows filesystem path to a CLI that loads it as a module: Command Code's `--mod <path>` and its bridge import, Pi's `-e <path>` and its bridge import. :: The four paths are two different problems and one of them needs no probe. SOURCE FACT, verified: the flags pass bare filesystem paths - CommandCodeSession.swift:164 `arguments += ["--mod", modURL.path]` and PiSession.swift:92 `var arguments = ["--mode", "rpc", "-e", extensionURL.path]`; the bridges use Node dynamic import of an env var - PiCLI.swift:169 `await import(process.env.DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE)` and CommandCodeAPI.swift:388-390 `const bridgePath = process.env.DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE; if (bridgePath) { import(bridgePath)... }`. DECISION (a), bridges, determinate from Node's documented behavior: `import('C:\\...')` throws ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME because 'C:' parses as a scheme, so on Windows the app sets DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE to `pathToFileURL(bridgePath).href`. Both shipped mods then load with their TypeScript byte-identical - no edit to either mod. DECISION (b), flags: pass the bare Windows path, exactly as `.path` does, because `--mod` and `-e` are filesystem-path options in every CLI convention and a file URL there would be the invention. Make (b) the first assertion of the Gate E Windows probe; it is invisible to the user unless it fails outright, so it is not an owner call.

## ED-023

[PROVCLI] Q60 [PROVCLI] CommandCodeAPI interpolates AppInfo.name into its support directory while PiCLI hard-codes 'Droppy Code/pi'; a renamed build scatters helper files across two roots. :: SOURCE FACT, verified: CommandCodeAPI.swift:443 `base.appendingPathComponent("\(AppInfo.name)/CommandCode", isDirectory: true)` versus PiCLI.swift:17 `base.appendingPathComponent("Droppy Code/pi", isDirectory: true)`; AppInfo.name is Text.swift:4, `CFBundleDisplayName` with the fallback 'Droppy Code', and project.yml:44 sets it to 'Droppy Code' in the shipping configuration (project.yml:56 sets 'Droppy Code Dev' in the dev one). DECISION: route both through the port's single app-data root, i.e. reproduce the CommandCodeAPI form for both, giving `<AppData>\Marrow\CommandCode` and `<AppData>\Marrow\pi`. [PROVCLI] Q63 [PROVCLI] Copilot de-duplicates reasoning text by Swift hashValue, which is randomly seeded per process; the port must not turn it into a persisted key. :: SOURCE FACT, verified at CopilotSession.swift:1068: `text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).hashValue`. The contract the source actually relies on is exactly two properties: stable within one run, never persisted. That satisfies both properties exactly, holds nothing across runs, and removes the only way the upstream form can misbehave - a 64-bit collision silently suppressing a distinct reasoning text. The observable difference requires such a collision inside a single turn's reasoning stream, which has never been observed and is not a behavior anyone specified. ## ED-027

[PROVACP] Q68 [PROVACP] StdioProcess.terminate's three-second graceful window has no Windows equivalent: TerminateProcess behaves like SIGKILL, so the first step is already forceful and the second redundant. :: SOURCE FACT, verified at StdioProcess.swift:114-122: stdin is closed on the write queue FIRST, then `process.terminate()` (SIGTERM), then SIGKILL at +3 seconds if still running. DECISION: preserve all three steps and the 3-second timing on Windows, in that order. Step 1 carries the real weight and ports exactly - for a stdio-protocol CLI, closing stdin IS the documented shutdown trigger, and it gives the child the same flush window the SIGTERM was there to provide. Step 2 becomes Node's subprocess.kill(), which on Windows is TerminateProcess with exit code 1; step 3 is then a no-op guarded by the same isRunning check, which is harmless and keeps the structure and the timing observable-identical. Do not collapse the wait: shortening it would make a CLI that flushes on shutdown lose output faster on Windows than on macOS, which is exactly the divergence the agent was protecting against. Record the SIGTERM/TerminateProcess collapse in COMPATIBILITY. Whether any of the four CLIs does anything on SIGTERM is worth capturing in the Gate E run, but the answer cannot make the wait wrong, only unnecessary.

[PROVAPI] Q77 [PROVAPI] UNK-0005 blocks implementation of five requirements: the three API-key environment variables, run_command, the grep argument vector and /bin/zsh -lc. :: SOURCE FACT, verified: run_command at OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:1154-1165 runs `/bin/zsh` with `["-lc", trimmed]`, cwd = workingDirectory, timeout 120, outputLimit 24_000, then re-clips with `if output.utf8.count > 24_000 { output = "…" + String(output.suffix(24_000)) }`; searchText runs `/usr/bin/grep` at :1136-1144 with timeout 30 and outputLimit 64_000 and caps at `lines.prefix(120)`. [HYDRA] Q95 [HYDRA] The worktree folder slug replaces spaces only; Windows forbids characters macOS allows, and writer and sweeper must agree. :: DECIDED. Decision: add one shared function `hydraSlug(_:)` used at BOTH sites and nowhere else. It performs, in order: (1) replace U+0020 with "-", (2) lowercase, (3) replace each of < > : " / \ | ? * and every character U+0000-U+001F with "-". Nothing else. Justification against the contract: step 3 is the minimum Windows requires and is invisible to the user for every project name macOS and Windows both accept, so parity is exact on the whole overlapping domain. Mapping to "-" rather than deleting is safe because the sweeper strips the slug by prefix length before it counts hyphen-separated parts, so extra hyphens inside the slug cannot change the parts arithmetic. No trailing-dot or reserved-device-name handling is needed: the folder name is always "<slug>-<persona>-<8 hex>", so the slug is never the last component and never stands alone. [HYDRA] Q96 [HYDRA] hydraProject tests absoluteness with hasPrefix("/") and walks up to "/"; tilde expansion has no analogue. :: DECIDED, and port_impacts.md:172 entry 82 already records the shape. [MCP] Q111 [MCP] The installed bridge calls spawn(entry.command) with no shell; a bare "npx" on Windows is npx.cmd, which Node will not launch. :: DECIDED; this does not need the owner. It is still an engineering decision and not an owner one, because the user-visible alternatives are "local MCP servers work" and "local MCP servers never work" - no owner would choose the second, and nothing else about the product changes. ## ED-043

[MCP] Q115 [MCP] MCPProxy relays an event stream as one HTTP chunk per byte; can a Windows HTTP stack express the same observable timing? :: DECIDED. Source verified at MCPProxy.swift:382-396: for a text/event-stream response it appends Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Connection: close, sends the status head, then for each byte of the stream sends a frame of exactly Data("1\r\n") + the byte + Data("\r\n"), and finally "0\r\n\r\n" before connection.cancel(). Decision: reproduce the FRAMING byte for byte - one 1-byte HTTP chunk per source byte, same terminator, same two headers in the same order - with one write call per frame. That is the only part any MCP client can observe; a chunked-encoding parser reconstructs an identical byte stream regardless of how TCP segments it. Do NOT set TCP_NODELAY: MCPProxy.swift sets no NWProtocolTCP options at all (the only NWParameters fields touched are at :100-103), so its connections run with Nagle at the platform default, and adding setNoDelay(true) on Windows would be a deliberate timing divergence, not parity. Record in COMPATIBILITY that TCP segmentation is not controlled and is not observable at the HTTP layer.

## ED-044

[GIT] Q121 [GIT] GitFileStamp.identifier is systemFileNumber, with no direct Windows equivalent. :: DECIDED. Source: Git.swift:498-504, `identifier = (attributes?[.systemFileNumber] as? NSNumber)?.uint64Value`, alongside modified, size, and `overrides = (environment["GIT_DIR"] ?? "") + "\u{0}" + (environment["GIT_INDEX_FILE"] ?? "")`. The struct's whole job is cache invalidation for a resolved git index path - it answers "is this the same file as last time", nothing more. Decision: identifier = the pair (volume serial, file index) read via fs.statSync(path, { bigint: true }) as (dev, ino), combined into one value; when ino is 0 or the stat throws, set identifier to null. Justification against the contract: (a) ino/dev on Windows Node are GetFileInformationByHandle's nFileIndexHigh/Low and dwVolumeSerialNumber, which is the exact NTFS analogue of systemFileNumber; (b) the null fallback is not an invention - it is precisely what the source already does when the attribute is absent, since `as? NSNumber` yields nil and the stamp then discriminates on modified + size + overrides alone. That degraded path is therefore reproduced, not designed, and it covers the cases where a Windows file index is unreliable (FAT, some network shares). Nothing user-visible changes; the worst effect either way is one redundant index-path re-resolution.

All four adopt one exported absoluteness predicate - drive-rooted /^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]/, UNC /^\\\\[^\\/]+[\\/][^\\/]+/, or a \\?\ prefix - and one path-normalization step (backslashes to forward slashes, \\?\ stripped, drive letter upper-cased) applied before any comparison. A bare leading "\" stays non-absolute and is joined onto the root, keeping the source's conservative direction. The root-containment comparison becomes case-insensitive per Q104(2); the absoluteness test itself is case-insensitive only in the drive letter. The critical constraint is that all four sites plus hydraProject share ONE implementation: the source's bug surface here is symmetric and splitting the rule would create a path the merge counts as inside and the diff counts as outside, or the reverse.

## ED-046

[TERM] Q126 [TERM] foregroundJobIsTheShell reads kp_eproc.e_tpgid against e_pgid via sysctl; ConPTY exposes neither. :: DECIDED. Source: TerminalStore.swift:69-76 - guard shell > 0, sysctl [CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID, shell] into a kinfo_proc, return `info.kp_eproc.e_tpgid == info.kp_eproc.e_pgid`, and false on any failure. Its one caller is TerminalPanel.swift:339-346: a local keyDown monitor that, for keyCode 53 with no allowed modifiers and the terminal view as first responder, calls onEscapeAtPrompt() and SWALLOWS the event (return nil) only when the shell owns the foreground; otherwise it returns the event and Escape reaches the terminal. So false-when-unknown means Escape always goes through to the terminal and the panel shortcut never fires - the safe direction, and the source's own on-failure answer. Decision: approximate, do not give up. On each Escape, enumerate live descendants of the ConPTY child PID (a snapshot of the process tree, or the shell's Job Object accounting if the shell is launched in one) and return true when the shell has no live descendant. Default to FALSE on any error, empty result, or enumeration timeout, exactly reproducing the source's fail-closed branch. Justification: the alternative - hard-coding false - silently deletes a shipped shortcut, and the approximation is correct in every ordinary case (a bare prompt has no children; vim, less or a CLI agent is a child). It is wrong only where the shell keeps a stopped background job, where the source would say true and this says false, i.e. it errs in the direction the source itself errs on failure. This must be labelled a DEVIATION in COMPATIBILITY, not parity.

## ED-047

[TERM] Q127 [TERM] Two deliberately different termination ladders, neither of which Windows can express in signals. :: DECIDED, and the difference is preserved. Source verified: Shell.terminate (Shell.swift:110-118) - guard isRunning, process.terminate() [SIGTERM to the child], then 1 second later on a utility queue `kill(getpgid(pid) == pid ? -pid : pid, SIGKILL)`, i.e. the whole process GROUP when the child leads one, else the single pid. StdioProcess.terminate (StdioProcess.swift:115-123) - close the stdin write handle FIRST, guard isRunning, process.terminate(), then 3 seconds later `kill(process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL)`, single PID only, no group. Decision: (a) Shell - spawn each child in its own Job Object; graceful step = CTRL_BREAK_EVENT to the child's process group (spawned with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP), which is the only signal Windows can deliver to a console child and the nearest analogue of SIGTERM; after 1 second, TerminateJobObject, which kills the tree and is the faithful expression of the -pid group kill. (b) StdioProcess - close stdin first, unchanged; graceful step = CTRL_BREAK_EVENT to that child only; after 3 seconds, TerminateProcess on that PID alone, with NO job object, so grandchildren survive exactly as they do on macOS. The 1-second and 3-second deadlines, the stdin-close-first ordering, and the tree-vs-single-process scope are all preserved, so the two ladders stay distinguishable as triage_summary.json:92 requires. Record in COMPATIBILITY that the graceful step is CTRL_BREAK rather than SIGTERM and that a CLI ignoring CTRL_BREAK reaches the kill step where a macOS one would have exited.

## ED-055

[STORE] [STORE] Q169: the orphan sweep's path regex matches the JSON-escaped POSIX form attachments/<uuid>.<ext>; on Windows the writer's separator and the pattern must change together or every attachment is deleted after 24 hours. :: CONFIRMED and it is the right thing to have flagged, with one refinement. The pattern at Storage.swift:129 is `#/attachments\\?\/([0-9A-Fa-f-]{36}\.[A-Za-z0-9]+)/#` - an OPTIONAL backslash followed by a REQUIRED forward slash, so it already matches both the raw 'attachments/uuid.ext' and the JSON-escaped 'attachments\/uuid.ext' that the comment at :128 describes. What it cannot match is a Windows separator, which the encoder writes as a doubled backslash. The writer is Storage.swift:102 and :109, `path: destination.path`, and destination comes from attachmentsDirectory.appendingPathComponent(...). DECISION (mine): (1) the port derives the sweep pattern and the path writer from ONE shared constant so they cannot drift; (2) the pattern is made strictly MORE permissive than the source's - accept a JSON-escaped backslash, a JSON-escaped forward slash, or a bare forward slash before the uuid - because the failure is asymmetric: over-matching only keeps an orphan for one more cycle, while under-matching deletes the user's photos 24 hours after they are written; (3) keep the source's mechanism otherwise intact, including the second pass that decodes StoredContinuation when the text contains '"continuation"' (Storage.swift:133-139), the 24-hour cutoff, and the name whole-match guard at :142 that stops anything not named the way importAttachment names it from being deleted; (4) a regression test is MANDATORY at implementation, not a code-review note - write an attachment, save the thread, run the sweep with the clock advanced past the cutoff, assert the file survives; and assert the inverse, that a genuinely unreferenced file is collected. This is the single highest-consequence line in the area and it must not ship on inspection alone.

## ED-056

[STORE] [STORE] Q170: Attachment.path is persisted as an ABSOLUTE path string; a store carried from macOS holds POSIX paths that will not resolve on Windows and the source has no rewrite logic. :: CONFIRMED: Storage.swift:102 and :109 both construct `Attachment(id:name:path: destination.path, mimeType:)`, an absolute path string, and there is no rewrite anywhere in the tree - correctly, since macOS never needed one. The agent was right not to invent a macOS-to-Windows migration, and I am not adding one: no product path carries a macOS store onto a Windows machine. But the agent missed the Windows-native version of the same failure, which IS live: %LOCALAPPDATA% moves under a username change, a roaming or redirected profile, a drive-letter change or a restore to a different machine, and every historical attachment then renders as missing. DECISION (mine): (1) persist the absolute path exactly as source does, so the field shape and every observable behaviour match upstream; (2) at READ time only, when the stored absolute path does not resolve, re-resolve by taking the file's last path component and joining it to the current attachmentsDirectory. This is additive and unreachable in the normal case (the stored path resolves), so parity is exact everywhere the source is observable, while the Windows-only failure mode is closed. One reassurance worth recording: a stale absolute path does NOT cause deletion - the sweep's pattern anchors on the 'attachments' + separator + uuid tail, not on the drive prefix, so the files survive the sweep and only their display breaks. Record the macOS-store migration gap in LIMITATIONS as out of scope.

## ED-057

[STORE] [STORE] Q171: Storage.root's Application Support analogue - %APPDATA% (Roaming) as specified, or %LOCALAPPDATA% which the Marrow build already uses. :: DECIDED: %LOCALAPPDATA%\<display name>. Two independent reasons, and they agree. (1) Compatibility, which is decisive on its own: the port already ships there. The owner runs 0.2.1 with data in %LOCALAPPDATA%, and the first start of a build from this branch takes over %LOCALAPPDATA%\Agent Workbench and becomes %LOCALAPPDATA%\Marrow. Moving the root to %APPDATA% now would orphan every existing user's library, threads and attachments behind an app that no longer looks there - the exact harm PR-STORE-013 escalates, arrived at deliberately. (2) Semantics: ~/Library/Application Support is explicitly excluded from macOS's roaming and cloud sync, so its true Windows counterpart for a store of this shape - library.json, per-thread JSON, attachment blobs, wallpaper - is the local, non-roaming folder. %APPDATA% would push that volume through domain profile sync. The pinned source cannot decide this (Storage.swift:20-23 just asks Foundation for .applicationSupportDirectory), so it is mine, and it is recorded in the ADR. One thing the question missed and the ADR must also record: Storage has a SECOND root. Storage.swift:43-48 (stateDirectory) puts worktrees (:38) and patches (:41) under LoginEnvironment.homeDirectory + AppInfo.stateDirectoryName, i.e. the '.droppy-code' dotfolder in the user's HOME (Text.swift:6), not in Application Support. That one maps to %USERPROFILE%\<dot name> and must not be folded into %LOCALAPPDATA%, or git worktree paths change shape.

[PROVCLI][TERM] OD-0008 A8 corrects the read-only command classifier where it wrongly lets a command that writes files or repository state run without approval or checkpoint. Everything else in the table is reproduced verbatim.

## ED-063

[WIN] Window chrome, from probe P7 (porting/probes/p7/RESULT.md, run 4). Declaring the app-drawn caption controls through Win32Properties.SetNonClientHitTestResult is not enough on Avalonia 12.1.2: drag and double-click work, but the minimise, maximise and close controls do nothing and right-click opens no system menu, on every WindowDecorations value. DECISION: the main window uses WindowDecorations.Full with ExtendClientAreaToDecorationsHint and a 44 px title bar (source geometry), declares its leading-edge controls through SetNonClientHitTestResult, and installs a WndProc hook that performs minimise, maximise, restore and close (swallow WM_NCLBUTTONDOWN on the control, post the SC_* command on WM_NCLBUTTONUP), shows TrackPopupMenu(GetSystemMenu) on WM_CONTEXTMENU and SC_KEYMENU, and sets the system menu's item states first. Measured with this hook: every action works, DWM minimise, maximise and restore animations run, and the Snap Layouts flyout appears. BorderOnly and None are ruled out (they lose the DWM animations and the system menu; None also loses Snap Layouts). Non-activating panels (MCPKeyPanel.swift:41, MCPSetupPanel.swift:66 use nonactivatingPanel): WS_EX_NOACTIVATE with MA_NOACTIVATE is not enough because Avalonia calls SetFocus on the panel; use a thread-local WH_CBT hook that refuses activation for the panel HWND, so the host keeps activation and Avalonia routes keyboard input to the panel's focused field. Rendering (probe P2): the glass needs the GPU; with a null GrContext at startup the app degrades the glass as a named deviation rather than running the scene in software at about 10 fps.

## ED-065

[CONVENTIONS] ADOPTED 2026-09-23 by the orchestrator. ED-065 The main actor. `MainActor` over `IMainExecutor` in Core, bound once by Marrow.App to Full text, rationale and tests: porting/IMPLEMENTING.md section 7 (binding under ED-064).

### ED-065 owner-approved amendment (OD-0034, 2026-09-30)

The following approved draft is reproduced in full. Its Evidence and Tests sections are attributed historical claims from the draft, not new execution or acceptance by this documentation batch. The old ED-065 entry above is retained for provenance; the queue policy below supersedes its per-job Default interpretation.

ED-065 The main actor (amended by the fix/mainexec ruling, rounds 1-2).

**Decision.**
- `MainActor` over `IMainExecutor` in Core, bound once by Marrow.App to `AvaloniaMainExecutor`. An unbound main actor traps. Statics that tests replace are `Ambient<T>` seams overridden per async flow.
- AvaloniaMainExecutor keeps one FIFO queue per Avalonia Dispatcher and drains it in passes, like the GCD main queue:
  - A pass takes the jobs queued when it began off the queue (its snapshot) and runs only those. Jobs enqueued during a pass wait for a later pass.
  - The first pass of an idle queue is posted with `Dispatcher.Post` at `DispatcherPriority.Default`. Every later pass is posted at `DispatcherPriority.Input`, so pending input is handled in between.
  - `Enqueue` never runs work inline, even on the UI thread.
- It is re-entrant:
  - While a pass runs, an enqueue also posts a pass at Input.
  - Only a nested message loop inside a job can start that pass early (OpenPanel.RunModal's Win32 modal loop, a DispatcherFrame, a nested RunJobs). It then drains the jobs queued after the outer snapshot in FIFO order, and the outer pass finishes its own snapshot when the loop returns.
  - Without a nested loop, that pass is superseded (by a pass id) when the outer pass ends, and the later pass is posted then.
- A job that throws leaves the rest of its snapshot queued ahead of newer jobs. The exception surfaces through `Dispatcher.Post` as before.
- Each job runs in its enqueuer's captured ExecutionContext. Passes are posted with flow suppressed.
- While a job runs, `SynchronizationContext.Current` is a context whose Post enqueues on the same dispatcher's queue. So an await continuation of a main-actor task is a main-queue job. That context never reads the static `Dispatcher.UIThread`.

**Why.**
- ADR-0002 constraint 11 names the dispatcher as the carrier of `@MainActor`, and 27 Core/Services main-actor sites cannot reference Avalonia.
- The old executor posted every job at Default. Avalonia 12.1.2 `Dispatcher.ExecuteJobsCore` runs jobs above Input back to back without returning to the Win32 message loop. A self-re-enqueuing main-actor cycle therefore froze input: in the archived-lead probe, the Unarchive click waited more than 20 s.
- The nested-loop rule keeps main-actor work (stream events, AsyncAfter, the HangWatchdog ping) running while a modal loop is open inside a job, as it did before the drain change.
- Per-dispatcher queues and the dispatcher-bound continuation context match AvaloniaSynchronizationContext. They also keep a pool thread from creating the UI dispatcher between headless tests.

**Evidence.**
- RUNTIME EVIDENCE (open-source libdispatch, cited by the ruling, not re-read here): `_dispatch_main_queue_drain` with `os_mpsc_capture_snapshot` (the snapshot is taken off the queue); the run loop handles events between drains.
- RUNTIME EVIDENCE (open-source CoreFoundation/AppKit behaviour, not observed on this machine): the main queue is serviced in the run loop's common modes, which include the modal-panel mode.
- SOURCE FACT: the Swift runs `panel.runModal()` from the button action (ComposerView.swift:526-533, PromptEditor.swift:117-124).
- ENGINEERING FACT, from decompiled Avalonia 12.1.2:
  - `DispatcherPriority`: Input = Default - 1.
  - `ExecuteJobsCore`: `if (Priority > Input) { ExecuteJob; continue; }`. At or below Input it checks `HasPendingInput`.
  - `Win32DispatcherImpl`: `CanQueryPendingInput` is true, and `HasPendingInput` uses `MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx(QS_INPUT|QS_POSTMESSAGE|QS_EVENT)`.
  - `AvaloniaSynchronizationContext.Post` posts to its own dispatcher.
  - `Dispatcher.UIThread` falls back to `CurrentDispatcher` when `s_uiThread` is null, which is the state `ResetGlobalState` leaves between headless tests.
- Archived-lead probe on the real executor (round 1): the Input click ran within 0-12 ms, against more than 22,950 ms before.
- `SettingsViewTests` alone: 5 of 5 green after round 2. The verifier had 2 of 5 fail at round 1.

**Tests.** These run on the real AvaloniaMainExecutor in Avalonia headless.
- `HeadlessTests.The_main_actor_bound_to_Avalonia_runs_posts_and_spawns_FIFO_on_the_UI_thread_never_inline`
- `MainExecutorDrainTests` (11):
  - `Work_runs_FIFO_and_never_inline_from_the_UI_thread_a_pool_thread_or_inside_a_pass`
  - `A_chain_of_main_actor_jobs_that_re_enqueues_itself_does_not_starve_an_Input_priority_job`
  - `A_main_actor_task_that_awaits_forever_does_not_starve_an_Input_priority_job`
  - `A_job_enqueued_during_a_pass_runs_after_an_Input_job_posted_before_that_pass_ended`
  - `The_first_pass_of_an_idle_queue_runs_at_Default_ahead_of_an_Input_job`
  - `Each_job_runs_in_the_async_flow_of_its_own_enqueuer_even_when_one_pass_runs_both`
  - `A_job_that_throws_leaves_the_jobs_behind_it_queued_and_they_still_run`
  - `A_job_that_runs_a_nested_loop_does_not_freeze_the_main_actor_and_its_pass_finishes_its_snapshot_afterwards`
  - `A_main_actor_task_awaiting_inside_a_nested_loop_resumes_inside_it`
  - `A_main_actor_post_from_a_pool_thread_runs_inside_a_nested_RunJobs_opened_by_a_main_actor_job`
  - `An_await_continuation_goes_back_to_the_dispatcher_of_its_job_without_reading_the_static_UIThread`
- `MainActorTests` (13).
- Mutations M1-M6 (round 1) and N1-N6 (round 2) are each caught.

## ED-087

[CHAT] OD-0012 G4 as the owner accepted it in porting/decision_batch_20260922b.md: the Mac-only "Open in" items change (Finder becomes "File Explorer"; Terminal means Windows Terminal; Xcode and iTerm are left out because they do not exist on Windows). The other editors upstream's catalogue lists stay. The owner_decisions.md summary "offers File Explorer and Terminal only" overstated the sheet and is corrected there. DECISION for the Windows detection the source does with Launch Services bundle ids (Components.swift:103-106, :139-147): an editor is present when its executable is registered under HKCU or HKLM Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths\<exe>, or is found on PATH (PATHEXT, ED-031 rules): Visual Studio Code "Code.exe" / "code", Cursor "Cursor.exe" / "cursor", Zed "Zed.exe" / "zed", Windows Terminal "wt.exe". Ghostty has no Windows build and is therefore never present. File Explorer is always present. Launch passes the folder as the single argument (explorer.exe for File Explorer; wt.exe -d <folder> for Terminal). The icon is the executable's own icon.

## ED-088

[ALL] Scope of OD-0012 F1 ("every remaining Droppy Code / droppy-code the app shows or sends out becomes Marrow / marrow"). DECISION: it covers everything a user can see or that the app writes into places the user owns: UI text, file and folder names in the user's home or projects (the state folder ".droppy-code" becomes ".marrow", shown in Settings; the home state directory becomes %USERPROFILE%\.marrow, with %USERPROFILE%\.marrow-dev for a development build), git data written into the user's repositories (the checkpoint ref namespace refs/droppy-code/checkpoints/ becomes refs/marrow/checkpoints/, the checkpoint author and messages per F1), and identities sent over the network or to other programs. It does not cover names that live only inside the app and its own helper processes and are never shown or stored in user space: the bridge variable DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG and the login-shell marker __DROPPY_CODE_ENVIRONMENT__ keep upstream's names (parity, invisible). The two F1 exceptions stand: droppy-code.json and DROPPY_CODE_PROJECT_ROOT. The OAuth callback page's Droppy logo is replaced by the port's own icon once the owner approves it (the owner chose a new icon design, 2026-09-23).

## ED-091

[THEME][UI] SwiftUI `Font` has no port-side model, so a unit that uses `.font(...)` (433 `.font(.system` sites, 71 `.font(.chat` sites, 29 `.monospacedDigit()`, 22 `design: .monospaced`, 8 `NSFont.systemFont`, 2 `NSFont.monospacedSystemFont`, 1 `NSFont.boldSystemFont` at B2) cannot be tested without inventing one; the wave A test agent for `UI/Common/ChatFont.swift` stopped on exactly that. DECISION: a foundation unit F.SwiftFont (`src/Marrow.UI/Port/SwiftFont.cs`) provides one immutable `SwiftFont` value that every UI unit uses: a text style (largeTitle, title, title2, title3, headline, subheadline, body, callout, footnote, caption, caption2) or a fixed point size, with an optional weight (ultraLight, thin, light, regular, medium, semibold, bold, heavy, black), a design (default or monospaced; rounded and serif do not occur at B2 and are not provided), and the monospacedDigit, italic and bold modifiers, each returning a new value. It resolves to Avalonia as: size from the ED-059 table (B1:DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift:44-57) or the fixed size, one point to one DIP (ED-071); weight to the OpenType weight classes 100 to 900 in that order; face Inter for the default design (OD-0009) and Cascadia Mono for monospaced (OD-0009); monospacedDigit as the tnum feature. A text style with no weight resolves regular, except headline, which macOS sets bold; that default is platform knowledge, not a B2 fact, and its visual parity is UNVERIFIED under OD-0001 like the rest of ED-059. Zoom is never applied here, because upstream scales the window and not the type (ChatFont.swift:4-5, AppZoom.swift).

## ED-092

[THEME][UI] The SwiftUI values a view passes around have no port type; the wave A skeleton for the Chrome cycle (c35) stopped on Color, Spring, AnyTransition and styled Text. R-VIEW-4 and R-VIEW-11 said the Chrome units define the curves and colours; they still define the VALUES, but the TYPES are shared by every UI unit and belong in `UI/Port`. DECISION, three foundation units: (1) F.SwiftColor, `SwiftColor`: an immutable value that is a fixed sRGB colour with alpha (`Color(red:green:blue:)`, `Color(white:)`, `Color(white:alpha:)`, `Color(hex:)` through the Core extension), an appearance pair resolved per the control's `ActualThemeVariant` (`NSColor(name:dynamicProvider:)`, ED-051 and ED-062 token pairs), or a named system colour (`.clear`, `.white`, `.black`, `.primary`, `.secondary`, `.accentColor`, `.yellow`, `NSColor.labelColor`, `.placeholderTextColor`, `.controlAccentColor`); `.opacity(x)` multiplies alpha and returns a new value; resolution gives an Avalonia `Color` for a theme and a brush that follows theme changes; the accent is the Windows personalization accent (ED-051); `.primary` and `.secondary` as foreground styles are the ED-051/ED-062 tokens; system colours with no B2 value use the macOS documented values, UNVERIFIED under OD-0001. (2) F.SwiftAnimation: concrete `Animation` records under the existing abstract `Animation` (ViewSupport.cs): spring(response:dampingFraction:blendDuration:), spring(duration:bounce:), `Spring(response:dampingRatio:)` with `settlingDuration` from ED-011, smooth (bounce 0), snappy (bounce 0.15), easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut (cubic Beziers 0.42,0,1,1 / 0,0,0.58,1 / 0.42,0,0.58,1), linear, `.delay`, with the documented SwiftUI defaults (duration 0.35 for the timing curves, 0.5 for smooth, snappy and spring(duration:)); a spring is a damped oscillator with omega0 = 2*pi/response and zeta = dampingFraction, or 1 - bounce for bounce >= 0 and 1/(1+bounce) below, sampled as an Avalonia easing; and `SwiftTransition`: identity, opacity, scale(scale:anchor:), offset(x:y:), move(edge:), blurReplace, modifier(active:identity:), asymmetric(insertion:removal:), combined(with:) and animation(_:), applied on insert from active to identity and on removal from identity to active before the control leaves, with `Transaction.Current`. The documented defaults and blurReplace's exact blur and scale are platform knowledge, not B2 facts, UNVERIFIED under OD-0001. (3) F.StyledText, `StyledText`: SwiftUI `Text` as a value (29 functions return `Text` at B2) made of runs, each with its string and optional SwiftFont, SwiftColor, weight, italic, underline, strikethrough, monospaced digits and baseline offset; `+` concatenates runs; it renders into a TextBlock's inlines. It depends on F.SwiftFont (ED-091) and F.SwiftColor. `AttributedString` (67 sites, mostly Markdown) is not part of this unit; it stays with the units that use it.

## ED-093

[SEC][MCP][PROVAPI] The secret store (ADR-0002 deviation 8, R-SEC-1) had no mapping from a Keychain item to a Credential Manager credential; the F.SecretStore test agent stopped on the target name, user name, persistence, case and size. SOURCE FACTS: both helpers use kSecClassGenericPassword with service `AppInfo.name` and one account per item (APIKeychain.swift:26-30, MCPKeychain.swift:14-16); Keychain account matching is exact, so accounts that differ only in case are different items, and MCP accounts contain user-written field keys (MCPStore.swift:107, :217); the Keychain has no small size limit and `field: "oauth"` stores whole OAuth token JSON (MCPOAuth.swift:712). Credential Manager compares target names without case and refuses a blob over 2560 bytes (CRED_MAX_CREDENTIAL_BLOB_SIZE, probed: 2560 accepted, 2561 refused with 1783). DECISION: one generic credential per item, CRED_TYPE_GENERIC, CRED_PERSIST_LOCAL_MACHINE (the login Keychain does not roam; ENTERPRISE would), UserName the account verbatim, TargetName `<service>:<account>:<h>` where h is the first 16 lowercase hex digits of SHA-256 of the account's UTF-8 bytes, so accounts that differ only in case get different targets and the account stays readable in Credential Manager. A value longer than 2560 bytes is split into 2560-byte chunks: continuation credentials `<target>#2`, `#3` and so on are written first and the primary credential last, carrying the chunk count in a credential attribute, so a reader never sees a half-written value; a read with a missing chunk is item-not-found; a shorter write removes the chunks it no longer needs; delete removes the primary first. Add, update, copy-matching and delete keep the SecItem status contract (duplicate on add of an existing item, not-found on update or delete of a missing one) because APIKeychain deletes then adds and MCPKeychain updates then adds. The Win32 calls sit behind a backend seam; unit tests use an in-memory backend that enforces case-insensitive targets and the 2560-byte limit, so they prove the encoding. One live test against the real Credential Manager, under a throwaway service `Marrow port tests <GUID>` that it deletes in `finally`, runs only when MARROW_PORT_CREDMAN_LIVE=1 (R-TEST-9: nothing touches the user's profile by default).

[FMT] IMPLEMENTING.md 7.1 question 5: `Calendar.current`. Swift's `Calendar.current` follows the user's calendar preference on macOS. DECISION: the port's `Calendar.current` is the Windows user's calendar (`CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.Calendar`) with the local time zone, which is the same kind of source, so a user with a non-Gregorian calendar gets that calendar on both platforms; tests pin a Gregorian culture per async flow. ## ED-095

[UI] Conventions the c35 skeleton had to choose, confirmed for every UI unit: `NSImage` is `Avalonia.Media.IImage`; `NSPopover` is an Avalonia `Popup` and `NSSize` is `Avalonia.Size`; a SwiftUI `View` is a `Decorator` whose constructor builds `body` (R-VIEW-1); a `ViewModifier` is a sealed record with `Control Body(Control content)`; a `Layout` is a `Panel`; an `NSView` is a `Control`; an `@Entry` environment value is an inherited attached property on the static class named after its Swift file (R-NAME-4, R-VIEW-6); a Swift parameter without a default that follows one with a default moves before it, and every call site then names its arguments. Name clashes: the Swift type `Chrome` (UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift) keeps its name in namespace `Marrow.UI.Chrome`; a file in another `Marrow.UI.*` namespace writes `using Chrome = Marrow.UI.Chrome.Chrome;` after its file-scoped namespace line (a `using` there is searched before the enclosing namespace's members, so `Chrome.X` finds the type, not the namespace); App-layer files use `using Marrow.UI.Chrome;`. The port seam `Marrow.UI.Port.Popovers` is renamed `Presentation` so `Marrow.UI.Chrome.Popovers` (Popovers.swift, R-NAME-4) keeps the Swift name.

## ED-097

[THEME][CHAT][GIT][COMPOSER][LAUNCH] How the loading mark of OD-0016 works. DECISION: (1) one port-only control, `LoadingMark` in `src/Marrow.UI/Port/LoadingMark.cs` (foundation unit F.LoadingMark), draws the OD-0015 icon from the geometry of `src/Marrow.App/Assets/icon.svg` (tile, glow, keyline, three arcs with their gradients, core), and above 24 px only; there is no small variant because it is never shown that small. (2) Motion "Orbit": the three arcs turn round the core, one full turn every 2.4 s at constant speed, and the core scales 1 to 0.86 and back every 1.2 s with ease-in-out; the tile does not move. Both run from the frame clock (ED-083, F.FrameClock), never a timer. If the owner picks "Ratchet" or "Bloom" (OD-0016), only these keyframes change. (3) Reduce motion (R-VIEW-6, ED-084): the mark is drawn still. (4) Sites and sizes: the thread history load (PR-CHAT-025), 64 px, centred in the timeline; the diff pane (UI-GIT-012), 64 px above the kept "Reading the diff..." label; the large attachment preview (UI-COMPOSER-077), 48 px, centred in its slot; the launch splash (PR-LAUNCH-028), 96 px, centred in a borderless 240 by 240 window with no taskbar button, over the same material as the main window. (5) No flash: upstream keeps the timeline empty so a fast load shows nothing, so the mark appears only when a wait has lasted 400 ms, and then fades in over 0.2 s; a wait that ends first shows exactly what upstream shows. The launch splash follows the same rule from process start, and closes the moment the main window is shown, so the launch prologue keeps its order (PR-LAUNCH-001). (6) The mark is a picture of work in progress, not a control: no hit testing, no focus, and an accessible name "Loading" on the splash and the timeline.

## ED-098

[UI][THEME] The F.SwiftAnimation test agent stopped on two gaps. (1) Time source: every animation, transition, spring and `TimelineView` in the port reads time from the frame clock seam of F.FrameClock (ED-083, R-VIEW-10), never from Avalonia's internal animation clock, so a headless test drives it by hand with the manual frame source; F.SwiftAnimation depends on F.FrameClock. (2) Animatable modifiers: a Swift `ViewModifier` with `animatableData` (SoftAppearModifier and SettleGlideModifier in Chrome.swift:937-999, ChipRowCollapse in ComposerView.swift:940-959, and any other the source animates) is a sealed record implementing `IAnimatableModifier` (namespace Marrow.UI.Port, built by F.SwiftAnimation): `ImmutableArray<double> AnimatableData` (a `CGFloat` is one value; an `AnimatablePair` is its two halves flattened in declaration order), `IAnimatableModifier WithAnimatableData(ImmutableArray<double> data)` returning a copy, `Control Body(Control content)` building the wrapper once, and `void Update(Control body)` applying the record's values to that wrapper. SwiftUI re-evaluates `body` each frame; the port calls `Update` each frame with the interpolated record. `SwiftTransition.Modifier(active, identity)` interpolates `AnimatableData` component-wise with the animation's progress (a spring may overshoot), from active to identity on insertion and from identity to active on removal, after which the control leaves. A modifier that does not implement `IAnimatableModifier` takes its end state at the start of the transaction, as SwiftUI does for `EmptyAnimatableData`. ED-095's "sealed record with Control Body(Control content)" stays the form for modifiers that never animate.

## ED-099

[SETTINGS][WIN] The Core.Models.Shortcuts test agent stopped because the port's chord format was never fixed and three sources disagreed (ED-050 (c): virtual keys in a new versioned key; OD-PENDING-06, resolved: scan codes; PR-SETTINGS-104: keep "keyboardShortcuts"). DECISION, which supersedes ED-050 (b) and (c) and follows OD-0008 B7, B8 and B9: (1) `KeyChord.KeyCode` is the Windows Set-1 scan code of the physical key, extended keys as 0xE000 | code, because only a scan code names a position independent of the layout, as the macOS key code does (Shortcuts.swift:4, :37). (2) The US-position table of Shortcuts.swift:52-69 maps one for one: A 0x1E, S 0x1F, D 0x20, F 0x21, H 0x23, G 0x22, Z 0x2C, X 0x2D, C 0x2E, V 0x2F, B 0x30, Q 0x10, W 0x11, E 0x12, R 0x13, Y 0x15, T 0x14, 1 0x02, 2 0x03, 3 0x04, 4 0x05, 6 0x07, 5 0x06, = 0x0D, 9 0x0A, 7 0x08, - 0x0C, 8 0x09, 0 0x0B, ] 0x1B, O 0x18, U 0x16, [ 0x1A, I 0x17, P 0x19, L 0x26, J 0x24, ' 0x28, K 0x25, ; 0x27, \ 0x2B, "," 0x33, / 0x35, N 0x31, M 0x32, . 0x34, ` 0x29; Return 0x1C, Tab 0x0F, Space 0x39, Delete (macOS 51, backspace) 0x0E, Esc 0x01, Del (macOS 117, forward delete) 0xE053, left 0xE04B, right 0xE04D, down 0xE050, up 0xE048, Home 0xE047, End 0xE04F, PgUp 0xE049, PgDn 0xE051, F1-F10 0x3B-0x44, F11 0x57, F12 0x58. Labels, `typesText` and the menu key equivalents keep the macOS lists, keyed by these codes. The modifier keys of :40 are LShift 0x2A, RShift 0x36, LCtrl 0x1D, RCtrl 0xE01D, LAlt 0x38, RAlt 0xE038, LWin 0xE05B, RWin 0xE05C and CapsLock 0x3A (macOS fn has no Windows scan code). An unknown key is labelled "Key <scan code in decimal>". (3) Modifiers: `ChordModifiers` [Flags] with Alt = 1, Control = 2, Shift = 4 (Avalonia's KeyModifiers values, so the UI casts directly); Command and Control both become Control (ED-050 (a); no default combines them), Option becomes Alt, and Win is masked out like fn, so the allowed set is Control | Alt | Shift and the shipped defaults are ED-050 (a)'s list. (4) Text: modifiers print as "Ctrl+", "Alt+", "Shift+" in that order before the label (OD-0008 B7), the typing refusal is "Add Ctrl or Alt so typing still works." (B7), and the reserved refusal is "Windows or Marrow already uses this chord." over upstream's 18 chords with Command read as Control (B8, which keeps the same list, so ED-050 (b)'s Ctrl+Y variant is withdrawn). (5) Storage: the defaults key stays "keyboardShortcuts" (Swift and PR-SETTINGS-104) with the Swift JSON shape, `keyCode` and `modifiers`, holding the values above; no macOS profile can reach Windows, so nothing needs a new key. (6) SwiftUI's `KeyboardShortcut`, `KeyEquivalent` and `EventModifiers` are the port values `KeyboardShortcut(KeyEquivalent Key, ChordModifiers Modifiers)` and `KeyEquivalent(string Name)` in `src/Marrow.Core/Port/Keyboard.cs`, where Name is the SwiftUI spelling: a lowercase character, or return, tab, space, delete, escape, deleteForward, leftArrow, rightArrow, downArrow, upArrow, home, end, pageUp, pageDown, F1-F12; the UI maps them to Avalonia key gestures.

## ED-100

[GIT] The Services.Git.RevertPreview test agent stopped on `CocoaError(.fileReadCorruptFile)` (RevertPreview.swift:33, :36), whose `localizedDescription` the message editor shows (PR-GIT-099); WorkingTreeWatch.swift:333 throws `CocoaError(.fileReadUnknown)`. DECISION: `CocoaError` in `src/Marrow.Core/Port/CocoaError.cs`, an `ISwiftErrorIdentity` and `ILocalizedError` with Domain "NSCocoaErrorDomain" and the Foundation codes the source uses, FileReadUnknown = 256 and FileReadCorruptFile = 259. Its `ErrorDescription` is Foundation's English text for an error with no file name: 256 "The file couldn’t be opened." and 259 "The file couldn’t be opened because it isn’t in the correct format." (U+2019). That text is Apple's, not the source's, so it is UNVERIFIED as oracle item O-25 (R-ERR-2), and R-ERR-2's refusal to invent text stays for every other foreign error.

## ED-101

[WIN][CHROME] How `stretch` (OD-0017) ships. DECISION: the probe's route, without the sync or flush hooks (they do not lower the residual and DwmFlush costs 24 % of UI frames during a drag). A port-only helper `ResizeStretch` in `src/Marrow.UI/Port/ResizeStretch.cs` (foundation unit F.ResizeStretch) is applied by the window chrome to every resizable top-level window after its first frame: on the UI thread it resolves `PlatformImpl`, `_glSurface`, the surface's `_window` (WinUiCompositedWindow) and that window's `_shared` (SyncRoot, Compositor), `_visual` and `_surfaceBrush` by reflection; under `lock (SyncRoot)` it sets the content visual's size to zero with RelativeSizeAdjustment (1,1), sets the surface brush's Stretch to Fill, and parks a detached sprite visual in `_visual` so `ResizeIfNeeded` sizes that one; it reads both values back, and if any member is missing or a read-back differs it logs once and leaves the window as Avalonia made it; on close, under the lock, it puts the real visual back before Avalonia disposes the surface. A test pinned to Avalonia 12.1.2 fails if the members are not found, so an upgrade cannot drop the remedy silently. No Win32 message handling is added; the ED-063 WndProc hook is unchanged. Evidence: porting/probes/p4b/RESULT.md, "How the production chrome should implement it". Reflection on Avalonia internals is accepted here because the alternative is carrying a patched Avalonia.Win32, which the stack decision (ADR-0002) does not provide for.

## ED-102

[THEME][LAUNCH] The Comet motion and the boot splash of OD-0018, as numbers (they supersede ED-097 (2) and, for the launch site, ED-097 (4) and (5); units are the icon's 1024 box, times in seconds). The reference implementation is `porting/design/loading_mark/boot_sequence.html` (superseding the first draft `boot_splash.html`) (canvas, frame by frame, the way the port draws); where this text and the preview differ, this text rules. (1) **Turn:** the arms turn 360 degrees every 2.4 s on cubic-bezier(.45, .05, .55, .95), so each turn starts and ends at rest; the tile never turns. (2) **Trails:** two copies of the arms, rotated back 14 and 30 degrees, blurred by 10 and 20 units, at opacity .42 and .2 times a trail factor that is clamp((speed - .35) / 1.4), where speed is the turn's angular speed relative to its mean (0 at rest, about 2 mid-turn). (3) **Pulse, once per turn, at rest:** over the last .28 s of each turn the core draws in to .9 scale and its glow dims by 45 %; at the instant the turn ends the core rises to 1.14 within .06 s and relaxes back to 1 as exp(-7 s), the glow flashes (opacity + 1.1, scale + .5, same decay), and one ring leaves the core: radius 96 to 346 over 1.9 s on cubic-bezier(.2, .6, .3, 1), opacity .6 to 0, 3 DIP wide, colour #DCE6FF; the next turn starts from rest at that instant. (4) **Boot splash:** a borderless, taskbar-less 420 by 420 DIP window, centred on the primary monitor's work area, over the same material as the main window, shown at process start on every launch; the mark is 210 DIP. Gather, 0 to 1.45 s: 216 particles (60 per arm, sampled along the arc and across 80 % of the stroke, coloured by the arm's gradient at that point; 36 in the core, #ECF2FF) start on a ring of radius 820 to 1080, 1.3 to 2.2 radians behind their target angle, and fly in with radius on ease-out-cubic and angle on ease-out-quart; arm k's particles start after .06 + .09 k + up to .34 s and fly .7 to .98 s, the core's start after .5 to .72 s and fly .6 to .75 s; a particle is drawn as a soft dot of radius 9 to 20 shrinking to 55 % as it lands, then melts out over .35 of its flight time; each arm fades in with the share of its particles landed, and the core grows the same way. The tile rises in from .55 to 1.2 s, opacity 0 to 1 and scale .94 to 1 on ease-out-back (1.4). Ignition at 1.45 s: the first pulse of (3), which starts the first turn. Running: (1) to (3) until the app is ready. Hand-over: at the later of "the app is ready" and 1.8 s, the mark grows 6 % and fades over .45 s while the main window is shown, and the splash closes. (5) **Reduce motion:** the still mark fades in over .3 s, with no particles, turn, trails or pulses. (6) **In-app sites** (ED-097 (4)) use (1) to (3) with the tile, at their sizes, after the 400 ms rule. (7) All drawing is done by the F.LoadingMark control from the frame clock (ED-083); particles are drawn as radial-gradient dots, the trails with a blur effect.

Reference: `porting/design/loading_mark/boot_sequence.html`; where this text and the preview differ, this text rules. (4) **Disintegration,** 0.1 s after the final rest (td = 0): the mark fades out over 0.22 s as its particles appear in place: the 216 gather particles at their landing points plus 84 from the tile (56 on its edge, 28 inside it). ## ED-104

[THEME][UI] SwiftUI Color.yellow. B2 uses Color.yellow at three sites and never defines it: App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.swift:80 `.foregroundStyle(.yellow)`, :669 `.foregroundStyle(isOn ? Color.yellow : Chrome.secondaryText)` and :673 `Circle().fill(isOn ? Color.yellow.opacity(0.18) : ...)`. ED-092 already decides the method: 'system colours with no B2 value use the macOS documented values, UNVERIFIED under OD-0001'. This decision only records the numbers. DECISION: SwiftColor.Yellow is an appearance pair, light sRGB (255, 204, 0) and dark sRGB (255, 214, 0), both opaque. These are the 'Default (light)' and 'Default (dark)' columns of the Yellow row (SwiftUI API `Color.yellow`) in Apple's Human Interface Guidelines system colours table, which applies to iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS (developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color, read 2026-09-23). That is the current table, and it fits B2's deployment target, macOS 26.0 (project.yml:20, DroppyCode.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:207). The 'Increased contrast' columns (light 161,106,0; dark 254,223,67) are not modelled. The ED-051/ED-062 tokens do not model them either, and the port has no mapping from the macOS Increase Contrast setting. Recorded as UNVERIFIED under OD-0001, like ED-051's label literals. No oracle id: without macOS access (OD-0001) there is nothing to run.

## ED-105

[THEME][UI] NSColor.placeholderTextColor. B2's only site is App/Views/Composer/ComposerTextView.swift:204 (`.foregroundColor: NSColor.placeholderTextColor`), which draws the composer placeholder.
