## ED-247

[BUILD][INSTALLER] An installer that knows what is installed (OD-0072; amends ED-235's title and shortcut; OD-0058, OD-0062 unchanged: local only, nothing signed, uploaded, published or run on a development PC). RESEARCH (SOURCE FACT, Velopack 1.2.161: the tag's source, https://codeload.github.com/velopack/velopack/tar.gz/refs/tags/1.2.161, read 2026-10-02, tied to the binary vpk packs, ~/.dotnet/tools/.store/vpk/1.2.161/vpk/1.2.161/vendor/setup_x64.exe, which carries "Velopack Setup (1.2.161)" and the dialog strings quoted here). (1) Setup.exe's arguments (src/bins/src/setup.rs, clap, errors ignored): -s/--silent ("Hides all dialogs and answers 'yes' to all prompts"), -v/--verbose, -l/--log <FILE>, -t/--installto <DIR>, -h/--help, and the app's arguments after `--`; it changes to its own folder before it uses --installto. (2) What it does (src/bins/src/commands/install.rs:18-168): the root is --installto or %LOCALAPPDATA%\<pack id>; when the root is not empty (shared/util_common.rs:65-73: missing, no entries, or a `.dead` marker count as empty) it reads the installed version through the locator (lib-rust/src/locator.rs:113-129, 368-378: <root>\Update.exe must exist and <root>\current\sq.version, the package nuspec, is read with strict SemVer; any failure is "no version") and shows show_overwrite_repair_dialog (src/l18n/src/dialogs.rs:188-252, locales/en-US.ftl): older installed "Marrow is already installed / Version {old} is currently installed. Would you like to update to version {new}?" [Update]; same "This application is already installed on your computer. If it is not working correctly, you can try repairing it by reinstalling." [Repair]; newer "A newer version of Marrow is already installed / ... Downgrading is not recommended and may cause problems. Continue anyway?" [Downgrade]; each also [Open install folder] [Cancel]; --silent answers yes without asking, a 300 s timeout is Cancel. On yes it force-stops every process running from the root, renames the root to <root>.<16 random characters> for rollback, extracts a fresh Update.exe, packages\<full nupkg> and current\, creates the shortcuts, runs the app's `--veloapp-install <version>` hook (30 s; windows/util.rs:19-62: a non-zero exit or a timeout only shows "Install Partially Succeeded"), writes HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\<pack id>, starts the app with VELOPACK_FIRSTRUN (not when silent) and deletes the rollback folder; a failure restores it. (3) Hooks (src/lib-csharp/VelopackApp.cs; 1.2.161's names are On..., not With...: OnFirstRun, OnRestarted, OnAfterInstallFastCallback, OnAfterUpdateFastCallback, OnBeforeUpdateFastCallback, OnBeforeUninstallFastCallback): --veloapp-obsolete and -updated run only when Update.exe applies an update (an in-app update), never from Setup.exe; the install hook runs after the old install has already been moved aside, cannot cancel and may show no UI (https://docs.velopack.io/integrating/hooks: "there is no way to provide feedback during the hooks that you would like to cancel the install/uninstall/update", "you may not show any UI to the user"). Setup.exe has no pre-install check and its texts are compiled in (https://docs.velopack.io/packaging/installer: "not a lot of customisation available"). vpk's --msi builds a machine-wide MSI (Velopack.Vpk WindowsPackCommand.cs:101-102), not OD-0062's per-user install. (4) vpk pack refuses a version equal to or lower than one already in its releases folder ("There is a release in channel win which is equal or greater to the current version"), so packing the same version again needs artifacts/releases emptied first. CONSEQUENCE: Velopack alone gives OD-0072's upgrade and fresh install, but for the same version it offers Repair (a full reinstall) and for a newer installed version Downgrade; neither its dialog nor any hook can refuse. DECISION: (1) the installer the owner shares is a small bootstrapper, `src/Marrow.Setup` (a new project in Marrow.sln: net10.0-windows WinExe, no Marrow project reference, the app's icon, an asInvoker / common-controls 6 / per-monitor DPI manifest), with vpk's Setup.exe embedded (resource VelopackSetup.exe) and the pack's title, id and version as assembly metadata. It runs `InstallerGate.Run` (src/Marrow.Core/Support/InstallerGate.cs, plain .NET, compiled into the bootstrapper by a linked Compile item): it reads the installed version exactly as Setup.exe does (same root, same `.dead`, Update.exe and sq.version rules, strict SemVer 2.0.0 with section 11's precedence, build metadata ignored) and decides: nothing readable installed -> Install (Setup.exe; for an unreadable leftover, Setup.exe's own Repair prompt); older -> Upgrade (Setup.exe, whose Update dialog is the one confirmation; it replaces the install folder in place, and the data folder %LOCALAPPDATA%\Marrow Code, outside it, is untouched); same -> a message box "Marrow 1.7.0 is already installed and up to date." (caption "Marrow Setup", Velopack's own title-setup), exit 0, nothing run or written; newer -> a warning "A newer version of Marrow (1.8.0) is already installed." (the owner's sentence, with the installed version as Velopack recorded it), exit 1 (Setup.exe's failure code), nothing run or written. Only for Install and Upgrade is Setup.exe copied to %TEMP%\MarrowSetup-<guid>\Setup.exe, run with the same arguments, waited for and deleted, and its exit code returned. The gate reads Setup.exe's own arguments: --silent/-s (also clustered, -vs) shows no message but keeps the outcome and exit code; -t/--installto (also -tDIR, -t=DIR, --installto=DIR) is the root checked and, resolved against the installer's folder as Setup.exe would, is passed on whole as `--installto <full path>` (Setup.exe now runs from a temporary copy); -h/--help goes straight to Setup.exe; nothing after `--` is read. A bootstrapper built without a version (a plain Marrow.sln build) says the version is not SemVer and runs nothing; one built without the payload says "This installer was built without Velopack's Setup.exe.". (2) Identity: title "Marrow" (Setup's dialogs, the Apps list, the shortcut), authors "Marrow Code", `--shortcuts StartMenu`, so the shortcut is Start Menu\Programs\Marrow Code\Marrow.lnk: the owner's Electron app "Marrow" has Start Menu\Programs\Marrow.lnk on this PC (seen 2026-10-02), which `StartMenuRoot` with the title "Marrow" would overwrite (shortcuts.rs: Lnk save_as at <Start Menu>\<title>.lnk) and Velopack's uninstall would later delete; the pack id MarrowCode, %LOCALAPPDATA%\MarrowCode, the uninstall key MarrowCode and the data folder are unchanged (ED-235), so neither app can replace the other. (3) scripts/package-windows.ps1 step 3 publishes Marrow.Setup (Release, win-x64, self-contained, single file, trimmed, compressed) with -p:InstallerTitle, InstallerAppId and InstallerVersion from the very variables given to vpk pack and -p:VelopackSetupExe=<the MarrowCode-*Setup.exe vpk produced>, to artifacts/installer/Marrow-<version>-Setup.exe; the bare Setup.exe in artifacts/releases is only its payload. EVIDENCE: the script ran locally on 2026-10-02 (final run; the installer never): vpk "Shortcuts: StartMenu"; the nuspec has title Marrow, authors Marrow Code, shortcutLocations StartMenu; MarrowCode-win-Setup.exe 71,163,712 bytes; Marrow-1.7.0-Setup.exe 83,441,931 bytes; the intermediate Marrow.Setup.dll holds vpk's Setup.exe byte for byte and InstallerTitle Marrow, InstallerVersion 1.7.0; trimming reported no warning. vpk 1.2.161 also warns that VelopackApp.Run() is in Program.RunVelopackHook rather than in Main itself (ED-235's guard, unchanged here; Main calls it first). Tests (Trait Decision ED-247): InstallerGateTests (every outcome, SemVer precedence including the specification's own chain, the manifest read from Velopack's layout, the gate's hand-over and messages through a recording host, silent, install folders absolute and relative, help, `--`, a version-less build, and the script and project wiring); 19 mutants of the gate and 3 of the script each fail at least one test (one equivalent mutant, a second version check in Run, showed the check redundant and it was removed). UNVERIFIED (needs a clean test machine or VM; nothing was installed here, by rule): the bootstrapper was compiled and packed but never run; each of the four cases end to end (the message boxes, Velopack's Update dialog after the gate, the upgrade keeping %LOCALAPPDATA%\Marrow Code, the app starting after it); the Start menu folder and name as Windows 11 shows them; the Apps list entry "Marrow" beside the Electron app's; SmartScreen and antivirus reactions to an unsigned 83 MB exe that writes and runs an exe under %TEMP%; the temporary copy's deletion; a machine whose %TEMP% is not writable. Not covered: an in-app Update.exe apply would not pass through the gate (no feed is set, OD-0008 I1, and OD-0072 makes the in-app option the provider CLIs' updater); nothing was ever installed from ED-235's "Marrow Code"/StartMenuRoot packages, so no migration from them is handled.

## ED-248

[UI][COMPOSER] Fast mode is Strike (OD-0073; supersedes OD-0063's "the fast-mode bolt animation stays constant"; amends OD-0051's set of liquid tracks; DEVIATION from EffortSlider.swift:992-996 (the amber fast fill and the brand-to-amber fusion fill), :1057-1064 and :1151-1201 (the speed streaks and bolts), :1099-1132 and :1343-1346 (their traits, trait cache and random), PR-COMPOSER-134 and PR-COMPOSER-136). SOURCE (owner-approved design, not the Swift source): the locked canvas E:/Droppy/work/design/fast-mode-strike-A2-locked.dc.html (sha256 3f8ad01a...7a4408, byte-identical to the board FastA.dc.html), variant A2, the board's key 'B', drawn by strike() and strikeAt(). The spec read from that code is E:/Droppy/work/design/strike/SPEC.md. Reference frames were rendered from the file itself (E:/Droppy/work/design/strike/canvas-frames/: four tubes, 288 frames each at 1/60 s, 2x; harness/capture.js drives time by hand and has the board's own drawAll(t) paint each frame). DECISION: (1) src/Marrow.App/Views/Composer/LiquidStrike.cs ports the canvas's code function by function: hash (unchecked 32-bit multiplies, unsigned shifts), vn, fbm, strikeAt (2.4 s slots, onset +0.2 + 0.5 hash(k, S+5)), the flicker count (hash(k, S+9) > 0.45 means three), the pulses (0 ms: 1, 50 ms; 75 ms: 0.6, 40 ms; 150 ms: 0.85, 55 ms; capped at 1.1), the glow-out e^(-a/0.5) cut at 1.8 s, the leader (seven 20 ms steps to 90 % of the channel, glow 0.32, a light pool at its tip), channel() (seed S*37 + k, a vertex every 5k + 2 px, amplitude 0.34h, clamped to 0.14h..0.86h, ends pinned by sin(pi u)^0.55), the five branches toward the cap end, the 30 Hz shimmer (+-0.8k), the inner flash (a light pool at the knob, 1.6 * 1.4h by 1.4h, alpha I/2, in the wash colour), the always-on pool (0.12 + 0.04 sin 2.6t), the knob spark (half the cycles, 1.1 to 1.5 s after a strike, 1/9 s, 0.6 (1-f)^2, never while a strike is under 0.5 s old), glow() as three strokes (outer 0.14a at wide*k, inner 0.36a at 2.4k, white 0.92a at max(0.8, 1.05k)), the colour alphas rounded as the canvas's toFixed(3), and the TINT table (Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini; Antigravity takes Gemini's; every other brand Claude's, as the canvas's `TINT[brand] || TINT.claude`). Size factor k = clamp(h/40, 0.62, 1): the port's 34 px track gives 0.85. (2) Cost: a frame is resolved on the UI thread into at most 22 drawing steps (StrikeChannels.Scene; mean 5.6 over a minute at 240 Hz); each strike's channel and branches are built once (30 channels in 60 s of 240 Hz frames) and the jittered copies once per 30th of a second; Scene measured 1.5 us a frame (Debug). The render thread strokes them into one offscreen layer at device scale (0.245 ms a frame on a CPU raster surface, 2x 787 x 80, Debug; the app's GPU path uses a GPU surface as the liquid's passes do, ED-233) and LiquidTrack's glass pass screens it over the refracted liquid (a second compile of GlassMain with a `light` child: premultiplied l + o - l o, the canvas's mix-blend-mode: screen), above the bubbles, under the gloss and the rims, clipped to the liquid by the glass's coverage. The lightning is sampled at the pixel itself, not refracted (on the canvas it is a plain layer over the liquid). No timer: time is the track's frame-clock time (ED-232, ED-237); every frame is evaluated (the canvas's own 60 fps gate is not copied; only the leader's 20 ms steps and the 30 Hz shimmer are stepped, as written). Everything is a function of time, so loops are seamless and the same moment draws the same. (3) TrackEffect (EffortSlider.cs): fast mode below the top (Kind.Fast) and at it (Kind.Fusion), solo or paired, is the model's own liquid (LiquidSpec.For, OD-0063's intensity when it lands) with Strike over it; IsLiquid is now every look but Plain. The fill under a fast track is the brand's, as at the top (the amber FastFill and the brand-to-amber fusion are no longer drawn; FastFill stays defined for the colour table). A pair strikes in its lead's tint (look.Brand). The knob: the slider's 42 px knob centred 21 px in from the fill's end (KnobInset, KnobRadius), so the channel leaves the knob's centre and the sparks start inside it. The seed per track is bubbleSeed * 97 + 13 (the board's own seed * 97 + 13 form). The source streaks, bolts, Streak, Traits, TraitCache, EdgeFade and Random are removed. (4) Currents: LiquidFlow carries how far the fast current, the slow current and the caustic have run; fast mode runs them at 4.67 s, 7.33 s and 4 s (from 7, 11 and 6; the breathe and the bubbles keep their pace), and LiquidPace keeps each layer where it is when fast mode is toggled on a track that keeps its view (a pair), so the pace changes without a jump. (5) Reduce motion (EnvironmentValues.AccessibilityReduceMotion, also when it changes at run time): the fast look draws the canvas's one still, 35 ms into strike 1 (I = 0.497, the channel, its five branches, the flash at about 0.25 and the ambient pool), over the liquid at rest (time 0, no flow, no bubbles). EVIDENCE: tests (Trait Decision ED-248 and the PR-COMPOSER-134/136/138 traits): EffortSliderStrikeTests, 31 tests on the manual frame clock, every expected value from the canvas file (its constants, or its own strike() run against a recording context: tests/fixtures/strike/canvas-log.json, written by canvas-log.mjs from the locked file, for the four reference tubes and the port's 260 x 34 track): hash and noise bit for bit; strike times, flicker counts and spark times of eight strikes; the pulses and the flash's end (~266 ms double, ~398 ms triple); the leader's steps; every logged frame drawing exactly the canvas's strokes and pools (points, widths, colours, alphas); the spark's life and the young-strike rule; one channel per strike built once and the shimmer re-rolled at 30 Hz; the tints in both appearances; pixel checks of the inner flash and the channel's brightness against a model of the screen blend under the gloss at 0, 75 and 200 ms, near white at the onset and the glow-out at 0.6 s; only the ambient pool between strikes; the streaks and bolts gone; fast at every effort and for pairs drawing its own seed's scene in the lead's tint; the 1.5x currents and the jump-free pace; the reduce-motion still. EffortSliderLiquidTests, EffortSliderSweepTests and EffortSliderTests were amended for the deviation only (fast below the top is liquid; the fill under it the brand's; the PR-COMPOSER-134 streak-trait tests removed with the traits). Runs: the Composer tests (579) and the other tests touching the slider and the liquid (95) pass. Mutation: 30 mutants of LiquidStrike.cs, LiquidTrack.cs and EffortSlider.cs (hash, period, flicker time, flicker count, leader steps, shimmer rate, flash strength, glow-out width and alpha, window, channel seed, ambient pool, tint, wash gradient, screen blend, the lightning over the gloss, currents and caustic pace, the jump on a pace change, fast below the top, reduce motion, a pair's tint, the knob centre, the amber fill, branch direction and brightness, leader glow, spark life, unpinned channel ends) each fail at least one test except one equivalent mutant: dropping the "no spark while a strike is under 0.5 s old" guard changes nothing, because a spark ends by 1.5 + 1/9 s after its strike and the next strike's leader starts no sooner than 1.9 - 0.14 s after it; the guard stays, as the canvas has it. Port frames of the four reference tubes at the reference strip's times: E:/Droppy/work/design/strike/port-frames/ (and port-frames-bare/, the same frames without the lightning), the side-by-side sheet compare.png and the numbers compare-numbers.json (harness/compare.py: the light the strike adds, s = (L_lit - L_bare) / (255 - L_bare), each side against the same frame without its lightning, canvas-frames-bare/ for the reference): over 4 tubes and 15 phases plus the sparks (leader, onset, each flicker, +250 ms, glow-out at 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 1.77 s, after the window, the quiet ambient), the port is within 0.011 of the reference in the flash box (mean ratio 1.04 where the reference exceeds 0.05), within 0.0024 in the channel box mean and within 0.017 in its 99th percentile; for example dark Claude 520 x 40: onset flash 0.242 / port 0.252, channel p99 0.941 / 0.940; flicker 2 (+83 ms) 0.188 / 0.197; flicker 3 (+150 ms) 0.242 / 0.253; glow-out at 0.5 s channel p99 0.112 / 0.116; at 1 s 0.047 / 0.044. The sheet's tube background and knob are stand-ins at the board's geometry, and the liquid under the strike is the port's own (the board's CSS liquid differs by design). UNVERIFIED: the strike in the running app at 240 Hz on the owner's display (no native window or gallery run here, by rule) and its GPU path on hardware (the tests render through Avalonia's headless Skia); the owner's eye on the result; the other brands' own tints (they take Claude's, as on the canvas) await the owner. Not changed: parity_matrix.json and spec/COMPOSER.json still describe the source's streak traits (PR-COMPOSER-134) and bolts; they are recorded as deviated here.

## ED-249

[WIN][SETTINGS][MOTION] The Settings window opens with Rise (OD-0074, variant 2 of the locked canvas E:/Droppy/work/design/settings-open-rise-2-locked.dc.html; exact spec E:/Droppy/work/design/settings-rise/SPEC.md), and the plain tint before its Acrylic blur is never on screen (closes ED-236 UNRESOLVED (b)). Replaces, for the Settings window only, the source's plain order-front (WindowManager.swift:57-60; the window's own close is unchanged, :98). (1) HAND-OVER, ED-236's readiness signal (not a measured delay): an open (the window hidden, then asked for) cloaks the window (WindowCloak, DWMWA_CLOAK) before it is shown and shows it without activation; DWM composes a cloaked window, Acrylic included, and P14 found the first frame displayed after an uncloak already blurred and tinted for a cloak of 0, 300 or 1200 ms (0 tinted-over-sharp samples of 47). The window is uncloaked at the first frame-clock frame at which the hidden starting state was already set by the frame before (the same controls hidden two frames running; at most 6 frames), so the first displayed frame is the wave's start and never the settled frame of a previous open; that frame is glass-ready, G; the window is then activated (ED-236's order). A second ShowSettings while still cloaked does nothing (the reveal activates); a window already up is brought forward as before, with no wave. Hidden during the open (its close control), the open stops: everything settled, the window uncloaked, no frame request left. Where the window cannot be cloaked (no Win32 window, DWM refuses; every headless test that does not stand in for the cloak) it is shown and activated at once and nothing animates, as before. (2) THE WAVE, on the frame clock (FrameClock.Source, ED-117; no timer), at Avalonia's Animation priority over the controls' own values (a row's own opacity, such as the launch row's 0.5 under Panel only, is multiplied and comes back after), removed at G + 260 ms (ED-117 (2)'s 1 ms): the window's app-drawn glass (WindowBackdrop: glass base, tint, hairline; the detail sheet's wash and tint) and the first card's surface fade 0 to 1 over 80 ms; each item rises from 10 DIP below its place at opacity 0 over 140 ms from G + 12 ms x its index, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) driving both (opacity = 1 - y / 10). Sidebar column: the search field 0, each page row 1 to 10. Page column: 1 the chrome row when the page has controls in it (Providers, MCP, Models, Archive, About), then the page's blocks top to bottom: a section heading, each row of the first card with the divider below it, every later card whole; on Appearance (the canvas's page) that is the heading "Appearance" 1, Theme to Open the sidebar at launch 2 to 6, the picture card 7, exactly the canvas. ENGINEERING DECISION for pages the canvas does not show: blocks past index 10 start with index 10, so no page's wave ends after G + 260 ms (General has more than ten). The caption buttons are outside the wave (whole at G, as on the canvas). Nothing is made hit-test invisible: the window takes input from the moment it is displayed. (3) REDUCE MOTION (ED-084, read at the frame, since SystemReduceMotion sets the window's value when it opens, inside a first open's show): the same cloaked show and reveal, with the window complete at G and nothing animated. NOT BUILT, owner's call (named, not hidden): (a) the canvas fades the blur with the tint (its glass layer 0.698 at G + 16.7 ms); DWM's Acrylic cannot be faded (Window.Opacity, a layered alpha and an off-screen position do not hide it, P14), so in the port the blur is whole at G and only the app-drawn glass follows the 80 ms curve. (b) The canvas's close (160 ms ease-in fade to 0 and scale to 0.985, card 1 squared) is not built: the Acrylic would stay whole under the fading content; the window hides as before. (c) The canvas quirks SPEC.md section 8 lists are inherited as built: caption glyphs whole at G (over the Acrylic here, not the bare desk), card 1's outline fading in under its rising rows, stagger computed from the continuous clock (not frame-aligned); (3) does not arise since the close is not built. EVIDENCE: SettingsRiseTests (Trait Decision ED-249; expectations transcribed from SPEC.md, the curve solved independently in the test and checked against the spec's 60 Hz tables): the cloak order (cloak, shown, uncloak, activated; still cloaked after frame 1; at the uncloak the glass, card 1 and all 18 items are at their hidden start), the glass and card 1 samples 0.698 / 0.912 / 0.976 / 0.997 / 1.0, every item's opacity and offset at every 1/60 s to G + 250 ms, the order of both columns between successive starts, About still rising at G + 250 ms and everything settled with no frame request at G + 260 ms, the caption buttons whole from G, reduce motion on a first and a later open, three opens alike, an open window brought forward without a wave, no cloak, input during the wave, a row's own opacity, hiding during the open, a page with more than ten blocks; 22 mutants each killed by 1 to 14 tests (mutation list in the commit report). Port frames (headless, the window alone) at the canvas's 17 times from G, dark and light: E:/Droppy/work/design/settings-rise/port-frames, side by side with the canvas in E:/Droppy/work/design/settings-rise/compare.png (tools/compare.py; the Acrylic simulated as the desk blurred 56 px at 175 % saturation from G); over 340 element-frames per appearance the port's opacities equal samples.json's to its 4 places and its offsets to 0.0005 px. UNVERIFIED (native, not run: another workflow holds the screen): the real reveal on DWM (that the first displayed frame after the uncloak is the wave's start with the blur), the frame cadence of the wave on the owner's 240 Hz display (ED-232, ED-237), the Settings window's taskbar button while cloaked for two frames, and that the activation after the reveal takes the foreground as the plain show did.

## ED-251

[UI][COMPOSER][MOTION] The composer lights (OD-0083, OD-0085, OD-0089): an owner-ruled addition beyond the pinned source; the specification is the approved playground (E:/Droppy/work/design/variants/project/ComposerLights.dc.html, generated by work/design/composer-lights/playground/src/gen.py from beam.js and logic.js; border-beam 1.4.1's tables work/design/composer-lights/border-beam-tables.json). DECISION: (1) Settings. `ComposerLightSettings` (Marrow.Core.Models.ComposerLights): style Border beam (the default, OD-0089) | Uiverse light | Off; every Border beam option of the playground with BEAM_DEFAULTS (theme Auto, Fitted on, Duration Auto: 3.69 s a turn on 820 x 52) and every Uiverse option with AURA_DEFAULTS; the presets (Calm for the composer, Library defaults, Calm defaults, Original values) and the Family/Type rule; each value clamped and stepped as the playground's slider() sets it. The playground's "Extra CSS" row is not carried (the port draws no CSS). Persisted as one JSON object with the playground's keys under the settings key "composerLight" (AppSettings.ComposerLight), read leniently (unreadable: the default). (2) Mathematics and time. beam.js and logic.js ported number for number (fitted geometry bbFitK/bbFitBlob, the outline walk bbPerim, the window profiles, bbEase/bez/bbSwing/bbKf, Line's keyframes and periods, the pulse oscillators, bbR, bbFitDur, beamEff), the frame clock advance() (every phase integrated on the eased step; k held at 0 under reduce motion), the registered properties' CSS transitions (.6 s on cubic-bezier(.25, .1, .25, 1), the aura's intensity .9 s, reversal shortening per CSS Transitions 1), the light groups' fade (.6 s in, .5 s out), Active (.6 s on, .5 s off) and beamSlots()'s three cross-fading slots; tests compare with the playground's own functions run under node. The composer's real size replaces the playground's 820 x 52 (so the Auto duration keeps the approved speed in px a second, and the fitted geometry follows a pill that grows); the Uiverse inside rim's fixed scale(8.2, .52) is generalised to 4w/400, 4h/400. (3) Rendering. Per the board's "in the port" notes: SkSL runtime effects drawn on the compositor's thread (ComposerLightView's CompositionCustomVisualHandler), uniforms only per frame, blurs baked (blurred rounded rectangles, once per size, scale or blur; on the GPU when there is one), no per-frame blur. Border beam Large and Small bake their static layers (the inner wash with its inset shadow and bands, the stroke's blobs on the ring, the ring) and each frame applies the package's window profiles at the share of the outline a pixel maps to (fitted: the ray from the centre or from an end's centre, exactly where beam.js's conics place their stops; as the package: the angle), the highlight, the bloom (the highlight's conic as the Gaussian-weighted mean over the box's inside, times the blurred edge) and the hue-rotate/brightness/saturate chain clamped per step. Line and the pulses evaluate their moving radial gradients directly as ellipse primitives; a blurred layer's blobs are widened to the blur's second moment instead of blurred. The Uiverse light: the turning two-tone over the blurred clip, the gradient taken at the restricted kernel's mean and smoothed by its spread along the gradient (both from the baked coverage's derivatives), the rim, the 3 px halftone (as a multiply on the light, equivalent to the playground's window-coloured dot screen), the inside rim, the playground's 13 px fade at the window's bottom edge. The outer light is masked to outside the composer (the playground's opaque plate). (4) The app. Every ComposerArea gets a ComposerLightSlot over the group's glass and under the tab and the pill (drawn before the group, after the glass material), reading AppSettings.ComposerLight (a change reaches every composer at once), the composer's state (ENGINEERING DECISION: running while a turn runs; typing while the draft holds anything; else at rest), the thread's maker liquid stops (heart and second dark, the deeper pair light) and Chrome.Accent for the Uiverse Maker/Accent schemes. ComposerLightView takes any settings value, so Settings > Customization can host a live preview with unsaved settings (the page itself is not built here). (5) Reduce motion: one still (k = 0, every transition at once, as the playground's prefers-reduced-motion rule). Without a GPU (Skia's software rasterizer) the light also draws one still: its shaders cost 15 to 60 ms a frame there (ComposerLightCostTests), which would make typing stutter. Evidence: 18 reference frames of the playground board itself (headless Chrome, tests/fixtures/composer-lights with ref.js) re-rendered by the port within per-job tolerances (Border beam Large, the default: at most 24 to 40 levels on at most 0.1 % of pixels, the stroke's corner antialiasing; the Uiverse light: at most 21 levels on at most 0.1 %); the full 63-frame comparison and the app-composer frames in E:/Droppy/work/design/composer-lights/port-evidence/. Known gap: Pulse Outside in the light theme (6.5 % of pixels off by more than 6 levels: the widened blobs are dimmer than Chrome's blur). Not measured: the GPU's time per frame (no GPU headless; estimated a few hundredths of a ms for the default beam and the Uiverse light, up to about 1 ms for Pulse Outside at 2x on an integrated GPU); the cost of the glass material redrawn under the animated light. Tests (Decision ED-251): BorderBeamMathTests, ComposerLightClockTests, ComposerLightSettingsTests, ComposerLightAnimatorTests, BorderBeamSceneTests (Marrow.Core.Tests); ComposerLightRendererTests, ComposerLightFidelityTests, ComposerLightViewTests, ComposerLightCostTests (Marrow.UI.Tests); AppSettingsComposerLightTests, ComposerLightSlotTests, ComposerLightEvidenceTests (Marrow.App.Tests). Credits: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (border-beam, MIT, Jakub Antalik; the Uiverse.io button, MIT, SelfMadeSystem).

## ED-250

[UI][SETTINGS][THEME][MOTION] The accent is the user's preference, picked on a Look card at the top of Settings > Appearance (OD-0088 variant D3 of the locked board E:/Droppy/work/design/accent-d3-locked.dc.html with the 22 colours of accent-palette-locked.json; exact spec E:/Droppy/work/design/accent-build/SPEC.md; OD-0075, OD-0081, OD-0076, OD-0069). Owner-ruled deviations from the source, which has no accent preference (Chrome.swift:80-87: the theme's accent ?? the system's) and a Theme capsule row (SettingsView.swift:424-426, :1155-1212). (1) MODEL. Port/AccentPalette.cs (Marrow.UI): the 22 (ten Classic: Windows accent, Blue, Purple, Pink, Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Teal, Graphite; twelve Signature: Ocean, Denim, Indigo, Lilac, Orchid, Rose, Coral, Bronze, Sage, Alpine, Mint, Slate), each with its Dark and Light hex, drawn as given; the lift of SPEC 3.2 (the board's liftCard, OKLCH lightness in 0.0005 steps at fixed hue, chroma kept unless sRGB cannot hold it, the first 8-bit colour with 3.1:1 on the card #4D4C4B / #D1CFCF and 3:1 on #1E1E1E / #FFFFFF), cached; OnColor (#FFFFFF or #111111). One new defaults key, "accent" (AppSettings.Accent), default and fallback for a missing or unknown id "windows", written only on a pick, mirrored into AccentChoice as the theme is into ThemeManager (set before the theme at launch so the one ThemeManager change of AppSettings.swift:732 carries it and posts once). "windows" is the default accent: the Windows accent under System, Light and Dark, the theme's own (raw) under a named theme; any other pick is its palette colour (an appearance pair) and stays across theme changes. (2) WHERE IT APPLIES (Chrome.accent's sites). ThemeManager.Spec carries the pick in place of the theme's accent when the pick is not the default (so Chrome.accent, Chrome.accentNSColor and Popovers' presentedChrome tint follow), and a pick posts ThemeManager.DidChange as a theme change does (its observers re-read the accent: HydraChargeLayerView, WorkingIndicators, the theme capsule). ThemeTint (WindowManager.swift:181-193) tints the window with the pick, else theme.spec.accent (nil for System, Light and Dark, as the source). Chrome.Accent and AccentNSColor are now one SwiftColor per spec that reads the spec's accent ?? the system accent whenever it is resolved (a new SwiftColor kind, Live), and a brush drawn with it re-resolves on ThemeManager.DidChange, easing to the new colour over 0.32 s CSS ease on the frame clock (SPEC 6.4; at once under Reduce Motion or with no frame clock; on the control's own dispatcher). (3) AMENDS ED-238 (3). The Windows accent is drawn lifted by the picker's rule wherever it is resolved, in place of ED-238's mix toward white or black (the board previews #0067C0 as #4B9FFC in Dark); ED-238's floor (3:1 on the window) holds for every accent: #000000 is #9C9C9C in Dark and black in Light, the headless #0078D7 #409FFF / #0073CF, #E81123 #FF6D63 / #E4051F. A theme's own accent and a palette pick are never lifted for the app; a named theme's own accent is lifted only where the picker draws it as the first swatch (seven of 23 change, e.g. Claude #C15F3C to #E6805C). (4) THE LOOK CARD (Port/LookCard.cs, Port/LookMotion.cs, Marrow.App). The page's first card (the source's first card follows without its Theme row, then the picture and zoom cards); its shell is the port's ChromeCard / ChromeRow / ChromeRowDivider (the board's 12 radius and 11 padding were stand-ins), everything inside takes the board's numbers: the mini window 496 x 128 flush with the card's top (SPEC 9.1, as the locked frames draw it), every bar, bubble, composer, tube and send button at SPEC 2.2's geometry and colours; the Theme segmented control (System | Light | Dark | "More themes" or the named theme's name; track 28, pill .3 s ez, labels crossfading in a box of the current label's width); the menu of the 23 named themes (the source's AppTheme order under Dark and Light, its ThemeSwatch per row) 264 wide, 15 below the control, its list 260 and scrolling with 16 / 22 fade masks, opening on the current row 64 below the top, growing .2 s / .22 s pop-in from 44 in from its right edge and closing .15 s, hung over the cards below (the card has ZIndex 1; the port's windows have no overlay layer); the Accent row (ten swatches on a 26 pitch and More 50 x 24, one ring per line, the Windows dot on the Windows accent only) and the Signature fold (36 open, opacity .17 s after .13 s opening, .08 s shutting, the line from -6, the card and everything below following its height); More's held state (a ring round More, the pick's dot, the chevron narrowing out) over a Signature pick when shut; hover, press and keyboard-focus states; detail lines that crossfade (.2 s) and name the accent without a hex (SPEC 9.2, OD-0088 "Names only"), "<Name> · over <Theme>" only when it fits the text column; the window colours of the card mixed by one appearance value easing .32 s when the theme's appearance turns over. Every transition is a CSS transition replayed on the frame clock (ED-117, ED-237: from where the value is, along the board's curve, complete within 1 ms of its end), Reduce Motion (ED-084) stills them. Keyboard (SPEC 7): each segment a tab stop (Space or Enter; segment 4 opens the menu, by keyboard on the current row), the Accent group one roving stop (the pick, or the first swatch when shut over a Signature pick; Signature swatches not focusable while shut), every arrow picks: Right / Left over all 22 wrapping, Down / Up the other line at the column (Signature j to Classic min(j, 9)), Home / End; moving onto the shut line opens it; focus moves without scrolling the page; More folds on Space or Enter; in the menu Down / Up move clamped, Space or Enter pick, Escape (however the menu was opened, SPEC 9.4) closes and returns focus to segment 4, a click outside closes. ENGINEERING DECISIONS: the segment and label widths follow SPEC 2.3's rule measured in the port's type (Inter, OD-0009), so they differ from its Segoe UI Variable table (the widest control is wider); a swatch's release eases back to the hover scale in .12 s as the board's frames measure (scenario 20), not SPEC 6.9's .08 s; the menu's row hover is PopoverItem's Chrome.Overlay(0.1) and its panel PopoverHost's (ED-238), the card's text, divider and rim the port's Chrome tokens (SPEC 3.3), the other new tokens the board's. NOT BUILT (named, not hidden; window-wide, SPEC 9.8): the whole Settings window turning over its colours on a theme of the other appearance; outside the card the window still changes appearance at once (the port's theme switch is a variant change), the card's own colours ease. The source's ThemePickerButton stays as its twin, no longer on the page. (5) TESTS CHANGED BY THE RULING. The Appearance page's structure (SettingsRestThemeTests, SettingsViewTests, SettingsViewFinishAppearanceTests, SettingsViewCoreProofTests: the capsule's own tests host it beside the page via ThemePickerHost; SettingsRiseTests: the wave's blocks on Appearance are now the title, the mini window, the Theme row with its divider, the Accent row, the fold, the rows card and the picture card, and the own-opacity test uses the rows card) and ED-238's accent values (AccentLegibilityTests, SwiftColorTests' three accent tests: the lifted values of SPEC 3.2). EVIDENCE: AccentPaletteTests (the 22 against the locked file, SPEC 3.2's 23-theme and six Windows-accent lift tables, OnColor, the resolution table), AccentChoiceTests (the spec, Chrome.accent, a brush easing frame by frame and at once under Reduce Motion), AppSettingsAccentTests (default, no write until a pick, relaunch, unknown ids, theme changes keep the pick, the window tint), LookCardTests (place, layout shut and open, every detail case, hover lines, colours, the held state, segments and the menu, scroll and fades, accessible names and states), LookCardMotionTests (every transition of SPEC 6.10 at every 1/60 s frame within 0.02 of the travel of the spec's table and 0.002 of the curve solved independently, CssCurve; largest steps; Reduce Motion), LookCardKeyboardTests (tab order, arrows, opening the line, More, the menu by keyboard and pointer, Escape, no scroll), LookCardRenderTests (the card drawn at the board's place over the still's own backdrop against canvas-frames rest-base and rest-named, dark and light: the mini window differs by a mean of 0.22 to 0.62 of 255 per channel (99.1 to 99.2 % of its pixels within 8) and its six landmarks by at most 2, every swatch dot exactly the board's, the whole card by 3.0 to 3.8 (91.6 to 95.6 % within 8; the rest is the type, Inter by OD-0009 against the board's Segoe UI Variable, and the row trailing padding, the port's 10 against the board's 11). Mutation checked, 26 of 26 killed (each re-run alone through one.sh): the lift's card floor and its direction, the system accent not lifted, the spec ignoring the pick, a brush not easing or easing under Reduce Motion, the window tint ignoring the pick, another default, a pick not written, the ring always sliding, the fold opening with no delay or on the wrong curve, More's labels not in sequence, the menu growing on ease, the appearance cut, the card ignoring Reduce Motion, arrows not wrapping, Up from Signature losing the column, the shut line not opened by keys, Escape unhandled, focus scrolling the page, the detail always naming the theme or carrying a hex, the first swatch not lifted, the mini window's accent bar in ink, a 27 pitch.

## ED-254

[UI][SETTINGS][THEME][MOTION] The accent picker, round 2 (OD-0088, OD-0076, OD-0069; spec E:/Droppy/work/design/accent-build/SPEC.md); amends ED-250 (4) and its note on the segment widths. (1) THE WINDOW TURNS OVER. A change of appearance no longer cuts any part of the Settings window. The window is marked (AppearanceTurn.SetTurnsOver in WindowManager.MakeSettingsWindow) and inside it every SwiftColor brush (SwiftColor.Brush's binding), every AnimatedColor (the sidebar's selected row), the backdrop scrim's strength (WindowBackdrop, Chrome.swift:258, 0.26 dark and 0.18 light) and the caption glyphs and rings (CaptionButton.Darkness) ease from what they show to the new appearance's colour over 0.32 s, CSS ease, on the frame clock, per channel premultiplied (SPEC 6.5, the board's scenarios 08 and 09). The change stays immediate under Reduce Motion, with no frame clock, for a control being attached (it takes its tree's appearance before it reaches the window), and in a window that has not drawn a frame since it was shown. This is a deviation from the source, where a theme change redraws in one frame. The main window is not marked and still changes at once. (2) THE WASH FOLLOWS THE THEME. The window's wash (WindowBackdrop :263-265, Chrome.glassTint at 12 %) and the sheet's (DetailSheetModifier :196, 22 % dark, 16 % light) read Chrome.glassTint whenever they are drawn (ThemeManager.LiveSurface). A named theme therefore washes the window with its surface, easing over 0.32 s; before, the wash kept the theme the window was built under. The amount is the source's 12 %, not the board's 16 %, which stands in for the port's glass (SPEC 3.3 `--tint`). (3) THE BOARD'S GEOMETRY. The segments follow SPEC 2.3's table: the board's label width + 22, and + 11 for segment 4 (61, 50, 48 and 106 at rest; 298 under Catppuccin Mocha). The labels are drawn in Inter (OD-0009), centred with the chevron, at least 6 from each end. The control is laid out unrounded against its right edge, so a width change glides to its last frame instead of ending on a whole-pixel step. The Look card's rows keep the board's 28 between text and control (ChromeRow's HStack gives 44). The Accent detail column is therefore 156 (the board's 155 with the port's 10 trailing padding), and every line of SPEC 4.3 fits whole, including the four the 140 column cut: "Terracotta · the theme's own" (149.2 at 11 Inter) under Claude and Claude Light, "Wave blue · the theme's own" under Kanagawa and "Magenta · the theme's own" under Codex. A line that would not fit falls back to shorter words; the rule now covers the theme's own line too. (4) TAB AND THE MENU. Tab while the theme menu is open closes it; from a row, focus returns to segment 4, as with Escape. EVIDENCE: LookCardTurnoverTests runs the real Settings window on the manual frame clock, dark and light. The click frame equals the frame before it within 2 levels everywhere. No frame moves more than 1 % of the turning pixels over half their change at once, outside the moving control and detail lines. The backdrop, card-fill and mini-window-surface pixels follow the 0.32 s ease within 3 % of their travel + 1.5 levels. The Theme title's brush follows it within one level and the caption glyphs' darkness within 0.001, every frame. Under Reduce Motion the change is at once, and the Dracula wash eases frame by frame. LookCardTests checks the board's segment widths under all 23 named themes and the bases, labels at least 6 clear; every detail line for 26 themes x 22 picks and 23 hovers, measured as laid out against its column; and the four formerly cut lines, whole. LookCardMotionTests checks the control's left edge on .3 s ez to its last frame with the right edge fixed; LookCardKeyboardTests checks that Tab closes the menu. LookCardRenderTests compares against canvas-frames at rest. Mini window mean difference: 0.25 and 0.22 dark (base, named), 0.62 and 0.61 light, 99.1 to 99.2 % of pixels within 8. Landmarks: at most 2. Swatch dots: all exact. Whole card: 2.91 and 2.88 dark, 3.49 and 3.72 light (95.6, 95.8, 91.9 and 92.2 % within 8; the rest is the type, Inter against the board's Segoe UI Variable, and the port's 10 trailing padding against the board's 11). Mutation checked, 14 of 15 killed, each run alone through one-names.sh. Killed: Settings window not marked; brushes not easing on a variant change; scrim cut; caption glyphs cut; sidebar row fill cut; wash fixed at construction; the 44 gap restored; RowGap 44; segments measured in Inter; Tab not handled; segment layout rounded; an attaching control easing; an undrawn window easing; easing under Reduce Motion. The survivor, the panel's whole-pixel measure removed, is equivalent: the segments are drawn against the right edge either way. Two failures predate this work and are unchanged. WindowManagerNativeTests.The_actual_Settings_sidebar_background_reaches_native_caption_hit_testing also fails alone on f79f4b0f7. ThemePickerThreadTests fails inside the whole Theme filter on 64ad888c1 too (HydraChargeLayerView reads ActualThemeVariant off the UI thread) and passes alone.

## ED-253

[UI][SETTINGS][THEME][MOTION][INPUT] The accent picker, round 3 (OD-0088, OD-0076; spec E:/Droppy/work/design/accent-build/SPEC.md); amends ED-250 and ED-254. (1) ESCAPE OVER THE SETTINGS WINDOW. The source's SecondaryWindow closes on Escape in sendEvent, ahead of every view (ThreadWindow.swift:47-55), and the port's tunnelling class handler did the same, so an Escape pressed in the open theme menu closed the whole Settings window. On the Mac a menu or popover over the window is a window of its own (NSMenu, NSPopover) that takes that Escape and closes; the port draws them over the window. PORT-ONLY: Marrow.UI.Port.WindowTransients lists the transients open over each window, newest last, and SecondaryWindow's Escape first closes the newest over it (the theme menu: closed, focus back on segment 4, SPEC 7, however it was opened, SPEC 9.4; a popover: its presenting state set false, as NSPopover's own Escape closes it), and closes the window only when none is open. The theme menu registers itself while open; every popover reachable in Settings registers through Presentation.SetPresented(popup, presented, anchor, dismiss): PlainControls.Popover (GlassPickerButton, ChromeVisualPicker, the theme capsule, the archive, Models, Shortcuts and MCP popovers, InfoHoverButton), HydraSettingsPage's cookbook and pair editor and AboutUpdateViews' release-note popovers (their own Popups). A focused text field keeps its Escape as before (:51). Not covered: an Avalonia ContextMenu (ParagraphTextPresenter, not in Settings) and the main window's popovers, whose Escape is unchanged. EVIDENCE: SettingsEscapeTests, on the real Settings window (WindowManager.ShowSettings, the manual frame clock): the menu opened by keyboard and by pointer, a GlassPickerButton popover on General and the Hydra cookbook popover each close on Escape with the window still shown and, for the menu, focus on segment 4; the next Escape hides the window. All four fail on 0243ffd63. (2) THE PANE'S TOP VEIL TURNS OVER. On a scrolled page the veil's two fades (PaneTopVeil, Chrome.swift:579-628) were rebuilt from new brushes in the click's frame on an appearance change (the verifier measured about 39,000 pixels change by more than 8 levels at once at 60 px). In a tree that turns over (ED-254) they now ease from what they show to the new colours over AppearanceTurn's 0.32 s ease (per channel premultiplied, the gradient's four stops kept, one brush per fade mutated each frame); a scroll redraws at once. The tint fade is Chrome.glassTint read as it is drawn (:589) and now also redraws on ThemeManager.DidChange, so a named theme of the same appearance turns it to its surface, easing, where before it kept the last theme's until the next scroll. EVIDENCE: LookCardTurnoverTests runs its whole-window turnover, dark and light, also at 60 px scrolled: the click frame within 2 levels of the frame before, no frame taking over half of a turning pixel's change, and both fades' colours on the curve within one level every frame (the window's top pixel, a composite of two easing layers there, is sampled only unscrolled); a scrolled Dracula change eases the tint fade to Dracula's surface at 30 %. The scrolled cases fail on 0243ffd63 (the click frame 147 and 153 levels from the frame before). (3) EVERY PAGE TURNS OVER. Three more parts of the Settings window cut on a change of appearance. The General page's Token activity month labels were new TextBlocks at each layout (TokenActivityMonthStrip rebuilt them in ArrangeOverride), so their SwiftColor brushes took the new appearance at once; the labels are now kept from one layout to the next, their text and place set again. The heatmap canvas resolved its cells only when something else invalidated it: a change of the system's appearance under System left the cells in the old one (Chrome.overlay, TokenActivitySection.swift:257, resolves as the Canvas draws); it now redraws on an appearance change and on ThemeManager.DidChange, and in a tree that turns over its cells ease from what they showed over 0.32 s. Text and glyphs that set no colour of their own inherit PortControlThemes' TopLevel default, a theme resource that changes in one frame (the About page's tagline, the provider icons on Providers and Models, Source control's Reveal); a window marked by AppearanceTurn.SetTurnsOver now holds that default as SwiftColor.LabelColor's brush, which eases. EVIDENCE: LookCardTurnoverTests turns each of the nine other pages over (Dark to Light) in the real window: the click frame within 2 levels of the frame before at every pixel that turns by more than 8, no later frame taking more than 1 % of them over half their change, and the end equal to a fresh drawing of every visual; under System the General page turns over on the system's own change (dark, then light) with a day cell of the heatmap on the 0.32 s curve. Mutation checked: the labels rebuilt, the cells not eased, the heatmap not redrawn on an appearance change, the window's default text colour left to the theme resource: each KILLED. Not mutation-covered: the heatmap's ThemeManager.DidChange redraw (a theme of the same appearance with accent-coloured cells; the tests have no ledger data). (4) THE FOLD'S NEXT CARD AT THE NEAREST PIXEL. Avalonia's layout rounding takes a desired size up, so what follows the Look card moved +2, +5, +8, +13 at frames 1 to 4 of the fold opening where the board's frames draw +1, +4, +8, +12 (SPEC 6.10's fold 1.38, 4.05, 7.94, 12.45). The fold now gives its height rounded to the nearest device pixel; its line still slides unrounded inside. EVIDENCE: LookCardMotionTests checks the next element's offset at every frame of the opening against the 0.3 s ease rounded to the nearest pixel (+1, +4, +8, +12 first); it fails on 0243ffd63 (2 for 1); the mutant without the rounding is KILLED. (5) LINKS. OD-0088 puts the pick wherever the source applies the theme accent, links included. The source's text links are Chrome.accentNSColor (LinkParagraphView.swift:482-487, StreamVeil.swift:423, already Chrome.Accent in the port). Its `.buttonStyle(.link)` buttons draw their label in the view's tint, and every window root tints its tree with the theme's accent (WindowManager.swift:186-192 ThemeTint `.tint(theme.spec.accent)`, a nil tint keeping the system accent; Popovers.swift:7-12 restates it for presented trees); the port drew them in SwiftColor.AccentColor, the Windows accent whatever the theme or pick. (Not changed, noted: FollowUpQueueTab maps the source's `Color.accentColor` (FollowUpQueueTab.swift:357-380, :468-471) to Chrome.Accent, another unit's mapping, so those already wear the pick.) The field is tinted with Chrome.accentNSColor (ComposerWorkingDots.swift:15-16), which is the pick, but the animated field sends one colour to the render server when it is installed or laid out, so a later pick or theme left the dots in the old accent until the composer was rebuilt. The field now resends the colour it resolves on ThemeManager.DidChange while attached (the source re-configures it as the body is drawn again, :104-111); the change is at once (the dots never ask a UI frame, PR-COMPOSER-103). Round 4 (the round-3 review, FIX FIRST: its three REVIEW tests, 38e5f2a63, now pass unchanged). (1) ESCAPE OVER A LINK'S POPOVER OR A TEXT MENU. Correction to (1) above: the text menu of a paragraph is in Settings. Markdown with links shows in the Licenses popover (LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES) and the About page's release notes; its paragraphs are ParagraphTextPresenter, whose Copy / Select All menu is NativeContextMenus' Win32 menu, and a right-click on a link opens LinkPopover, which presented through the presenter directly, so the window's Escape, which runs first, closed Settings. LinkPopover now presents through Presentation.SetPresented with its anchor (closed by close(), and gone from the window's transients on popoverDidClose); the text menu is among the transients over its control's window for the span of the modal menu, and an Escape reaching the window ends it (EndMenu) instead of closing the window. (2) A POPOVER INSIDE A POPOVER. DismissNewest kept only entries whose anchor sat directly in the window, so a popover opened from inside another (the MCP editor's Kind picker, MCPSettingsPage.cs:642; on Windows each popup is a top level of its own) was skipped and Escape closed the outer editor with its draft. WindowTransients.WindowOf walks each PopupRoot up through its popup's placement target (else its nearest logical ancestor, as Popup.Open places it) to the window that owns it. (3) THE WORKING DOTS EASE (SPEC 6.4 "Every use of the effective accent eases .32 s"). A later pick cut the dots to the new accent while every other use eased. The frame sent to the render server now carries the colour the field showed and when the change began; each render-server sample blends to the target on AppearanceTurn's 0.32 s curve (per channel premultiplied, as SwiftColor's accent brushes ease), a change during the blend retargets from what is shown, and the server asks for frames only while there is something to draw; the UI thread is never asked for a frame (PR-COMPOSER-103). The colour is resolved and sent as an immutable brush: the SwiftColor brush made at each resend kept a binding subscribed to the field for its whole life. The still dots (Reduce Motion) take a change at once; a change of the Windows accent reaches both (ColorValuesChanged). ComposerWorkingDotsAccentTests now lets the pick's 0.32 s run before reading the colour it rests in. (4) A SCROLL DURING THE TURNOVER. It redrew PaneTopVeil's fades at once, cutting them to their end colours mid-turn; the turn now runs on, retargeted at the colours of the new scroll position, and ends where a fresh drawing there is; a scroll to the top during it takes the veil and the turn away together. (5) THE TURNOVER TESTS UNDER THE FULL SUITE. Two causes, both found by running LookCardTurnoverTests beside the AppModel test classes (539 tests): 3 failed (Mcp frame 2, Models frame 0, light scrolled frame 1); alone they pass. (a) R-TEST-5: every AppSettings init assigns the process-wide ThemeManager.Current (AppSettings.swift:728, with the accent restored) and posts ThemeManager.didChange from its own thread, and some 60 test classes in parallel collections make a model; beside them a window proved frame by frame turned to another theme at a moment no test chose. The Headless collection, which changes and reads that state, now never runs in parallel with another (DisableParallelization: xUnit runs it alone after the parallel collections), so the App suite runs longer. (b) A frame drawn by dirty regions kept 31 opaque pixels (x 649-651, y 120-150 at the end of a Models page line) in the frame before the change, only when other test classes had run first in the process; the change redraws the whole window, and they "jumped". The change's own frame was byte-identical to the same frame in a run alone, so nothing in the turnover cut. The frame before a change is now the window drawn whole (every visual invalidated), as the end is compared with a fresh drawing. ## ED-255

[UI][CHAT][TIMELINE] ThreadTimeline: the eager stack, how a pass of the body reaches it, the check it makes of itself, and what the tests carry. Closes the F-1 draft (porting/reality/F1_TIMELINE_ED_DRAFT.md of branch claude/phase1-reality, written 2026-10-01: keep the eager row stack and do not port the lazy stack's repair machinery, provided the behaviour it protects is tested; the tests it asked for are ThreadTimelineScrollStabilityTests and ThreadTimelineCheckTests) and decides its open item (does Draw update the stack incrementally). DECISION: (1) Eager stack, no group-A repairs. Rows are realised eagerly in one StackPanel inside the one ScrollViewer, bounded by the window (TimelineWindow: 3, 24, 24 and the 96 ceiling, ThreadTimeline.swift:1804-1811). The lazy stack's own repairs (telling it where the viewport is: refreshViewport, beginNudge, restoreNudge, armViewportRefresh's refresh; remaking it: stackGeneration, :785-788, :881-887) have nothing to repair and stay unported (PR-CHAT-056/057/167/168 windows_path); armViewportRefresh only resets the drift. What the repairs protect is tested on the real timeline: a pane is never blank, a pinned reader stays at the end, a reader who scrolled up stays (ThreadTimelineScrollStabilityTests, ThreadTimelineCheckTests). (2) The check is ported where it concerns the reader's place. TimelineScrollTracking.CheckRequest (raised by the return to the front, the blank watch and the phase watch) is consumed as ThreadTimeline.swift:609-615 consumes it: reportActivity, then RepairLayout (:770-803): deferred while a scroll is in progress (repairSkippedWhileScrolling), a viewport past the end or a reader pinned to the end and away from it goes to the end unanimated, and a blank viewport is repaired in up to three steps a beat apart, the first two (the lazy stack's own) only counting, the third pinning the reader to the end; the fourth blank is left alone. (3) A pass of the body diffs the stack. A row whose block id survives is the same view in the same stack in the same place and is never taken out of the tree and put back (the F-1 note measured 100 to 170 ms a pass at 96 rows, and a popover anchored in a row, a selection, the hover and the focus were lost at every new entry; measured 2026-10-03 headless with 96 blocks laid out, a pass that changes nothing costs 1.1 ms (at most 1.5) kept in place and 92 ms (at most 170) when every row is taken out of the stack and put back); a view made again for an id that stood takes the old one's place with no arrival; rows that left the window or the thread leave at once (:339 removal identity); a question badge that is answered leaves with the soft appear's removal where it stood; the earlier pill is made again only when its count changes; a row reports itself gone when it leaves, not at every pass (:338). The first pass of a timeline places its views with the stack (a thread opens in one frame, CATALOGUE.md C 164.452-164.640; SwiftTransition.Place), and so does the pass of a timeline that comes back after it had gone (the switch below); the passes after it bring new ids in with their transitions (:317-321, :396). A row whose block id stands is the same view whatever changed under it: `.id(block.id)` on an `.equatable()` row (:332-334) runs its body again when the block's value or its context changes, and every view that stands in the same place of that body keeps its @State; a view is made again only where the body's branch for it changed (the review of round 1 refuted the first wording of this decision, which kept a row only when block and context were both equal, rebuilt one whose rewind flag flipped (every finished turn in the window at every turn start and end on a provider that rewinds: Provider.SupportsRewind, :167-172) and so folded the turns the reader had opened, and rebuilt the finished heads' row when a head finished; round 2 refuted the next wording, that such a row keeps every @State inside it, because a message row handed a new rewind flag made its whole body again, so an attachment preview the reader opened closed, a selection in an earlier prompt was lost and a brief's popover closed at every turn start and end). DisplayBlockView.TryUpdate hands the new value to the view of every branch of the source's body (:1902-1935): the merge pill between its phases, a group (TimelineGroupView.TryUpdate: a work group its entries, the heads' list its rows by entry, a message row whether it can revert, which reaches its hover line's pencil and its right-click menu's entry only (TimelineRows.swift:131, :168-178; UserMessageRow.SetCanRevert refills the pencil's slot, and the menu reads the flag from a box when it opens, without capturing the row), so the attachment strip with its preview, the quote chips, the bubble's selectable text, a brief's popover and the row's hover and editor stand, a reply its summary (AssistantMessageRow.SetSummary makes the reply's body again; no pass hands one a new summary, since a group's reply has no turn and so none, :1851-1855)), a running turn (TurnRunningBlock.Update, and each row's context: the message of a turn left without its end marker loses and regains its pencil as a later turn starts and ends), a finished turn (TurnFinishedBlock.Update: the fold and the files worked out once stay, the user rows and the file card's revert button are handed canRewind, the header says the new summary, the steps or the answer are made again only when the turn's entries changed, the heads' list follows its entries), the working line (a working block's work: the build hands it none today, :1600-1602 `liveWork: []`, so that path is proven by handing the view the value as a pass would), and the heads' pills (HydraHeadsWorkingRow.Update runs the ForEach diff of :411-415, so the pill that joins glides in beside the ones already there and an open report stays open). ## ED-256

[UI][CHAT][POPOVER] The TimelineRows parity pass's own engineering decisions (heading ED-256; the lead numbers it at merge; amended by the adversarial reviews of 2026-10-03). Each is a necessary internal choice made against the contract's section 8; none changes what the Mac shows except (4), which is owner-ruled. (1) THE onDisappear READING. SOURCE FACT: `.onDisappear` (ChatBadge.swift:75 and :109, TimelineRows.swift:198, and MessagePopoverMenu.swift:6 and :13-18, the row menu's own state and popover) fires only when a view leaves the hierarchy; a row the eager VStack keeps (ThreadTimeline.swift:384-391) has not disappeared, so an open badge popover, report, row menu or message editor stays open while other rows arrive. ThreadTimeline.Draw takes each kept row out of its old stack and puts it into a new one on every change of the thread, inside one synchronous pass, so Avalonia's DetachedFromVisualTree fires for a row that only moved. DECIDED: a control has disappeared only if it is still out of the tree once the pass is over (a Dispatcher post, then IsAttachedToVisualTree). Applied to ChatBadge (BadgePopoverCoordinator.Appear and Disappear, :74-75), the badgePopover modifier (the same pair, :108-109: the Hydra report, heads and brief pills, TimelineRows.swift:293, :470, :583), the row menu (MessagePopoverMenu) and the message editor (UserMessageRow). A real leave closes the popover one dispatcher turn later. LIMIT (measured headless 2026-10-03 with the overlay presenter, STOP #11 of TimelineRowsTests; corrected by review round 3, which found that the earlier wording named only the row menu): the reading covers each handler's own close and nothing more. A real Popup closes itself in the very Remove call that takes its placement target out of the tree, so on the real timeline every popover whose placement target is a view inside a row still closes when another row arrives: the message editor (target the AttachmentAnchorCapture behind the pencil, TimelineRows.swift:148-155; the anchor capture then opens it again on a new MessageEditor, whose @State restoresFiles, error and isSending start over, MessageEditor.swift:26-29), the row menu (target the row's content), the attachment previews of AttachmentStrip and ToolRow (target the strip, a thumbnail or the tool row's label), the tool row's head-steps popover (:1864-1867), the merge outcome's report (:1111-1120) and the turn-end card's files popover and revert confirmation (:2742-2766, :2777). Badge popovers (ChatBadge and the badgePopover modifier) hang from the window and are not affected. The cure is ThreadTimeline.Draw keeping its kept rows in place, as the eager VStack does (ThreadTimeline.swift:384-391): the ThreadTimeline unit's change (made on unit/parity-threadtimeline, a48fd1ae9), not this unit's. PR-CHAT-080 is blocked on it (STOP #11), and TimelineRowsParityReview3Tests' editor REVIEW test, which runs headless with the overlay presenter and needs no native check, is its regression guard: it fails on this branch alone and passes on the combined tree of this branch and unit/parity-threadtimeline (measured 2026-10-03, STOP #11). (2) PlanCard's IDENTITY. SOURCE FACT: ForEach(groups) in TurnRunningBlock keeps the card by its plan entry (ThreadTimeline.swift:1979-1984), so its @State isShowingPlan (TimelineRows.swift:2261) and its badge's @State coordinator (ChatBadge.swift:20) live as long as the plan is a row of the running turn, and an open plan popover stays open while the turn's other rows arrive; the popover keeps the content it opened with (ChatBadge.swift:138-147), so the plan's own updates reach only the next opening. The port builds a block's rows anew on every change. DECIDED: the identity (a ViewState and a BadgePopoverCoordinator) is held per plan entry and place in a static ConditionalWeakTable keyed by the TimelineEntry, and every PlanCard built for them reads it; the places are the running block with the plain groups ("turn") and the finished turn's two (:2642, :2672), which are other views in SwiftUI with their own @State. The table lives as long as the entry. REVIEW FINDING (round 2, PLAUSIBLE from code reading; fixed): the coordinator then outlived its badge and held the Window (Swift's shownIn is weak, ChatBadge.swift:119), the Popup's PlacementTarget and the frozen detail; shownIn is now a WeakReference and a closed popover releases its PlacementTarget and Child (a closed NSPopover keeps neither) after its Closed event, so the closing animation still draws it; the next opening sets both again. Measured headless: a closed window is not reliably collected (the platform keeps some of them reachable), so the proof is structural (ChatBadgeTests: the popover keeps its content while it closes and lets go when closed; no coordinator field holds a window). OWED NATIVE: a memory check that a closed secondary window is collected after a plan popover was opened in it. (3) ChatBadge's PORT-ONLY API. The optional `coordinator` parameter (a host whose identity outlives the control hands in the coordinator it keeps) and the Update method (the host's body ran again with new values for the same badge: its label, glyph, caption, chevron, attention dot, enabled state, accessibility name and value follow, the pill and an open popover stay, and the next opening builds the new detail) have no Swift counterpart, because SwiftUI keeps a view's identity across its host's bodies. They are new API; ED-095, which the code comments cited for them, covers only the order of parameters. (4) THE PENCIL'S FADE. SOURCE FACT: the Mac cuts the message hover line's opacity with no animation (TimelineRows.swift:161 `.opacity(isHovering || isEditing ? 1 : 0)`; 2-chat-use.mov 23.415-24.187 s, catalogue hover.message-edit-pencil). SOURCE FACT: InlineText's link branch asks the favicon of each host it shows (fetchLinkAssets, MarkdownView.swift:1226-1238 at B3; FaviconCache.image, :914-953), which goes out to https://host/favicon.ico. Round 5 added a seeded in-flight fetch to the tests it changed and said every test that shows a link had one; the new merge-outcome row (a markdown link to gitlab.com) had none. Measured 2026-10-03 (round 6): that row sent nothing, by accident, and left the cache with gitlab.com in its failed set: the report is measured in a hidden window first (PopoverScroll.MeasuredHeight attaches and detaches the paragraph in one turn), so the ask is cancelled before it starts, URLSession.Data fails a cancelled request before it reaches the client, and FaviconCache records the host as one with no icon, which a later test for the same host (HydraMergePopoverCardTests) then finds. DECIDED: (i) the rig NoLinkNetwork (Marrow.App.Tests, Fixtures) is made first by every test of this unit that shows link text: each host it names has an in-flight fetch that never ends (HydraMergeFaviconSeed), the flow's HTTP client is a fail-closed InProcessHttpHandler with no answer (a request to a host that is not loopback is refused in process and recorded), and the cache's own tables are watched, so disposing the rig fails the test for a refused request and for a host the cache learned that the test did not name; NoLinkNetworkTests holds those claims (main-actor work runs under the rig's client, an unnamed host is refused and reported, a cancelled ask is reported, a named host asks nothing; mutants killed). (ii) The audit: with MARROW_TEST_NETWORK_AUDIT set to a file path, each test assembly (Marrow.Testing.NetworkAudit, installed from a module initializer of Marrow.App.Tests and Marrow.UI.Tests) makes the process default HTTP handler fail-closed and appends every non-loopback request to that file, whatever flow makes it; unset, it does nothing. AUDIT (2026-10-03, round-6 fix): positive controls first: a direct request and an unseeded link's favicon each reached the handler and were logged in Marrow.App.Tests, a direct request in Marrow.UI.Tests, with no socket opened. Then every Views.Chat test (Marrow.App.Tests, 1405 tests, 1404 passing; the failure is PR-CHAT-080's guard, STOP #11): the first run logged two requests, both GET https://gitlab.com/favicon.ico, from the two Copy link tests of HydraMergePopoverCardTests (the HydraMergePopover unit's tests, not a test this unit added or changed); each now names gitlab.com in the rig (a mutant that names none fails the first of them, and each leaks alone), and the second run logged nothing. The whole Marrow.UI.Tests assembly (2292 tests, none failing) logged one request, GET https://gitlab.com/favicon.ico, which run class by class comes from LinkPopoverRowsTests and from LinkPopoverTests (the LinkPopover unit's tests, whose popover asks its host's favicon when it appears; the UI test project has no rig): OPEN, not changed here. The scoped check of round 6 ran the audit again with the favicon cache's memory and failed-set short-cuts switched off (an uncommitted probe, so that a host an earlier test left in the cache cannot hide a request): the Marrow.UI.Tests Markdown filter logged five GET https://gitlab.com/favicon.ico (those of LinkPopoverRowsTests and LinkPopoverTests among them) and one GET https://github.com/favicon.ico, which a normal run hides behind another test's cache entry, and this unit's own UI classes (InlineTextTests, LinkHoverTests, LinkParagraphViewTests, StreamVeilTests, TableBlockPanelTests; 107 tests) logged nothing. Both are OPEN for the lead, outside this unit; the hover case added by that check (InlineTextTests) seeds its host's icon and logged nothing under the audit. Every test this unit added or changed that renders link text (the Views.Chat tests above, InlineTextTests, LinkParagraphViewTests, LinkHoverTests, TableBlockPanelTests) asked nothing. Rerun: MARROW_TEST_NETWORK_AUDIT=<file> bash one-names.sh <worktree> Marrow.App.Tests "FullyQualifiedName~Marrow.App.Tests.Views.Chat&FullyQualifiedName!~Native", then read the file: it must be empty.

Resolved (lead's ruling 2026-10-03, zero stutter: neither the stall nor dropping the warm-up): (1) Kept programs: Skia's own persistent cache is not reachable (SkiaSharp 3.119's GRContextOptions has no PersistentCache; Avalonia makes the context), but Avalonia's ANGLE (D3D11) offers EGL_ANDROID_blob_cache: GpuProgramCache installs its two callbacks on the render thread's display before the knob's programs are first linked and keeps each linked program's binary as a file under StoragePaths.Root\Cache\GPU Programs\<sha256 of ANGLE's renderer string (GPU and driver), the GL version and the app build's module id>, no new package; off (and recorded why) where the renderer is not ANGLE or the paths are not bound. Skia's own SkSL compile of the four runs on a pool thread before the first step. The CPU renderer draws the gem's picture on every other frame and reuses it between, so the first reads after a frame may show the last frame's picture (a first version of the test read one and failed on the head): the reads draw until the picture is the frame's own, and the full-opacity read is repeated at the end to show it did not change. (5) ENGINEERING DECISION, not mirrored (a port decision either way: the page has no fast toggle): turning fast mode on scales the knob's signal by the incoming effect's opacity because a knob lit at once under a bolt not yet drawn is a light with no bolt, a jump the fade prevents; turning it off needs no such rule because nothing jumps: the signal falls to 0 at once and shape() lets the light go (the charge's 0.65 s smoothstep from where it is, the flare held 0.18 s and then falling on its two stages), which outlasts the bolt's 0.3 s fade, so under reduce motion, where the bolt shows the strike's still moment, the knob is at least as lit as the bolt still drawn on every frame of the fade (charge at least its opacity, flare at least its opacity times the still moment's flare; pinned). Without reduce motion that is not claimed: a strike landing inside the fade is drawn by the bolt and not read by the knob, so the bolt can flare above the knob's falling light (review round 9's probe: frame 6 of the fade, the bolt's flare 0.3811 at opacity 0.381, the knob's 0.3183). What mirroring would add is a charge or a flare for a strike landing inside those 0.3 s on the fading bolt; the knob does not read it (pinned). It is not mirrored because it needs a choice the page does not make: more than one fast effect can be leaving or arriving at once (a pair joining while fast mode is on: the old bolt fades out as the new fades in, both fast), and reading the brighter of two bolts on two strike clocks would jump the knob's signal at the crossover, where it now reads the incoming one only.
