## ED-291

[UI][SIDEBAR] The H3 sidebar-leftovers unit, Windows verification fix on unit/integ-h3 (the lead numbers this at merge). UI-SIDEBAR-017, -021, -022; PR-SIDEBAR-065, -070; OD-0076 ("nothing cuts"). UI-SIDEBAR-020 (the settle pop) is NOT resolved by this fix and stays UNRESOLVED.
1. ONE FACE PER ROW, UPDATED IN PLACE (LEAD RULING 2026-10-04, from SidebarView.swift:1739-1743; SOURCE FACT for the shape, ENGINEERING DECISION for the mechanism). The Swift keeps one ThreadRowFace under the row's identity and re-reads its inputs (isSelected :1721, the thread, mergeStage :1735, trailingClearance); its trailing padding keeps easing (:2068) when any of them changes. The port's SidebarThreadRow built a new ThreadRowFace whenever (thread, selected, mergeStage) changed, at the END value of the padding, so a click during the hover jumped the title's room from 34.5 to 60 in one frame (review commit de592d020). Now the row builds the face once and calls ThreadRowFace.Update(thread, selected, mergeStage, clearance, Transaction.Current); the face is never rebuilt for these three inputs. A thread change that alters the layout itself (IsSettled flips: :2023, :2037, :2053, the leading slot, the project line, the paddings and the minimum height) rebuilds the face's CONTENT inside the same object and carries the animated values (padding, weight, opacity) across, because they live in the face as scalars (AnimatedScalar), not in the content.
2. ONLY A CHANGED TARGET IS SET. AnimatedScalar.Set with no animation takes the value at once and stops a running animation, so an update whose target equals the target already on its way must not call Set (an unrelated input change carries no transaction and would cut the glide to its end). The face keeps each property's target and sets only on a different one; a different target in no transaction is taken at once, which is SwiftUI's rule (the new transaction replaces the running animation); a different target inside a transaction eases on from the value drawn now.
3. WHAT THE FACE ANIMATES, AND IN WHICH TRANSACTION. The four animated properties are the trailing padding (:2068), the title's weight (:2041, :2048), the title's opacity (:2042, :2049, :2075-2078) and the project line's mark (:2055). Each takes the transaction its input is written in, as SwiftUI does: the hover is written in withAnimation(Chrome.hover) (:1816-1818), so the padding glides; a selection is written with no transaction (SidebarView.swift:1737 `model.selectedThreadID = thread.id`) and only the BACKGROUND fill eases with it (:1750-1754 `.animation(Chrome.hover, value: isSelected)`), so the weight and the opacity change at once on a click, as the earlier tests assert. The weight does NOT ride as an in-between font weight: see item 6 (lead ruling 2026-10-04). The mark swap (folder to branch) inside a transaction is a crossfade (OD-0076, the port's motion language: ENGINEERING DECISION; the Swift changes the symbol name and SwiftUI crossfades or cuts by the transaction), each mark on its own scalar, so a swap that arrives while a mark is half shown fades it out from where it stands; with no transaction the mark is replaced at once. The round-2 review measured that the project name holds its place in every frame of the swap, both ways (both marks are the same 12 pt square, OD-0010).
4. THE BADGE. The leading badge (ThreadBadge, :2152-2166) reads the thread it was built with. The face builds it again, inside the same face, exactly when what it reads changes (provider, pinned, unread, last status) and keeps it otherwise, so a title change no longer restarts a running spinner.
5. TESTS. SidebarFaceInPlaceTests starts each property on its way in its transaction (hover, an unread record, a selection, a worktree) and changes each other input with no transaction (thread, selection, merge stage), asserting the same face object, the value drawn right after equal to the value drawn right before, still moving towards its end afterwards, and arriving; a selection taken back inside an animation turns the weight and the opacity round from where they stand; a thread that settles mid-animation rebuilds the content inside the same face and carries padding, weight and opacity; the mark crossfade, its second swap mid-fade and its cut without a transaction; the badge rebuilt only when what it shows changes. The PR-SIDEBAR-065 trait is removed from the padding/clearance theory in SidebarLeftoversTests (the record states the title's size, weight and opacity, not the paddings; the paddings are UI-SIDEBAR-017).
6. THE TITLE'S WEIGHT CHANGE IS A CROSSFADE OF TWO COPIES (lead ruling 2026-10-04: in-between weights resolve to heavier Inter faces (measured), so weight changes crossfade Regular and Medium). The first version eased the title's FontWeight 400 to 500 as a number; the embedded Inter is static faces and Avalonia resolves 413 to Bold and 425..498 to SemiBold (measured by the round-2 review, FontManager.TryGetGlyphTypeface), so the title was drawn past the source's .medium (:2041) for most of the 0.1 s. Now the title never asks for an in-between weight. The face keeps its weight scalar (400 to 500, on the transaction the input is written in) and draws it as two copies of the same text stacked exactly in one panel, Regular under Medium, with opacities (1 - share) and share, share being the scalar's distance from 400 over 100, so they run along the same curve (Chrome.hover, .easeOut 0.1 s, frame by frame). At rest only one copy exists (the Regular one at share 0, the Medium one at 1); a copy is added when its opacity leaves 0 and removed when it comes back to 0. A change that arrives mid-crossfade (a reversal, or any other input) retargets the scalar from where it stands, so the opacities turn round from their current values and nothing cuts (OD-0076); an update with the same target leaves it alone (item 2). No face outside Regular (400) and Medium (500) is ever drawn. The face has no other weight easing. ENGINEERING DECISION; the Mac's own in-between (SF is a variable font) is not stated by the pinned source. Tests: SidebarFaceInPlaceTests (the faces drawn per frame, the opacities along the curve to 1e-6, the reversal) and SidebarLeftoversReviewTests.REVIEW_the_title_easing_from_regular_to_medium_is_never_drawn_in_a_face_outside_regular_and_medium.

## ED-292

[VOICE][ENGINEERING] Voice typing unit VT-3 (Core recognition and session: seams, scripted doubles, SpeechLabel, StreamingTranscriber, TranscriptOps, VoiceSession, insertion rules; branch cloud/f-vt-3, built on cloud/f-vt-1; the lead numbers it at merge). ENGINEERING DECISIONS where voice-SPEC.md and the OD-0099 picks are silent; none changes an owner ruling. The code is `src/Marrow.Core/Port/Voice/{Seams,Session,Transcript}/`, the tests `tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Port/Voice/` (fixtures `Fixtures/VoiceSessionRig.cs`, `DecimatingResampler.cs`, `VoiceTestSinks.cs`).
1. Seams (V-2.4, V-2.5). Defined here with a fail-closed default each (`FailClosed*`, throwing `SeamNotBoundException` synchronously, also from Task-returning members) and one `Ambient<T>` each in `VoiceSeams`: `IAudioCapture`, `IVoiceActivityDetector`, `ISpeechEngine`, `IMicrophoneAccess`, `IStreamingResampler` (3), `IModelTransport` (`GetRange(uri, offset, ct)` -> `ModelTransportResponse(StatusCode, ContentLength, Body)`, the only member V-2.4 names). `IModelStore`, `IHardwareProbe`, the OpenAI handler seam are NOT defined: the spec names no member for them, so VT-6, VT-7 and VT-16 define them and add their stub and one line to `VoiceSeams.All`, which `VoiceSeamsTests` checks against the ambient properties by reflection (a seam added without a registry line fails V-T46). `ICredentialBackend` and `ISettingsStore` already exist. `IAudioCapture.Start(sink)` returns the mix format and the sink gets interleaved float samples in it (V-4.2: PCM16/24/32 to float is the capture adapter's job); the sink must be called on the main executor (the VT-5 pipeline posts its batches).
2. `ISpeechEngine` (V-2.4, V-7.1): `LoadAsync(SpeechModel(Id, Path?), EngineLoadOptions(UseGpu?, Threads?), ct)` and `TranscribeAsync(audio16k, DecodeRequest(Language, Prompt, Mode Live|Final, AudioStart), ct) -> Hypothesis(Words, Language?)`; word times are seconds from the first decoded sample (V-7.2). `DecodeRequest.AudioStart` is an addition: a real engine ignores it, `ScriptedEngine` and `VoiceScript` answer by session time while the window slides. NOT DELIVERED: the unload after 5 minutes without a session (V-7.9): V-2.4 gives the interface no unload member, so residency is VT-6's; the hub only shares one load between the hover and the click.
3. Resampling. The session averages the channels (V-5.1) and, when the mix format is not 16 kHz, passes the mono block to `IStreamingResampler` (VT-2's `PolyphaseResampler` implements it; its default fails closed). An exception in the audio path (an unbound resampler included) ends the session with the capture note instead of escaping into the audio callback.
4. The final schedule (V-7.6, V-T25). UNRESOLVED: the design's `planFinal` (voice-composer.js:304-324) is not in the repository. Built from the clause: the operations are `Diff(shown, final words)` in Diff order, Confirm left out (Landing inks, V-8.7); the first at 0.18 s, each later one after the one before by ITS OWN kind's spacing (Add 0.07 s, Revise and Remove 0.12 s); `ScheduleEnd` is the last operation's time (zero with none); Processing lasts `max(0.75 s, resultAfterClick + ScheduleEnd + 0.3 s)` from the click and the Landing timer is that minus the time the result took. Final words are tentative until Landing; Landing inks every tentative word 25 ms apart (V-8.7); a cancel withdraws from the end 30 ms apart (V-8.6). If the fixture shows another reading of the mixed spacing or the end, `TranscriptOps.PlanFinal` is the one place to change. "Adding a word confirms the previous one" (V-7.5) is left to the dictation layer (VT-11): the operations here follow V-7.3 (tentative = not yet committed), so a layer that confirms the previous word on every Add would contradict the tail. REVIEW (unit/integ-vt3, test-first, against voice-composer.js:305-323 read on the Windows PC): the design spaces the slot AFTER an operation by THAT operation's kind (`at += e.kind === 'add' ? 0.07 : 0.12`) and returns the slot after the last one (`return at - now`, 0.18 s with nothing planned), so `PlanFinal` now does the same: a revision then an add are at 0.18 and 0.30 s with `ScheduleEnd` 0.37 s. Still different from the design, for a ruling: its ORDER is the simulated stream's (pending adds and revisions in arrival order, then the shown words' final forms), which a Diff cannot reproduce (the design's own flow clicked at 7.16 s adds `too.` before revising `tool -> tooltip`; Diff order revises first), and the design schedules a no-op revision (0.12 s) for a word its final pass already added in final form, which the port leaves out.
5. Insertion (V-8.1, V-T31). Offsets are UTF-16 (a TextBox's); the neighbours are read as Unicode scalars (a surrogate pair is one character); "whitespace" is `Rune.IsWhiteSpace`, "punctuation" `Rune.IsPunctuation`; words are joined by single spaces; the caret ends after the inserted text including the space after it; a selection outside the text is clamped at both ends. The rule is read literally: an opening bracket before the caret is not whitespace, so `(` + word gives `( word`; no special case is invented.
6. `StreamingTranscriber` (V-7.3, V-7.4, V-7.6, V-7.8), choices the clauses leave open: words compare by exact ordinal text; a hypothesis word ending at or before the last committed word's end (+1 ms) is the 0.1 s overlap heard again and is dropped; the long-pause pass commits everything and the buffer start jumps to the newest sample; while the buffer holds no speech it trails the newest sample by 0.1 s (so silence is never kept and speech starts 0.1 s into the decode); the long-pause pass decodes only up to the end of the last speech frame; the 25 s rule is strict (more than 25 s, tentative words ending strictly before now - 10 s, from the first one on, stopping at the first that does not qualify); a decode is the newest 30 s of the buffer; the final pass decodes the buffer plus 0.3 s of zeros, calls the engine only when the buffer holds speech, and drops words that overlap no speech span (the padding included); a pass that throws or is cancelled gives its 0.5 s back; the speech state is the VAD's per-frame state with the hysteresis of V-6.2 counted in 32 ms frames (it leaves at the fourth quiet frame, 128 ms, the first multiple of 32 ms that reaches 100 ms); a word "arrives" for the label when a live update contains an Add; a live update with no operation is not raised. REVIEW (unit/integ-vt3, test-first): after a long-pause pass the buffer started at the newest sample, so speech that began while the pass decoded was dropped with the silence; the buffer now starts at that speech less the 0.1 s lead-in (at the newest sample only when no speech came after the decoded end).
7. V-14.8 script data. UNRESOLVED: the design's `SCRIPT`, `SYN` (rng 91) and `STREAM` (rng 7) tables of voice-composer.js are not in the repository (`tests/fixtures/voice/` does not exist), so the design's speaker words and times are NOT carried. Delivered: the mechanism that replays any such table (`ScriptedWord`: text, start, end, first guess, arrival delay, revision delay; `VoiceScript`: the capture signal, the VAD's speech spans, the engine's hypotheses by session time and window; `ScriptedVoiceSource`: a `VoiceSession` bound only to the three scripted doubles and a scripted microphone), with the four first-guess pairs the clause names (`theme -> team`, `switch, -> switch`, `tooltip -> tool`, `too. -> too`) exercised in `ScriptedVoiceSourceTests` on a script of this unit's own. The speaker's signal is a tone inside the speech spans and a deterministic dither of +-1e-4 elsewhere, never exactly 0.0, so a quiet room is not mistaken for a blocked microphone (V-4.5). When the fixture is committed, its rows become `ScriptedWord` values and V-T89's fixture half is added.
8. Session behaviour where the table is silent. Blocked ignores clicks until its 5.2 s are over. The click that would ask (V-7.14 D) is decided before the microphone and the model are touched, so Asking touches no seam at all (V-T124 with the throwing ambient seams). No model selected, no microphone, a device that will not open, a model that will not load and an engine failure each end the session at Rest with a `VoiceNoteKind` (in that order: ModelLoadFailed, NoMicrophone, CaptureFailed, ModelLoadFailed, EngineFailed); the wording is Q-V-7 A's variants page (D-VN, VT-17). A device event other than "in use" (removed, default changed, format changed) stops the session like a click (V-4.4); "in use" mid-session is an error that discards. A final pass that recognises nothing ends like a session without speech (the no speech note, Rest). The hover starts the model load whatever the language default is. `afterVoice` is read when Landing begins, not when the session starts. A new session started during Landing drops the send still waiting. The 300 s cap and the 270 s countdown are timers from the click that began the session (`CapCountdownActive`, `CapCountdownRemaining`, `CapCountdownStarted`); the countdown carries no look (D-VN).
9. One session at a time (V-7.11). `VoiceSessionHub.Active` is the session that is Listening or Processing. A click on another orb queues its start (`StartQueued`) and stops the active one as a second click; the queued orb starts the moment the active one leaves Processing (Landing or Rest) or, when it had nothing, at once. Only the latest click waits (an earlier waiting orb is dropped, never started and stopped at once); Esc or the same orb clicked again withdraws a waiting start; a question open in another composer closes.
10. Send (V-8.8, Q-V-11 C). The send intent is `SendIntent(text, AsReturn)`: the session knows nothing of a running turn, the composer's Return path (ComposerView.swift:370-381) does what Return does. READING: V-8.8 and V-T80 say "0.35 s after landing", the table says "Landing 0.5 s elapsed -> Rest, with send 0.35 s later"; 0.35 s is shorter than Landing's 0.5 s, so the intent is raised 0.35 s after Landing BEGINS (two statements against one). Never raised for cancel, for a composer that left, or for empty text.
11. Tests. V-T21, V-T22, V-T23, V-T24, V-T25, V-T26, V-T30, V-T31, V-T46, V-T89 (pure part), V-T124 and the V-T121 half that belongs to `SpeechLabel`, plus V-T80's session half and V-6.2's hysteresis, carry `Feature` VT-3, their `Spec` id and `Decision` ED-267 (the stand-in VT-1 used until this entry is numbered). All time is the manual clock (`TestRuntime`); no test uses a real timer, microphone, model, download, network or the real data folder. Note for later units: `ManualTimeProvider.Advance` moves time before the main loop has run what a click spawned, so a test that clicks and then advances calls `Settle()` (`TestRuntime.RunUntilIdle`) first; production has no such gap. Mutation check, run by hand against the VT-3 tests: 28 changes to the pinned numbers and 6 to logic each made at least one test fail (one logic change, a pass without the speech check, makes the test host loop forever, which also fails the run); the three survivors of the first pass (buffer cap 24.5 s, cap age 9 s, the VAD thresholds) got boundary tests.

## ED-293

[TEST][FIRST-RELEASE] SK-0 = DL-0 of porting/first-release/skills-ONDEMAND-PLAN.md section 7 (BUILD-PLAN.md section 2.5): the fake download server and the network guard. ENGINEERING DECISIONS for what the plan leaves open; none is a deviation. The plan's own sentences are SOURCE FACT of the plan; everything below is a decision.
1. WHERE (shared test support). `tests/Marrow.Testing/Downloads/` (namespace `Marrow.Testing.Downloads`): Marrow.Testing is the library every test project already references (ED-079), so SK-3 (downloader), VT-7 (voice model downloads) and UE-2 (update listings, "parsed from fixtures on SK-0's fake server") reuse it with no project reference added. It holds `FakeDownloadServer`, `FakeBehavior` (and `FakeTrickle`), `FakeDownloadRequest` (the log entry), `FakeArtifact` (bytes, length, SHA-256; `Pattern`, `FromText`, `Zip`), `NetworkGuard`, `FakeDownloadTransport` (`CreateHandler`) with `GuardedDownloadHandler`, and the internal `FakeTlsCertificates`. The tests are in `tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Port/Downloads/` (net10.0, so they run on Linux as well as Windows) with their helpers in `Fixtures/DownloadFixtures.cs`; a unit that tests a Services downloader puts its own tests in Marrow.Services.Tests and calls this harness.
2. NO KESTREL, NO PACKAGE. The https server is a `TcpListener` with `SslStream` and a small HTTP/1.1 reader and writer (GET and HEAD, keep-alive, a request body is read and ignored). Kestrel would need a framework reference in a protected project file, and `HttpListener` has no TLS on Linux. Writing the bytes ourselves is also what makes "drop after N bytes", "wrong length" and a trickle exact.
3. THE TEST CERTIFICATE is made in memory per server (ECDSA P-256, self-signed, SAN 127.0.0.1, 127.0.0.2, ::1 and localhost, valid from an hour ago to a day ahead), never written to a file or a store, so the machine trusts nothing new. `GuardedDownloadHandler` accepts a server certificate only when its bytes equal one a fake server of that test made and the only policy error is the chain (a name mismatch still fails). `FakeDownloadServer.PresentUntrustedCertificate` switches to a second certificate no handler trusts, for the "TLS failure" case (the client gets `HttpRequestError.SecureConnectionError`; no request is read).
4. THE GUARD is the handler's `SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback` (`NetworkGuard`), as the plan says. It lets a connection through only to a loopback address and port that one of the fake servers handed to `CreateHandler` listens on. Everything else, loopback ports of other listeners included, is refused as `SocketException(ConnectionRefused)` before a socket is opened, and recorded in `Refusals` as `host:port`. A host name is never resolved: only an IP literal and the name `localhost` (both loopback addresses, each checked against the allowed endpoints) are even considered, so a refused name causes no DNS traffic. IPv4-mapped IPv6 spellings are normalised. The refusal maps through URLSession to `URLError.Code.CannotConnectToHost` (Http.cs:999).
5. THE HANDLER'S SETTINGS: no system proxy (a proxy address is not loopback and the guard would refuse it, but the loopback fake must not be routed through it), no automatic redirect (a test sees the 3xx the server sent and the downloader's own policy is what is tested), no decompression, no cookies, no timeout of its own (R-NET-1; a test bounds its waits with `FakeDownloadServer.Guard`). The same handler works as `URLSession.Transport.Override(handler)` (proved) and as the handler of a downloader's own `HttpClient`.
6. FAIL CLOSED WITHOUT A FAKE. `CreateHandler()` with no server returns a handler that throws `HttpRequestException(ConnectionError)` with an inner `SocketException(ConnectionRefused)` for every request before any connection, loopback included, and records `GET url` in `Refusals`; `NoFakeConfigured` is true. Whether the PRODUCT seam fails closed by default in a test assembly is SK-3's to build: it should take a handler (or use `URLSession.Transport`), and a test assembly's module initializer may install `CreateHandler()` as its default. SK-0 does not change `URLSession.Transport`'s process default and no existing test assembly's behaviour (NetworkAudit and the in-process handler stay as they are).
7. THE SWITCHES (`FakeBehavior`, set per route at `Serve` and replaceable at any time by `Behave`; read once per request). Where the plan names a switch but not its wire form: (a) `AcceptRanges` true sends `Accept-Ranges: bytes`, answers `Range: bytes=N-` (or `N-M`, the first byte is what counts) with 206 and `Content-Range: bytes N-(len-1)/len`, and answers N at or past the end 416 with `Content-Range: bytes */len` (RFC 9110); false sends no `Accept-Ranges` header at all and ignores Range (200, the whole body), which is what the downloader treats as "start over". (b) `DropAfterBytes` sends the head with the full `Content-Length`, N body bytes, flushes, then closes the connection with a FIN (not a reset: a reset can discard bytes already sent on Windows, which would make "bytes received" nondeterministic); the client sees a cut stream. (c) `WrongByteAt` flips one byte (XOR 0xFF): right length, wrong hash. (d) `WrongLengthDelta` is a complete, well-formed answer whose body is longer (zeros) or shorter than the artifact, so only the downloader's own size check can notice. (e) `Status` answers any status (404, 410, 500, 503 ...) with a short text body. (f) `Trickle(chunkBytes, interval)` writes the first chunk at once and waits `interval` on the server's `TimeProvider` before each later one; tests pass a `ManualTimeProvider` so no wall-clock time is measured. (g) `RedirectTo` (301, 302 by default, 307 or 308) to any URI: another loopback host (a second server on 127.0.0.2), a plain-http server (`StartPlainHttp`), or an address off loopback. (h) `FaultyRequests` limits the faults of (b) to (g) to the first N requests of the route, so "the first attempt is cut, the retry is fine" needs no mid-test switching; the default is every request. An unrouted path is 404.
8. THE LOG. `FakeDownloadRequest` (sequence, connection id, method, target, path, the Range header as sent, its first byte, status, body bytes promised and sent, dropped, client closed early, headers) is added when the response is finished, cut or abandoned; `WaitForRequests(n)` waits for the log to reach n (bounded by the hang guard) so a test reads it without a sleep. "Bytes not refetched" is the sum of `BodyBytesSent` over the log. `PeakConcurrentRequests` and `HoldRequests()` (requests wait after being read until `Release()`; `WaitForArrivals(n)`) are there so SK-3's "six in flight" can be asserted; `ConnectionCount` shows that nothing connected.
9. LOOPBACK ONLY. `FakeDownloadServer` refuses to start on an address that is not loopback (`ArgumentException`); 127.0.0.2 is the second loopback host.
10. TRACEABILITY. The tests carry `[Trait("Feature","SK-0")]` as the brief asks, and `Traceability.AssertEveryTestNamesWhatItProves` rejected any trait it did not know, so `Feature` is now accepted there (pattern: two or three capitals, a dash, one or two digits, the build plan's unit ids). A Feature trait never counts as what a test proves: each test also carries `Rule` R-TEST-10 (no network, loopback only, no skips), which is the rule this unit exists for.
11. WINDOWS. NOT VERIFIED ON WINDOWS (this was built and run on Linux, .NET 10.0.112): the certificate is re-loaded with `X509CertificateLoader.LoadPkcs12(pfx, null)` and default key storage, the usual way to give `SslStream` a private key on Windows, but SChannel's handling of that key, and binding 127.0.0.2, were not observed there. If either fails on Windows, the tests that start an https server (all but the pure-guard and artifact tests) fail loudly at server start; nothing else in the harness depends on the platform. No test is skipped.
12. Evidence: 46 tests in `Marrow.Core.Tests.Port.Downloads` pass on Linux (five consecutive runs, with the three TraceabilityTests); a guard that allowed any loopback address failed 4 of them and a no-fake handler that passed requests through failed 1 (mutations run by hand, then reverted).

Windows verification addendum (2026-10-04, unit/integ-sk, Opus review): FIX FIRST then fixed test-first. (a) HTTP/3 (QUIC over UDP) bypassed ConnectCallback, so GuardedDownloadHandler.SendAsync now refuses any request asking for HTTP/3 or allowing a higher version (the fakes speak HTTP/1.1 only); all 13 non-loopback addresses of the PC refused. (b) The IPv4-mapped test no longer depends on port 4242. (c) A disposed server stops listening (new test). Item 10's Traceability change was dropped at the merge (staging's shared checker already accepts Feature/Spec); item 11 is now verified on Windows. Known leftover: a never-disposed server or a killed test process leaves its two CNG key files in %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Crypto\Keys (an ephemeral key breaks the Windows TLS handshake).

## ED-295

[SKILLS][BUILD][TEST] Skills downloads, unit SK-7 (DL-7 of porting/first-release/skills-ONDEMAND-PLAN.md section 7, "State model (Core)"; builds on SK-1's catalogue; the lead numbers this at merge). Code: src/Marrow.Core/Port/Skills/State/ (ItemState.cs the states, records and edges; AddonsState.cs the whole state; AddonsStateJson.cs; AddonsStateStore.cs; ItemDependents.cs; UpdateCheck.cs; ItemTerms.cs; StateRules.cs); tests: tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Port/Skills/State/ (8 test classes, 67 tests, all [Trait("Feature","SK-7")] with Rule R-TEST-4, or R-TEST-9 for the store). ENGINEERING DECISIONS where the plan is silent; none changes an owner ruling.
1. The nine states are DL-7's list; an item with no record is Available, and an Available item is never written (one state, one file text). A record is (id, state, installedPin, targetPin, failure) and ItemRecord.Problem() states the invariants: Available has no pins; Queued, Downloading and Checking name the pin they are for; Installed, Damaged and Removing have an installed pin and no target; UpdateAvailable has both and they differ; Failed has a message and the target it was for; only Failed has a message. A record that breaks one cannot enter a transition and cannot be read from or written to state.json.
2. Legal edges (the plan's flows, 5.4, 3.2, 3.5, 3.7, 3.8, 3.9, plus the OD-0099 review item 3): Available to Queued or Downloading; Queued to Downloading, Failed, or back; Downloading to Checking, Failed, or back; Checking to Installed or Failed; Installed to UpdateAvailable, Damaged, Removing; UpdateAvailable to UpdateAvailable (re-pointed), Installed, Queued, Downloading, Damaged, Removing; Failed to Queued, Downloading (Retry), Checking (a file placed by hand, OD-0099 review item 3), back, or Removing when something is installed; Damaged to Queued, Downloading (Repair), Removing; Removing to Available. "Back" (a cancel, or giving up on a failure) goes where the item came from, read from its pins: nothing installed is Available, a download of the installed pin itself (a Repair) is Damaged, any other target is UpdateAvailable. Everything else is refused with IllegalTransitionException and changes nothing (the state is immutable and Transition returns a new one). The test holds the code to a hand-written table over 17 valid records (first install, update and repair flavours) x 9 targets = 153 pairs, 53 legal (counted by hand), and applies every legal edge and checks the result against the invariants.
3. Transition arguments: a download started from Available needs its pin; from UpdateAvailable, Queued or Failed the pin pending is used and a different one is refused; from Damaged a Repair is of the installed pin only (3.5 "a fresh download of that version"); an update offer needs a pin different from the installed one and from the one already offered; a failure needs a message and no other transition may carry one; no stray pin is accepted anywhere else. Checking to Installed makes the target the installed pin; damage, removal and a finished check clear a pending update (Compute offers it again later).
4. A state read from disk is settled by AfterRestart (ONDEMAND-PLAN.md DL-19: a download resumes only on the next Download press): Queued, Downloading and Checking items settle by the "back" rule above; a Failed item stays with its Retry (3.9) and a Removing item stays pending for the next GC (3.8). AddonsStateStore.Load applies it; Save writes the state as given.
5. state.json (3.1): schema 1, items, acceptedTerms, declined, found; indented, ordinally sorted, ending in a line feed; read as strictly as SK-1's catalogue (the small exact-case enum converter is repeated here because SK-1's is private and this unit may only touch State/); dates are UTC instants ending in Z (an offset is converted on the way in, so only the instant is kept). The store takes the file or folder it is given, requires an absolute path, has no default (the caller resolves %LOCALAPPDATA%\Marrow Code\addons through DevDataRoot), treats a missing file as a first run, fails closed on a file that does not parse or is not UTF-8 (the file is left as it was, never replaced by an empty state), and never creates a missing folder.
6. Dependents (2.4, 3.8): Direct, Transitive and Installed from the catalogue's item-level needs (which already cover every skill's needs, an SK-1 gate rule). "Installed" means an installed version exists (an update, a repair or a failed update still counts) and the item is not being removed; it is the list 3.8's removal confirmation names. What removal then does to package sets and skill sets is SK-8's.
7. Update available (3.7): UpdateCheck.Compute is run after an app update, since the catalogue is compiled in. The catalogue's pin for an item is its pin, or for a set pinned one skill at a time (O3) the string folder=pin of every skill sorted by folder and joined with semicolons, or null when the catalogue has none yet. Plain text equality, never version order (a pin that reads lower is still a different pin; 2.1 says pins change only with the owner's approval of a report). An Installed item with a different pin becomes UpdateAvailable for it; an offered update follows the catalogue (re-pointed when it moves, back to Installed when it matches again); items in flight, failed, damaged, removing or not installed are untouched; installed items missing from the catalogue are returned as Orphans and ones whose catalogue pin is null as Undecidable, both unchanged. Each offer carries old, new and the plan's approximate size (3.7 "old -> new and the download size"). With the real catalogue today the pin is null, so the item is Undecidable, for A6 and the package sets P1 to P6; O3 has its composite pin and every other item has a version or a commit.
8. Accepted terms (2.5, 3.7): keyed by the licence file's SHA-256 alone, stored with the item id it was accepted for and the date; accepting a hash already accepted keeps the first acceptance; the caller passes the time. The hash of an item's licence is the SHA-256 the catalogue's files list holds for the item's licenceFile; while the catalogue has none (today, for every item) the terms cannot be keyed and are therefore always required for a non-open item and cannot be accepted (fail closed). An open item never asks. A changed licence file has a new hash, so it asks again. No item-level termsClass other than open is exempt, and the per-skill termsClass of A2's doc-coauthoring is not used here (the set is asked as a whole).
9. Declined offers (5.3): per chat, per item, idempotent; a decline in one chat says nothing about another; ForgetChat drops a chat's list so the file cannot grow without end (the caller calls it when a chat is deleted; this unit does not know about chats).
10. Found on this PC (3.6): MergeFound takes the catalogue, the ids a probe run probed and its results; the run's answer replaces the earlier one for exactly the tools it probed (found at a path, or no longer found) and leaves the others; only catalogue tools can be probed or found (a package set or a skill set is refused), each result must be for a probed tool, appear once and carry an absolute path (a Windows drive path with either slash, a UNC path or a rooted path; relative, drive-relative C:name, empty, or with an unexpanded %variable% or a control character is refused). Item states are never touched: the copy the user has and the copy Marrow downloaded are independent ("Download Marrow's copy anyway", 3.6).
11. ## ED-296

[SKILLS][BUILD][TEST] Skills downloads, unit SK-10 (DL-10 of porting/first-release/skills-ONDEMAND-PLAN.md section 7, "Missing-tool detector (pure, Core)", and the sections it cites, 5.1 to 5.5; builds on SK-1's catalogue and SK-7's state; the lead numbers this at merge). Code: src/Marrow.Core/Port/Skills/Detect/ (CommandTokenizer.cs, ToolEvents.cs, FailurePatterns.cs, MissingToolDetector.cs); tests: tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Port/Skills/Detect/ (9 test classes, 143 tests, all [Trait("Feature","SK-10")] with Rule R-TEST-4). ENGINEERING DECISIONS where the plan is silent; none changes an owner ruling.
1. Pure. MissingToolDetector.Detect(context, events) decides from facts it is handed: the catalogue, the AddonsState (installed, found on this PC, downloading, declined per chat), the chat id, and the set of items already offered in this chat (a runtime fact the caller keeps). There is no seam to the machine at all, so nothing can be probed wrongly: no PATH search, no process, no folder, no clock, no network. A test holds the source to it (no member takes a delegate; the four source files name no file, process, network, registry, clock, environment or delay API) and the file list is pinned. A context that cannot be trusted (blank chat, null catalogue, state or offered set, a null event) is refused with an exception; an event of a type the detector does not know is ignored.
2. Events and result. The four normalized events of 5.2: CommandHeld(commandLine), CommandFinished(commandLine, exitCode?, isError, output), SkillUsed(skill, itemId?), ToolRequested(name, reason). Result: Findings (one per item, first signal wins, each with the signal S1 to S4, the token it was found by and a verdict Offer, AttachToDownload or Suppressed with a reason), one OfferCard for the whole batch (or null) and AttachTo. "One offer at a time per chat" is the caller's: it passes the items already offered and keeps one card showing.
3. Tokenizer (5.3). One scanner for cmd, PowerShell and bash, since the shell is not known: separators are | || |& && & ; and line breaks outside quotes; an ampersand beside a redirection (2>&1, >&2, &>, <&3) stays in the word; single and double quotes group; inside double quotes a backslash before a quote escapes it, every other backslash is a plain character (so C:\x\soffice.exe survives in all three shells); a quote can start mid-word (pre"fix"post is one word, quoted); an unterminated quote runs to the end; an empty quoted word is kept. No ^ or backtick escapes and no $(...) are understood (the plan lists none). Program = the segment's first word after skipping, as the plan says, a cd segment (it runs nothing), call, env, VAR=value words and start (with its /options and one quoted window title, cmd's own rule), reduced to its last path component, lower case, without a trailing .exe, .cmd, .bat or .com (any other extension stays, so report.docx is not a program). A leading & needs no case of its own: it is a separator, so PowerShell's & 'C:\...\soffice.exe' works. For py, python and python3 a -m before the first non-option word names the module, which counts as a second target (case-sensitive -m; -c and script words stop the scan).
4. S2, a held command: the program of every segment goes through the provides index as a program; the -m module goes through it as a Python module first and then as a program (so python -m pip finds pip and python -m playwright finds the Playwright set), because 5.3 says "the module counts" and the plan does not say how. Only the first word counts: echo soffice finds nothing.
5. S3, a failed command. Failed = a non-zero exit code, or, when the provider gives none (Claude's tool result: error flag and text, 5.1), its error flag. A command that succeeded never signals, whatever its output says. Missing program: exit 9009 or the identifier CommandNotFoundException in the output (any exit code, any language) names the missing programs by every word of the output; exit 127, or no exit code, with "command not found" (German bash: "Befehl nicht gefunden"; UNVERIFIED wording from memory, the plan gives only the English phrase) names it by the word in front of the phrase only (so the shell's own "bash:" prefix is not mistaken for a missing bash); the Store alias is exit 9009 with python in the output, which also covers python3 (its message names Python, not python3; UNVERIFIED that python3's alias prints the same). In every case the program named must also be a token of the command (the plan's rule), where tokens are every word of the command, normalised, plus the words of a quoted word that holds blanks, one level (cmd /c "soffice a.docx" and bash -lc '...' count), in command order. A script that calls soffice itself, run as bash run.sh, therefore finds nothing (deliberate, per the plan). Missing module: Python "No module named" with the name reduced to its top package (looked up as a Python module, then as a program, for pip); Node needs MODULE_NOT_FOUND or ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND in the output together with Cannot find module or package, the specifier reduced to its package name (scoped names keep both parts; relative, absolute and node: specifiers are not catalogue names), looked up as a Node module only; Playwright's "Executable doesn't exist at" is the message the catalogue provides to Chromium. Order when one failure shows several: programs, Python modules, Node modules, Playwright.
6. S1, a skill used: the per-skill needs the catalogue lists (and no more: a skill with no listed needs gives nothing; SK-1's catalogue lists them for five A1 skills until SK-2 reads the rest). Skill names are folders; an unnamed skill is taken from the one installed set (an installed version exists) that has it, none or several give nothing (A1 and O1 both have skill-creator); a named set decides even when it is not installed. The finding's token is the need's id. S4, the model asks: the name is a catalogue item id (exact) or a program name from the provides index (any case, no extension stripped); anything else gets no hit. The plan does not say which spelling the model uses (DL-14 settles the tool).
7. Guards (5.3), in this order when several apply (the order is ours): installed and healthy (Installed, UpdateAvailable, or an update in flight or failed with the old version still installed; a repair in flight, which downloads the installed pin itself, is not healthy) → found on this PC → being removed (ours; the plan lists none) → a download running (Queued, Downloading, Checking) → the offer attaches to it → declined in this chat (SK-7's per-chat list) → already offered in this chat. A damaged or failed item is not there, so it is offered (repair or retry) unless already offered. The guards apply to every signal alike.
8. One card. All items found missing in a batch (Offer verdicts, in the order found) share one OfferCard: Requested, Items (everything to download, the needs they lack first in dependency order, each once, from item-level needs) and ApproxSizeMb (the plan's sizes added; null, not zero, when any is unknown). A need that is installed, found on this PC or already on its way is left out; the declined and already-offered guards are about the trigger, not about needs. 5.4 "one download with its combined size" and 2.4 "Also needs ..." are the sources; the card is data, how it looks is DL-18's.
9. Fixtures. The provider shapes in DetectFixtures.MissingSoffice are hand-written to the plan's descriptions of 5.1 and 5.2 (Claude: error flag and text, no exit code; Codex: exit code and output; Copilot, ACP, Pi, Command Code and native with and without an exit code; English and German cmd, PowerShell and bash texts). They are NOT recordings of real runs, which need the real CLIs; the Windows message texts are written from memory and are UNVERIFIED as exact wording. The detector's rules do not rest on the wording (exit codes, the identifier CommandNotFoundException, the program's own name), except the two bash phrases above. SK-11's adapters and DL-20 must check that real providers deliver these shapes; note for SK-11a: Claude's tool result may carry "Exit code N" in its text, which the adapter may parse into exitCode, otherwise the error flag and the bash phrase decide.
10. Not in this unit: the offer's states and the continuation message (5.4, 5.5; DL-13), the adapters that build the events from provider JSON (DL-12, SK-11), request_tool itself (DL-14), unwrapping of cmd /c, powershell -Command and bash -c beyond the one-level token rule, and the real "found on this PC" probe (WU-13; only its merged results are read).

## ED-298

[SKILLS][BUILD][TEST] Skills downloads, unit SK-2 (DL-2 of porting/first-release/skills-ONDEMAND-PLAN.md section 7, "Catalogue builder and its offline check"; builds on SK-1's catalogue and gate (ED-294) and SK-7's terms keyed by licence hash (ED-295); the lead numbers this at merge). Code: src/Marrow.Core/Port/Skills/Catalogue/CatalogueChangeReport.cs and SkillsCatalogueWriter.cs; tools/skills-catalogue/ (build-catalogue.mjs, sources.json, lib.mjs, CatalogueTool.cs, selftest.mjs, rehearsal.mjs, README.md); tests: tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Port/Skills/Catalogue/ (6 test classes and ChangeReportFixtures.cs, 54 tests, all [Trait("Feature","SK-2")] with Rule R-TEST-4). The network pin run was NOT performed (the lead's). ENGINEERING DECISIONS where the plan is silent; none changes an owner ruling.
1. Split. The offline, testable parts are in Core: CatalogueChangeReport (two catalogues in, one report out) and SkillsCatalogueWriter (the loader's exact inverse). The network work is a Node script (the repository's other tools are Node; fetch, crypto and child_process need no package), because the plan wants it run by hand with the network allowed. The two meet in tools/skills-catalogue/CatalogueTool.cs, a single-file .NET 10 program (#:project of Marrow.Core, #:property PublishAot=false, since a file-based app defaults to AOT, which turns reflection JSON off): finalize, report, gate. It is not a project of the solution (R-IMPL rule 8 forbids a new project), and it means the builder and the app cannot disagree about the schema, the gate or the report. The script writes only into the folder given to --out; copying catalogue.json over the embedded one is the owner's step after reading the report (ONDEMAND-PLAN.md 2.1).
2. The change report (3.7 "versions, hashes, licence changes, sizes"; DL-2). Every field of SK-1's schema is compared (a test lists the schema's fields and fails when one is added without a line), grouped as Item (added, removed, kind), Version (pin, pin hint, per-skill pins, package versions), Source (source URL, artifact URLs), Hash (artifact and file SHA-256, files and artifacts added or removed), Size (the plan's approximate size, artifact sizes, the total of an item's files), Licence (name, URL, file, the licence text, package licences), Terms (terms class, per-skill terms class), Needs, Provides, Skills (count, skills, plugin folders, skillsListed), State (pin state, count state) and Text (title, summary, vendor, notes). Every changed file is listed (DL-2 says "every"); ChangeReportRenderOptions.MaxFilesPerItem shortens the markdown for a human and always says how many were left out; the data keeps all. Hashes and commits show twelve digits, the data keeps them whole; sizes are written with invariant digit groups; line breaks inside a value cannot split a report line. An item's download size is its artifacts' sizes (all known) or else its files' (3.7 "the download size"), shown before and after for an item present in both catalogues.
3. The terms flags (2.5, 3.7). AsksTermsAgain: the item is not open in the new catalogue, and the hash of its licence file (SK-7's ItemTerms.LicenceHash, the SHA-256 of the licence file in its files list) was known before and is a different one now. A hash that arrives for the first time is not a change of text (no acceptance can exist for a hash that was never known), so it asks nothing again; it is listed as a licence change. TermsNowRequired: an open item that is not open any more. LicenceTextNotRecorded: a non-open item with no licence hash in the catalogue, changed or not, because SK-7 cannot record an acceptance without one (so A2 and O5 cannot be downloaded until the pin run records it); this is also shown for items that did not change, and for new items. A licence change in an open item is listed but flags nothing. The three flags are the owner's "needs attention" list at the top of the report.
4. Writer (the pin run's output must be read by SK-1's loader and passed by its gate). Canonical: two-space indent, line feeds, one final line feed, keys in the schema's declared order, enums as camelCase words, numbers the invariant way, no needless escaping (an apostrophe stays one), a required key with no value written as an explicit null, an optional one left out when it has nothing (pin hint, notes, skill count, a false skillsListed, empty skills, folders and packages, a hash hint, a per-skill terms class or pin). The committed catalogue.json was written by a one-off script with another key order; the writer's output is the canonical form from the first pin run on, so that file will change in layout as well as in values. WithDerivedPinStates sets every pin state from CatalogueGate.Missing, so a pin state is never typed by hand and the gate's "declared equals derived" rule cannot fail on the builder's output.
5. The script. Reads the pins from the previous catalogue (A6's full commit, ab024cdcfa7ca80be204acd4907656ba5a968589, given by the lead and recorded in sources.json with its source, is checked against the catalogue's eight-digit hint). Checks, and stops the item on any failure: every repository file's size and git blob id against GitHub's tree at the pin (no symbolic links or submodules; a truncated tree is refused), a tool's exact size and the digest prefix the plan prints, the digest GitHub publishes for a release asset, the sha256 PyPI lists for a wheel, the integrity npm's lock records for a tarball, Sigstore (cosign verify-blob, or python -m sigstore) for python.org with an identity and issuer the caller supplies, SHASUMS256.txt.sig checked with gpg against a key file the caller supplies and the zip's hash found in the file for Node, the .asc and the published .sha256 for LibreOffice. No identity, issuer or key is shipped or invented: the run refuses to start without them unless --skip-signatures, which makes the change report say NOT VERIFIED for each. gpg runs in a throwaway home with the key file imported; the key file's own trust is the lead's to establish, the record keeps the signing fingerprint. The first URL of every download must be on a host list in sources.json; redirects may go to any https host (ONDEMAND 3.2: the pinned hash, not the host, makes the bytes trusted) and the host the bytes came from is recorded. If any item fails the run writes catalogue.raw.json and run-record.json only and exits 1; nothing is repaired silently. Otherwise it runs CatalogueTool finalize and report and appends the Pin run section (every verification, warning and note) to the report. Measured sizes replace the plan's estimates in approxSizeMb (decimal MB, two digits); a difference of more than 15% from the plan's number is a warning.
6. Repository layouts (sources.json). Stated by the plan: A1, A2 and O1 take their skills' paths from the catalogue; A5 takes every skill folder; O2 takes the folders directly under skills/.curated that hold a SKILL.md, except pdf, openai-docs and anything starting figma, plus skills/.system/plugin-creator (2.1); O6 takes the figma folders; O3 finds each skill's folder at its own commit (exactly one directory of that name that holds a SKILL.md, else an error); A3, O4 and O5 take the plugin folders the catalogue names (a plugin folder is a directory that holds a SKILL.md somewhere beneath it) and list a name found nowhere as an error and an extra one as a warning; O4's plugin-eval drops files under a folder named fixtures ("fixtures dropped"). UNVERIFIED, not in the plan, to be confirmed from the first run's notes: that A4's and O4's and O5's plugin folders sit under plugins/ (the rule tries plugins/ and then the root and says which it used), that A6's Anthropic-authored plugins sit under plugins/ (BUILD-PLAN.md says only "Anthropic-authored"), and that "figma" as a name prefix selects exactly the eight folders. The licence file of an item is the licence at the root of its repository (LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt, COPYING and its variants, in that order) and is added to its files; licenceUrl is by SK-1's rule the raw URL at the pin. Per-skill front matter names are read from every SKILL.md and compared with the folder name (a difference is a warning, and SK-1's gate then refuses the file); per-skill needs, terms class and pin are kept from the previous catalogue. Every skill of a skill set or plugin is listed (skillsListed true), because SK-1's review fix makes an unlisted set unpinnable.
7. Package sets. Python: pip download with --only-binary=:all:, --python-version 3.14, --implementation cp, --platform win_amd64 and --abi cp314, abi3 and none, for the packages the catalogue lists (name==version where the plan gave one), so pip chooses the dependencies; each wheel is then matched to PyPI's own listing. The set's packages become the resolved wheels (names and licences kept where the plan had them, licence null otherwise), its artifacts the wheels, its pin "lock-" and the first sixteen digits of the SHA-256 of its sorted "file hash" lines (a new set of files is a new pin), its sourceUrl https://files.pythonhosted.org/ when it had none. The modules a set provides are NOT extended: SK-1's ED 6 left "and the rest" for SK-2, but no import name is assumed and none is computed (it would need unpacking every wheel, and equal-sized sets providing the same module are a gate violation); the run does not touch provides. Node: npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts with the plan's packages that have a version as dependencies, then the lock's tarballs for win32 and x64 (entries whose os or cpu exclude it are skipped and counted), each checked against the lock's integrity. Install scripts never run (3.4).
8. What the real run will surface, for the lead (each is a decision, not a guess made here). (a) SK-1's schema has one licenceFile per item, but A1, A2 and others keep a licence in each skill folder; an item with none at its root stays unpinned, and A2 and O5 (non-open) then cannot have their terms accepted (flag LicenceTextNotRecorded). Fix by naming a licenceFile in sources.json, or by letting the schema carry a licence file per skill or folder (a schema bump). (b) SK-1's Missing requires licenceFile and licenceUrl for every item, including tools and package sets, for which the plan names no licence file or URL; they will stay unpinned unless the rule is relaxed for those kinds or the values are supplied. (c) Plugins list skills and SK-1's gate allows a skill folder name once per item; the same name in two plugins of A3, A4, A6 or O5 is a violation the run reports. (d) P3 to P5 still have no consumer set (the plan names none). (e) The change report's first line of attention will be every non-open item for (a).
9. Tests that encode today's catalogue and will move with the first real catalogue.json (they are not edited here): SkillsCataloguePinsTests, SkillsCatalogueCountsTests (the plan's size sums, A6 and O6 counts, "every item unpinned") and SkillsCatalogueSkillNamesTests (the listed skills) of SK-1; UpdateCheckTests (A6 and the package sets undecidable) and ItemTermsTests (no licence hash anywhere) of SK-7. This unit's own tests that read the embedded catalogue assert only what holds for any catalogue (round trip, no change against itself, the attention list computed from the catalogue's own values).

1. Shape (V-5.3, V-2.3). `LevelAnalyser(sampleRate, subtractNoiseFloor = true)`: `Push(mono)` feeds the device-rate mono signal (a ring of the last 2048 samples), `Read()` is ONE analysis and returns `LevelBands(All, Low, Mid, High)` (doubles, 0..1). The caller reads at the spec's fixed 60 Hz cadence; the smoothing X = 0.65 X_prev + 0.35 |X| moves once per `Read`, as Web Audio moves it once per `getByteFrequencyData` (the port has no clock: a caller reads once per frame). `Spectrum` exposes the 1024 bytes of the last read, `Rms` the raw RMS. Before 2048 samples have been pushed the window holds zeros, as the node's buffer does. The FFT is a double-precision radix-2 transform; Blackman window a0 0.42, a1 0.5, a2 0.08; magnitude / 2048; bin 0 is the DC magnitude (Chrome zeroes the packed Nyquist term). The band edges use JavaScript's `Math.round` (halves up) and clamp to bin 1023, so a 16 kHz device gives a high band of 2000 Hz to Nyquist.
2. Noise floor on or off (V-5.4). The spec subtracts the floor from `rms` inside the same formula, so the AnalyserNode comparison of V-T18 needs it off: `subtractNoiseFloor = false` is the design's response exactly (the fixtures), `true` is the product's. `effective = max(0, rms - floor)`, then `all = min(1, max(0, effective - 0.004) * 5.5)`; the bands stay 0 whenever `all` is 0 (V-5.3), so a pause in a noisy room reads 0 in all four. The spectrum bytes are never changed by the floor.
3. Fixtures (V-T18). `tests/fixtures/voice/analyser/generate.cjs` renders four deterministic float32 signals (a 1 kHz tone at 48 kHz, a log sweep 80 Hz to 16 kHz at 44.1 kHz, a voiced stretch / noise burst / dead-zone tone / silence at 48 kHz, a three-tone signal at 16 kHz) through the REAL `AnalyserNode` of headless Chrome 154.0.8037.93 (`C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome`, playwright-core from `E:\Droppy\work\tools\pw`), in an `OfflineAudioContext` suspended every 128-frame render quantum near the 60 Hz cadence (47, 44, 94 and 62 reads). Per read it records `getByteFrequencyData` and runs the design's own `fileRead` arithmetic (voice-composer.js:114-127) on Chrome's data. It also checks that Chrome's `getFloatTimeDomainData` equals the input slice [p - 2048, p) at every read (the alignment proof) and fails if not. A second run reproduces the files byte for byte. Committed: the generator, `manifest.json`, and per signal `<name>.f32` (the samples, little-endian) and `<name>.json` (positions, 1024 base64 bytes, rms, all, low, mid, high per read).
4. Result (V-T18). The port equals Chrome exactly on x64 .NET 10: all 252,928 spectrum bytes and every all / low / mid / high value (bit for bit, max difference 0).
5. Tolerance (V-T18). The spec states none ("equals Web Audio's"), so the test states the strictest: every byte equal, the four values within 1e-12. Chrome's FFT is float32 and the port's is double, so a byte on a `floor()` edge could differ on another machine; none does here. If a reviewer's machine ever shows one, the tolerance to introduce is one byte on the spectrum (and 2/255 on a band mean), not more.
6. Followers (V-5.5, V-T20). `Follower.Follow(x, target, dt, up, down)` is the design's `follow` (tau = up when the target is above, otherwise down; `max(1e-3, tau)`). `LevelFollowers.Step(raw, dt)` updates the four band followers (attack 0.07 s, release 0.24 s, a value under 1e-4 set to exactly 0) and then the voice value from the band value just updated (0.12 s / 0.45 s), the order of voice-composer.js:718-722. The "values under 1e-4 to 0" rule is read, as in the design, for the BAND values only: `v = follow(...)` has no zeroing line in the source, so `Voice` decays exponentially and is not zeroed (it is below 1e-4 only long after the bands read 0, and no consumer can tell). The orb-audio.ts `gain` (0.7) of the standalone orb page is not part of V-5.5 and is not carried.
7. Bad numbers. A negative or non-finite `dt` is no time (nothing moves), a non-finite raw band reads as 0, and a non-finite input sample reads as 0 in the analyser and the floor, so one bad frame from a device cannot poison the smoothing for the rest of a session. The design would propagate a NaN; this is a port-side guard.
8. `NoiseFloor` (V-5.4, RESEARCH 3.2 item 3). Consecutive, non-overlapping 50 ms RMS windows (`round(rate * 0.05)` samples), the last 40 kept in a ring, the floor their minimum. A window counts when complete, so the floor is 0 for the first 50 ms; a quiet window is forgotten 2.0 s after it ended. It tracks the minimum of the whole stream including speech: a session that starts mid-sentence has a high floor until the first pause (the rule as written; no warm-up is invented).
9. `PolyphaseResampler` (V-5.2, ED-292 (3)). `IStreamingResampler.Process(inputRate, mono, output)`. The ratio is 16000/g to rate/g (L/M). The prototype is a Kaiser-windowed sinc designed for 70 dB (60 required): passband edge 7200 Hz, stopband edge 8000 Hz, cutoff 7600 Hz, length by Kaiser's rule (261 taps at 48 kHz, about 38,000 at 44.1 kHz), summing to L so the passband gain is 1; stored as L phases. It is odd-length and symmetric, and its centre delay is taken out of the output timing (output sample k is time k / 16000 of the input, so an impulse at 0.1 s lands on output sample 1600). Measured (a sweep every 50 Hz, 0.6 s tones): worst stopband from 8 kHz up -70.6 dB (48k, 44.1k, 32k, 22.05k, 96k), passband flat within the measuring noise of a 0.6 s tone. Streaming equals one-shot bit for bit (each output is a fixed-order double sum over the input samples around it). A rate change or `Reset()` starts a new stream; the filters are cached per rate. Rates below 16 kHz are up-sampled with the stopband at the input's own Nyquist and the passband edge at 0.9 of it. A rate of 16000 is copied through unchanged (nothing to convert). A rate that is not positive throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`, and so does one whose reduced ratio needs more than 2048 phases (no Windows mix format does; the session ends with the capture note, ED-292 (3)). There is no flush: the last (centre delay / L) input samples, 2.7 ms at 44.1 kHz and 2.7 ms at 48 kHz, stay in the filter at the end of a session and are not emitted.
10. Tests. 73 tests (V-T17, V-T18, V-T19, V-T20) carry `Feature` VT-2, their `Spec` id and `Decision` ED-267 (the stand-in VT-1 and VT-3 use until their entry is numbered) or ED-292 for the seam items. No microphone, model, network or timer; the signals are synthesised or read from the committed fixtures. NOT WIRED: nothing yet calls the analyser, the followers or the resampler in a running session (`VoiceSeams.Resampler` stays fail-closed until the app's composition binds `PolyphaseResampler`; the processing thread that pushes and reads at 60 Hz is VT-5, the per-frame `LevelFollowers.Step` is the orb and glow drivers, VT-4 and VT-8).

[DOWNLOADS][FIRST-RELEASE] SK-3 = DL-3 of porting/first-release/skills-ONDEMAND-PLAN.md section 7 (BUILD-PLAN.md section 2.5): the one shared downloader of the app (skills and tools; the voice models of VT-7 reuse it). ENGINEERING DECISIONS for what the plan leaves open; none is a deviation. Code: `src/Marrow.Services/Port/Downloads/`; tests: `tests/Marrow.Services.Tests/Port/Downloads/` with `Fixtures/DownloadRig.cs`, `CountingHandler.cs`, `DownloaderFailClosed.cs`, all on SK-0's fake server (`Marrow.Testing.Downloads`). The plan's sentences (3.2, 3.3, 3.9, DL-3) are SOURCE FACT of the plan.
1. THE SEAM FAILS CLOSED (ED-293 (6)). `Downloader(partFolder, policy, options?, handler?)`; with no handler it uses the ambient `DownloaderSeams.Handler`, whose production default is a `SocketsHttpHandler` (system proxy, no automatic redirect, no decompression, no cookies). `Marrow.Services.Tests` installs, from a module initializer, SK-0's `FakeDownloadTransport.CreateHandler()` with no fake server as that ambient's process default, so a test that forgets to hand its downloader a handler is refused before any connection (proved: `DownloaderSeamTests`). The `HttpClient` has no timeout of its own (R-NET-1: its timeout would read as a cancellation); every wait is the downloader's own, on `SwiftClock.Provider` or a token.
2. SHAPE. `Start(file)` and `StartSet(files)` return a `DownloadJob`: `State`, `Progress`, `BytesReceived`, `ProgressChanged`, `AttemptsStarted`, `IsWaitingToRetry`, `Pause()`, `Resume()`, `Cancel()`, and `Completion` (a task that never faults; `DownloadOutcome` = Succeeded, Failed or Cancelled, the finished files in request order, the failure). The partial file is `<part folder>\<first 8 hex digits of the pinned hash>.part` (3.1); the verified file appears at `DestinationPath` only by a move after the length and SHA-256 matched, so a failed or cancelled download never touches an older file there. The pinned hash may be written in either case; the result carries it in lower case. The first-URL policy is `DownloadPolicy` (exact host, case-insensitive, https only); `DownloadPolicy.CatalogueHosts` is 3.2's list of eight. VT-7 builds its own policy (Hugging Face) and passes `RetryDelays` of 2 s, 4 s, 8 s (voice-SPEC V-9.5 item 6).
3. TIMEOUTS (not in the plan, so engineering defaults, all options): 30 s for the response headers of one request and 60 s without a body byte (the stall timer restarts with every chunk). Both are timers on the downloader's clock; both end as "Couldn't reach {source}." (cause Timeout) with the partial file kept.
4. RETRIES. None by default: a failure is shown with Retry, which starts a new job that resumes from the partial (3.9). `RetryDelays` (default empty) retries TRANSIENT failures only (no connection, TLS, a cut stream, a timeout, a 5xx), each wait a timer on the clock, each retry a Range request from the bytes already on disk; 404, 410, other 4xx, a mismatch and a refusal are never retried.
5. REDIRECTS AND HOSTS (3.2). Followed by the downloader itself (up to `MaxRedirects` = 10, an engineering choice), only to https; the first URL must be https and on the policy's list, checked before any directory is made or any connection opened (proved with a counting handler and the fake's connection count); the redirect target need not be on the list. A redirect to plain http, to another scheme, with no Location, or the 11th hop, is refused (`Refused`). The final host is logged once the answer is accepted (`Logger` channel downloads/fetch, "downloading from {host}", host only: no path, query or header reaches a log). No credential and no cookie is ever sent.
6. PROGRESS. 3.2 says "about ten times a second", DL-3 "at least every 100 ms on a slow trickle", voice V-9.5 "at most 10 per second". Read together: a report is never sooner than `ProgressInterval` (100 ms) after the one before, the first chunk is reported at once, a chunk that comes sooner is reported by a timer on the clock at the end of the interval with the newest numbers (so no received byte waits longer than 100 ms), and one last report closes the job. Bytes a resumed partial already held count from the first report. `BytesReceived` (and `Progress`) are updated after the report for the same bytes has been decided, which is what lets a test gate on it. The reports come from whatever thread is transferring.
7. FAILURES BEYOND 3.9'S TABLE. A 5xx, or any non-success status other than 404, 410 and 416, reads as 3.9's "Couldn't reach {source}." (`ServerError`, the status in `HttpStatus`; only 5xx is transient). A local write failure is `DiskError`, "The file couldn't be written to disk." (3.9 has no row; its "install step failed" belongs to SK-4). A 416 to a resume, or a 206 that answers another range, restarts the file from zero (at most twice per chain, so nothing loops).
8. REFUSAL WORDS (not in 3.9, because a refusal is a catalogue bug or an attack, not something a user meets): "Marrow only downloads over https.", "Marrow won't download from {host}.", "Marrow gave up following redirects from {host}.", "{host} sent a redirect with nowhere to go.", "Marrow won't follow a redirect to plain http ({host}).", "{host} sent a redirect Marrow can't follow." The `DownloadCause` carries the reason for code.
9. RESUME AND VERIFY (3.2, 3.3). A partial that holds bytes is asked for with `Range: bytes=N-` every time (the server's answer says whether it can: 206 with the right Content-Range resumes, 200 starts over from zero and is reported as `RestartedFromZero`); a partial longer than the pin is deleted; one exactly as long is hashed and moved with no request (a wrong one is thrown away and the file fetched whole). The hash runs while the bytes stream to disk (a resumed partial is hashed first). The Content-Length of the answer is checked against the pin before the body is read, and a body longer than the pin stops the download; a wrong length or hash deletes the partial and fails with "The file didn't match its checksum." 3.3 says "never retrying silently more than once": the one silent retry is spent only when a RESUMED (or complete but wrong) partial ends in the wrong hash, since the cause may be the old bytes; a fresh download that mismatches fails at once, and a second mismatch after the silent restart fails.
10. DISK SPACE (3.2, 3.9). Checked once per job start, before any directory or connection: `(pinned size - bytes the partial holds + UnpackedBytes) x 1.10`, summed over a set, against `options.FreeSpace(part folder)` (a real `DriveInfo` by default, a number in tests; a probe that throws is "unknown" and does not refuse). The message writes decimal units rounded UP so the figure is enough: whole MB below 1000 MB, tenths of a GB from there ("Needs 1.1 GB free on C:."); the volume is "C:" for a drive path, `\\server\share` for UNC, "/" otherwise. Retry is a new job, so it checks again first.
11. SETS (3.2). Six files in flight (`MaxInFlight`), taken in request order. The first failure wins: the files in flight are interrupted (their partials are kept for Retry), none further starts, files already finished stay where they are and are listed in `Files`; the failure names the failing file's destination. A Retry of a set is a new `StartSet` over the files not yet in place. Progress is one number over all the files.
12. PAUSE, RESUME, CANCEL. All three stop the transfer at once and keep the partial files; a paused job holds no connection and waits (for Resume or Cancel, both token-bounded); Resume asks for the rest with Range. Cancel ends as `Cancelled`, not a failure (3.9). `DeleteStalePartials(maxAge = 7 days)` deletes `*.part` files whose last write is OLDER than the age, by the downloader's clock; calling it at app start is the App wiring's (DL-19).
13. TESTS. 96 tests carry `Feature` SK-3 and `Rule` R-TEST-10 (the rule this unit exists for), plus the project's traceability and layering tests. Time: the downloader's clock and the fake server's clock are two manual clocks, so a test moves each side on purpose (the downloader first, then the server); every real-time wait is bounded by `FakeDownloadServer.Guard`, and the only wall-clock looks are two 400 ms negative waits ("no seventh request arrives") in `DownloaderSetTests`. Mutation probes run by hand against the unit's tests (resume, verify, redirects, policy, timeouts, disk, sets: 22 changes): each was caught except three EQUIVALENT ones (the 200-answer and final-length checks and the Content-Range start check each only bring a later hash check forward, so the outcome is the same), and a probe that let 4xx statuses be retried survived until a 403/503 test was added.
14. NOT DONE HERE. DL-19's shared per-item job registry (an offer attaching to a download already running in Settings); the app-start call of `DeleteStalePartials`; the plan's checks that need the real sources (DL-20). NOT VERIFIED ON WINDOWS (built and run on Linux, .NET 10.0.112): the production `SocketsHttpHandler` and the system proxy were not exercised at all (tests use only the loopback fake), and SK-0's certificate note (11) applies to every test here.
15. WINDOWS REVIEW (2026-10-04, unit/integ-sk3-vt7, Opus; Windows 11, .NET 10). Verified on Windows: every SK-3 test, SK-0's certificate on SChannel, a move from the part folder on C: to a destination on E: (copy across volumes), a destination deeper than 260 characters (test), and the PRODUCTION transport (`DownloaderSeams.CreateProductionHandler`, now internal for this) against the loopback fake: its self-signed certificate is a TLS failure (`DownloadCause.Tls`, "Couldn't reach {source}.") through the real handler, and the handler follows no redirect, decompresses nothing, sends no cookie and uses the system proxy (tests; the proxy check is skipped if this PC's proxy would carry a loopback url anywhere). DEFECT FIXED test-first: files with the same pinned hash share one `<sha8>.part` (3.1), so a set holding byte-identical files (the same LICENSE.txt in several skills, empty `__init__.py` files) failed on Windows with "The file couldn't be written to disk." (the second writer cannot open the first one's partial). `PartFileTurns` (process-wide, keyed by the partial's full path, case-insensitive) gives one transfer at a time per partial, held per attempt (not across a pause or a retry wait): the next one resumes what the first left or, once the first moved it into place, fetches its own copy (test `Two_files_of_a_set_with_the_same_bytes_both_land`). Also proved on Windows: a destination a reader holds is `DiskError` and the verified partial is kept, so the next run moves it with no request (test). Hand mutations on Windows (no Range header; suffix host match; no 10% margin; no throttle; per-file instead of per-partial turns): each caught. Left as notes for the lead, not changed: an authenticating proxy (407) reads as "Couldn't reach" because no proxy credentials are sent (the system's default credentials would be a new decision); a Cancel that lands after the last file moved still ends as Cancelled; `DriveLabel` of a `\\?\` path names `\\?\C:`.

(c) FOLDER SWAP: Windows refuses to rename or empty a folder while any handle is open inside it, even one with delete sharing (probed); the install deleted the old folder file by file (a held file left it half-deleted) and threw. Now the old folder is set aside WHOLE by a rename, the new one renamed in, the old one deleted; a refused rename is tried again after 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 s on the installer's clock (a scanner looking at the fresh 564 MB DLL; an ENGINEERING choice), and when it still fails the old folder is back untouched and the answer is `Failed` (`DiskError`), never an exception; any IO failure of verify or unpack is `Failed` too, a cancelled SHA-512 pass is `Cancelled`, and temp or set-aside folders a scanner kept are deleted at the next install. `Remove` sets the folder aside first, so a loaded runtime is not half-deleted (false). ## ED-308

[UPDATES][BUILD][TEST] Update everything, unit UE-2 (BUILD-PLAN.md 2.4 UE-2; OD-0100 and its pick: places A and D, words U1, one at a time, Marrow last; the lead numbers this at merge). Code: src/Marrow.Core/Port/Updates/ (UpdateItems.cs, UpdateOrchestrator.cs, PublicVersionListings.cs, ProviderCliUpdateItem.cs), src/Marrow.Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.cs (UpdateCLI, UpdatableProviders, implements ICliUpdateRunner), src/Marrow.Services/Port/Updates/HttpVersionFetch.cs; tests: Core.Tests/Port/Updates (4 classes + fixtures, 33 tests) and Services.Tests/Providers/ProviderRegistryUpdateCliTests.cs (3), all [Trait("Feature","UE-2")] with Rule R-TEST-4.
1. Model. IUpdateItem (id, title, kind, installed version, latest version or null, Update with progress) is what UE-1 (Marrow over Velopack, kind Marrow, may report RestartRequired), SK-8 (kind SkillsAndTools) and UE-3 (kind DevTool) implement; ProviderCliUpdateItem is the CLI one. A row (UpdateRow) carries state Unchecked, NotInstalled, UpToDate, UpdateAvailable, ChecksWhenUpdated, Queued, Updating, Updated or Failed, the installed and latest text, progress (null = indeterminate, which a CLI's own updater always is) and a message. Row texts are the page's (UE-4); the messages here are plain reasons, not U1 words.
2. Order. Rows and runs go by kind: provider CLIs, developer tools, skills and tools, Marrow last (OD-0100; ONDEMAND 3.7 for skills before Marrow); the dev tools' place before skills is mine. One item at a time; a failed item never stops the rest and Marrow still runs last; a second run (or Check now, or Retry) while one is going is refused, not queued; a cancel puts the running and waiting rows back as they were. Update everything checks first when any row was never checked, then runs rows that are UpdateAvailable, ChecksWhenUpdated (the version cannot be known beforehand) or Failed; UpToDate and NotInstalled rows are not run. After an item the installed version is read again; changed = Updated, unchanged = UpToDate, failed = Failed with the item's message (an exception becomes the message). Retry runs one Failed row alone. RestartRequired is the Marrow item's flag (page: "Restart Marrow").
