## ED-319

Unit UE-1, Velopack self-update (OD-0062; OD-0012 I1; OD-0100's answer: the feed is the public repository Oak993/marrow-releases). Velopack stays pinned at 1.2.161. Core: `src/Marrow.Core/Port/SelfUpdate/`; App: `src/Marrow.App/Port/{VelopackSelfUpdateEngine,SelfUpdateEngine}.cs` and edits to `UpdateChecker.cs`, `AppUpdater.cs`, `UpdateInstallBoundary.cs`, `AboutUpdateViews.cs` (strings only) and `scripts/package-windows.ps1`. Nothing was published, signed, installed or restarted; no test reaches GitHub.

1. Shape. `ISelfUpdateEngine` (IsInstalled, CheckAsync, DownloadAsync with whole percent, WaitExitThenApplyAndRestart) is the seam; `VelopackSelfUpdateEngine` is the production engine over `UpdateManager` with `GithubSource(MarrowReleaseFeed.Url, no token, stable releases only)` and Velopack's own `IUpdateSource` / `IFileDownloader` seams (a test gives it an in-process fake downloader that refuses every address it was not given). The UpdateManager is made on first use. Without a locator, only the Velopack layout counts as an install (`Program.InstalledByVelopack`, ED-235), so a dev run or a test host never reaches Velopack. `FailClosedSelfUpdateEngine` is the unbound default.
2. The feed. `UpdateChecker.DefaultFeed` is now `MarrowReleaseFeed.Url` (the one named constant, `Repository = "Oak993/marrow-releases"`). An empty feed still means OD-0012 I1: no request, "No update feed is set.". A feed that names a GitHub repository is read through the engine (the shared one, or one passed in); any other non-empty feed keeps the release-list JSON reader (what a loopback feed in an older test serves). A run that is not a Velopack install says "No update feed is set." (nothing to update in place; no new string).
3. What a check yields. A newer release becomes the same `AvailableUpdate`: Version from the package, Tag `v<version>`, Notes the release's markdown notes (empty when none), Size the package size, ReleasedAt null (Velopack's asset has none). Velopack picks and fetches the package itself, so DownloadURL and PageURL are both `MarrowReleaseFeed.LatestReleasePage` (`.../releases/latest`: the offer is always the newest release, so GitHub's own address names it without guessing the tag vpk gave it). Nothing newer: `Update` is null, no error. The user-visible "GitLab" in the checker's messages and the About page (the five lines of `AboutUpdateViews` and "Couldn't reach", "answered with HTTP") become "GitHub": the product-name substitution of OD-0012 F1's pattern, now that OD-0100 makes GitHub the feed; the tests that pin those lines are amended with the decision cited.
4. Install. `AppUpdater` made with an engine (the shared one, in production) downloads through it, with Velopack's percent mapped to the pill's fraction (`SelfUpdateProgress`), then runs the existing `Stage` / `Verify` / `ReadVersion` sequence on the package, then hands off through the engine's `WaitExitThenApplyAndRestart` ("Restart Marrow": Velopack's Update.exe waits for this process, swaps the install, starts the new Marrow) with the same writability gate, relaunch marker, 25 s give-up and 350 ms quit as before (`FinishHandOff`). An `AppUpdater` made without an engine keeps the installer-script pipeline unchanged (every earlier test drives it). UNRESOLVED (needs a real install, WINDOWS-RUN-PENDING in a real run): whether Update.exe's wait for this process has a time limit if the quit is refused; the 25 s give-up resets the pill and the marker but cannot stop Update.exe.
5. `WindowsUpdateInstallBoundary` (closes UNK-0009: the Windows release asset is Velopack's full package, `MarrowCode-<version>-full.nupkg`, a zip whose root nuspec names the id and version). `Stage` returns the package where Velopack put it and does not delete it (Update.exe applies it from there; :322/:325's removal does not apply); `ReadVersion` reads the nuspec version (null for anything else, which `AppUpdater.Stage` reports as the existing "version unknown" line); `Verify` of a `.nupkg` checks the nuspec id is `MarrowCode` (Velopack has already verified the feed's checksum when the download ended; the package is not an Authenticode file and nothing is signed, ED-235), refusing with the existing "The downloaded app is not signed by Marrow. " prefix and the reason "Not a MarrowCode package"; any other file keeps the Authenticode gate. The staging folder helper and `LaunchDetachedInstaller` stay for the engine-less pipeline. Two tests that pinned the old blocker (`Stage_deletes_the_downloaded_artifact...`, `Stage_names_UNK_0009...`) are replaced, with the decision cited, by tests of the new behaviour.
6. Errors without Swift text. Velopack's and Windows' exceptions have no Swift text (`SwiftErrors.LocalizedDescription` refuses them), so per site (R-ERR-2, OD-0056, the platform's own text): a download failure reads "The update could not be downloaded. " plus the exception's own message (the :523-527 sentence); a refused updater start shows the exception's own message. A download when the feed has nothing newer is the existing NoRelease error.
7. Packaging. `scripts/package-windows.ps1` already leaves the folder `vpk upload github` takes (full and delta nupkgs, RELEASES, releases.win.json, Setup.exe) in `artifacts/releases`. New: `-ReleaseNotesFile` (markdown, passed as `--releaseNotes`, shown by the About page), the feed repository value `$feedRepoUrl` (a test holds it equal to `MarrowReleaseFeed.Url`) and a printed, never executed, `vpk upload github ... --repoUrl <feed> --releaseName "Marrow <version>" --tag v<version> --publish --token <token>` for the owner to run after his word for that publish. A test reads the script and fails on any executable `vpk upload|publish|download`, `gh release`, `git push`, a web request or `--signParams`. A delta needs the earlier release's files in the folder first (`vpk download github` would fetch them: a network call the script does not make).
8. Linux build note. `Marrow.UI` and `Marrow.App` do not build on this worker's SDK (10.0.112) without `ComposerLightRenderer`'s span fix (cloud/f-cz-2 carries it) and without `-p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` (`SettingsRise.cs` CS8604); neither is changed here.
9. WINDOWS REVIEW (2026-10-04, unit/integ-ue1, Opus; Windows 11, .NET 10; nothing installed, published or uploaded; no request left 127.0.0.1). (a) Traceability: the App checker takes Decision values ED-nnn only, so the 33 UE-1 App tests tagged Decision OD-0100 or OD-0062 failed it (and the nested record `Rig` in VelopackSelfUpdateEngineTests failed R-TEST-3); they now carry Decision ED-235 (the Velopack decision) as the stand-in until this ED is numbered, and the rig is `Fixtures/VelopackEngineRig.cs`. (b) Added `VelopackLoopbackFeedTests`: the whole chain on a loopback fake GitHub with nothing faked between Marrow and the socket: Velopack's own GithubSource and HttpClientFileDownloader (`Fixtures/LoopbackPortDownloader` puts back the port GithubSource drops: for a host other than github.com it reads <scheme>://<host>/api/v3/ without the port, and the fixture refuses any host but 127.0.0.1), the real UpdateChecker (1.8.0 offered with notes and size), the real AppUpdater (Velopack's percent reported, ending at 100), the real WindowsUpdateInstallBoundary on a real MarrowCode zip package, the relaunch marker and the quit; Restart Marrow reaches the engine's apply step, a recorder. %LOCALAPPDATA%elopackelopack.log was unchanged by every run. (c) UNK-0009 in porting/unknowns.md records what is settled (the asset and the feed) and what stays open: the repository holds no release, so the live path is unverified until the owner publishes one. (d) scripts/package-windows.ps1 was read, not run (it has no dry mode and would publish and pack the app): the only upload command is a Write-Host line; nothing that runs uploads, signs, pushes or fetches. (e) Mutations (reverted), all killed: the not-installed guard of the checker removed; the package id check of Verify removed; the Velopack-layout guard of IsInstalled removed; Velopack's percent mapped to half. (f) For the lead: the About page and checker lines say "GitHub" for "GitLab" (the product-name substitution of item 3, not an owner-worded string); NoRelease still reads "No release with a disk image was found." (the Swift text), which a Velopack download can now show.

## ED-320

[UI][GLASS][CHAT][COMPOSER][TEST] The glass material was not drawn for a control that is its parent's first child (unit glass-firstchild; the lead numbers this at merge; found by the review of unit/blitz-frames at 090e8b843 and, for the composer, by ED-241 on the unmerged unit/polish-composer-glass at 6a2692a5d; PORT-ONLY, the Swift draws the glass under every such control).
1. The defect (SOURCE FACT, measured). GlassMaterial.Attachment.Synchronize keeps one custom visual (the material) in the composition children of its owner's visual parent, directly before the owner's own visual, and inserted it only when `existing != index - 1`. A material not yet in the parent reads -1 from IndexOf, and for an owner at index 0 `index - 1` is also -1, so the test was false: for any owner that is its parent's first child (or only child) the material was never inserted and nothing was drawn. The chat chrome row's GlassEffectContainer (ChatView.cs, the first child of its parent), the composer area's GlassEffectContainer (ComposerView.cs:109-114, the only child of the padding Border) and every glass piece that is the Child of a Border or Decorator, or the first of a Panel's children, were such owners. The review's census saw it as "a material under a non-root parent drops out of the composition tree": the parent of those cases was a Border, and in the headless scene a first child under the window's root panel is the same case. That is the first of TWO defects (the review of 6677feb8a found the second, item 7): a material under a non-root parent in the middle or at the end of its parent's children was always placed at the first synchronisation (the placement tests pass there before the fix), but see item 7 for what removed it afterwards.
2. The fix for the first defect (ENGINEERING DECISION). The test is `existing < 0 || existing != index - 1`: a material that is absent is always inserted, a present one stays only when it is directly before its owner. Taken from 6a2692a5d only this condition. NOT taken from that commit, because they are other decisions refuted or still open on that branch and not what this defect needs: the translucent underlay (transparent clear instead of the flat grey), the 14 % dark veil, the hairline rim, the InternalsVisibleTo and the internal Region/State/Draw (ED-241's optical values stay UNVERIFIED and unmerged).
3. Tests, written first and seen to fail on HEAD 181aa46f6 for the right reason. GlassMaterialPlacementTests (Marrow.UI.Tests/Port, 38 tests): the owner is a piece with its own effect, a container, or a container whose child is a container; it is the first, the middle or the last of three children of a Panel; the Panel is the window's root or under a Border. For each of the 18 cases the material is in the parent's composition children directly before the owner (and for the nested case both containers), and the fine stripes (4-pixel period, 255 of contrast without glass) keep under 64 of contrast behind the piece. On HEAD exactly the 12 first-child cases failed (6 composition, 6 pixel) and the 24 middle and last cases passed; a scene without glass keeps the full contrast (so the pixel test measures the frost); a first child's material follows it when a sibling is inserted ahead and leaves with it. GlassMaterialPlacementReviewTests (taken from the review at 090e8b843, unchanged: 7 tests, 5 failed on HEAD, all pass now). ChatViewGlassPlacementReviewTests (taken from the same commit): the chrome row's one container pass is in the tree directly before the container (failed on HEAD, passes); its census test, which wrote a file and had no requirement trait, was dropped. ComposerViewGlassPlacementTests (Marrow.App.Tests/Views/Composer): the mounted ComposerArea's 8-point container is its parent's first child, its material is in the composition tree directly before it, and it has been sent regions to draw (failed on HEAD, passes). The frames unit's ancestor-watch tests (GlassMaterialTests, GlassMaterialWatchReviewTests, ChatViewFramesReviewTests) are unchanged and green.
4. One existing test changed, and why. GreyscaleTextRenderTests.A_text_on_a_glass_pill_has_no_colour_fringes (ED-281) put its glass pill first in a StackPanel, so on HEAD it drew no glass and the label sat on the neutral backdrop, and the test counted any pixel with unequal channels as a subpixel fringe. With the glass drawn the fill is the veil over the backdrop (245, 245, 247 at 18 percent: 36, 36, 37 over 40, 40, 40), one level off neutral by design. The test now measures a fringe as a channel spread of more than the fill's own spread plus two levels; a subpixel fringe (per-channel coverage) differs by tens of levels, greyscale ink is a mix of the fill and white and cannot spread more than the fill. The test still fails if the text is drawn with subpixel antialiasing; no other expectation changed.
5. What draws now that did not (by the code, each an owner that is the only or the first child of its parent; the chat row, the composer container and the stack/border cases are proven by the tests above, the rest are read from the code and not individually pixel-tested): the chat chrome row's container (one pass for the row, PR-CHAT-171), the composer area's container (ComposerView.swift:23), the follow-up queue tab's rounded shape (FollowUpQueueTab, Child of the tab), the request card (RequestCards, Child of the host), the subagent panel's shape (Child of its scrim), the usage floating panel's glass layer (first of its Grid), and a glass pill that is the first child of a stack (the greyscale test's pill). In Marrow.UI's chrome (completed after the review of 98acdd51e): ChromeGlassSurface.Body (Chrome.cs, Surface: Panel { fill, content }, the glass fill first), so every ChromeGlassCapsule, ChromeGlassFieldCapsule and ChromeGlassCircle, 28 call expressions by grep at this head: Chrome.cs itself 7 (the chrome buttons and the search field's capsule), the Settings segmented picker (ChromeSegmentedPicker), SettingsView 2, the About page's update buttons (AboutUpdateViews 3), WallpaperCard, Hydra (HydraPanel 2, HydraButton), SubagentPanel, RootView 2, Usage (UsageViews 4, UsageFloatingPanel), the Tour (TourView), the floating sidebar's title (FloatingSidebarPanel) and the prompt editor's add button (PromptEditor); SmallAccentGlassButton (Panel { fill, button }, the fill first; SettingsView, AboutUpdateViews); and the window backdrop's wallpaper overlay (Chrome.cs WindowBackdrop, GlassLayer: the only child of the overlay Panel while the wallpaper setting is below 0.98), a window-sized piece whose material now draws on every redraw of the window, since every dirty rect meets it. Its cost, measured once headless (CPU Skia; a scratch test, not committed; a 1200 x 800 window, a flat fill under a window-sized glass layer, 60 redraws of a 40 x 16 wash over it, then 20 whole redraws): a partial redraw takes 13.2 to 15.4 ms a frame with the layer and 2.1 to 2.5 ms without it (11.6 to 12.1 ms at 11a1e05be, before the kept backdrop of item 11: its copy of the window-sized backdrop costs about 2 to 3 ms); a whole redraw takes 501 to 535 ms with the layer and 2.3 to 2.4 ms without (515 to 518 ms at 11a1e05be): the shader runs on every pixel of the window on the CPU. A whole redraw comes at a first show, a resize and the repaint of 7b. UNVERIFIED: the GPU path of a real Win32 window was not measured. Sites in the middle or last (the command palette's panel after its scrim, the floating sidebar's surface after its plate) were already drawn. Not measured: whether a real Win32 composition shows the same as the headless one; two glass siblings in one parent were not tested together (each keeps its own material directly before itself).
6. THE GLASS TURNS OVER WITH THE WINDOW (ENGINEERING DECISION; OD-0076, ED-253, ED-254, SPEC 6.5). Drawn now, the Settings window's glass took the new appearance in the click frame while every other colour eases over 0.32 s: LookCardTurnoverTests failed 8 of 18 on this change (each alone twice; 18 of 18 on HEAD, where that glass, all first and only children, was never drawn). GlassMaterial now eases what it derives from the appearance on AppearanceTurn's own curve and clock (AppearanceTurn.Run: Curve 0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1 over 0.32 s, FrameClock, SwiftClock; at once under Reduce Motion, with no frame clock, in a window that has not drawn a frame, and in a tree that does not turn over). Each piece holds its veil darkness (0 light to 1 dark, was the bool Region.Dark: the veil colour (30, 30, 32) or (245, 245, 247) at 18 percent, and the colour the underlay is cleared to, are mixed by it) and its resolved tint (SwiftColor.PremultipliedMix, the mix the accent's own ease uses); a change of the appearance starts a run from what is drawn now to what the new appearance resolves, a run still going is replaced from where it stands, and each frame of it synchronises the container that draws the piece. A change of the effect's own tint (a different SwiftColor or opacity, not the appearance resolving the same one differently) is made at once. The backdrop the glass samples is the window's own pixels and eases with them. The tint of an untinted piece is Transparent in both appearances and is left alone (mixing transparent with transparent gave #00000000, a different record, so a message and a repaint in the click frame).
7. THE SECOND DEFECT: AVALONIA RE-SYNCHRONISES THE PARENT'S COMPOSITION CHILDREN AND DROPS EVERY MATERIAL IN IT (SOURCE FACT, read in Avalonia 12.1.2 by the review of 6677feb8a; ENGINEERING DECISION for the fix). CompositingRenderer.UpdateCore, for every visual dirty at a render update (a render-only change counts: a new Background, a hover, a colour ease, InvalidateVisual) runs Visual.SynchronizeCompositionChildVisuals, which compares the count of the visual's composition children with its visual children's (plus one for an ElementComposition child visual) and, when they differ, clears the composition children and adds back only the controls' own visuals. A parent that holds a material always has one more, so each such update dropped every material in the parent, and nothing put it back until the owner's next layout pass, property change or appearance change; the glass was gone for those frames. It is older than this unit and not the first-child defect: it hits the middle child as well (GlassMaterialFirstChildReviewTests, c4898af8b, failed for position 0 and 1). The point is closed to a subclass (an internal virtual of Visual), and the one extension, ElementComposition.SetElementChildVisual, adds a child after all the others, above the owner and its content, so a material cannot live there. FIX: each window's renderer is given a step after its update: GlassMaterial names the private readonly field `_update` of the renderer (TopLevel.Renderer, CompositingRenderer; the package is pinned, Directory.Packages.props) and wraps it, so that in the same composition update, before the frame is committed, every material of the window is put back directly before its owner (WindowHook.Repair, Attachment.Reinsert, the same placement as Synchronize, Place). If the members are not found the materials keep to the layout pass as before. The earlier whole-window repaint at the click (6677feb8a) is removed: it had worked only because it invalidated every parent and so wiped every material, making the click frame and the Fresh frame both glass-less.
7b. THE REPAINT AFTER THE TURNOVER (ENGINEERING DECISION, MEASURED NOT TRACED). With the easing and the hook alone, LookCardTurnoverTests Mcp and Models (2 of 18) fail: the last partial redraws of the turnover leave the antialiased edge of a vector icon (SwiftImage; the Models chevron, the Mcp server icon, near a glass piece) a few levels from a whole drawing (4 and 44 channels, past the 2 allowed; the pixel is not under any glass; it is also reproduced by a material that draws nothing, and an invisible one or one with no render bounds does not show it). Not caused by the easing, the hook or what the glass draws; the cause is how Avalonia's dirty regions combine the glass's invalidations with the icon's own (not read out of its code). So once per turnover and window, one frame after the last eased glass piece has ended, the window is redrawn whole (RepaintWhole: InvalidateVisual on every visual of the top level; counted by turnover in WindowTurns, so a turnover that a later one interrupts does not repaint, and nothing is drawn extra for a change made at once). With it 18 of 18 pass; at the click or at both ends it did nothing for the end picture; right after the end (the same frame) it did nothing either: it has to follow the last tick. Without it Mcp and Models fail, and that is the only reason it is kept. What is not known: why the partial redraw differs. After item 11 it was taken out once more: LookCardTurnoverTests 13 of 18 (About 15, Mcp 44, Models 4, Hydra 4 and SourceControl 7 channels apart), so it stays; item 11 does not touch this residue (7b reproduced it with a material that draws nothing). Item 13 corrects when it comes.
8. Tests for 6 and 7. GlassMaterialTurnoverTests (Marrow.UI.Tests/Port, 2): a flat window with a glass piece that is its parent's first child, plain and tinted, in a window marked to turn over (AppearanceTurn.SetTurnsOver, ManualFrameSource, ManualTimeProvider): the click frame is the frame before it (within 1 level), no frame takes more than 12 percent of the change at once (the curve's steepest 60 Hz step is about 5), frame 10 is between the two, and frame 24 is the end. Both failed on HEAD of this unit (the click frame had changed the glass: #6e6e6f to #959595 plain, #b77b37 to #ca8f4a tinted). The 8 LookCardTurnoverTests (ED-253, ED-254) are the other proof and are not changed.
9. Tests for the hook: GlassMaterialFirstChildReviewTests (c4898af8b, unchanged): the material stays in the tree through a render-only change of the parent for the first and the middle child, with the stripes still frosted; two glass siblings keep one material each through reorder, removal and an appearance change; no frame after an appearance change lacks the material; a reparented first child takes its material with it.
10. Verification (Windows, one-names scripts, MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR fresh, filter `&FullyQualifiedName!~Native`, no mutations by the author). Marrow.UI.Tests, all: 2702 passed, 0 failed (the 6 review tests included). Marrow.App.Tests Views.Chat + Views.Composer + Views.Sidebar + Views.Settings + Traceability: 4555 passed, 0 failed. LookCardTurnoverTests and the App glass placement tests: 20 of 20 alone.
11. A PARTIAL REDRAW DREW THE GLASS FROM THE LAST FINISHED FRAME (SOURCE FACT, measured, and read in Avalonia 12.1.2; ENGINEERING DECISION for the fix; found by the review of 98acdd51e, GlassMaterialPartialRedrawReviewTests, 11a1e05be, also failing at 181aa46f6). Draw sampled `lease.SkSurface.Snapshot()`, the whole retained surface. Avalonia redraws only the frame's dirty rect (ServerCompositionTarget.RenderRootToContextWithClip: it clips to SingleDirtyRectTracker.CombinedRect, clears it and draws every visual that meets it), so outside that rect the surface is the previous frame's finished picture: the glass's own output and what lies over it. When only a control over the glass was redrawn (a caret, a hover wash, a line of text), the blur inside the rect read up to 66 pt around it from that picture, so the veil was laid over itself and the content above leaked into the frost: 8 levels after four redraws that changed nothing, 11 at the first (0 without the effect). FIX: the material keeps the pixels it took (GlassMaterial.Backdrop: the snapshot's crop, in the surface's pixels) and on each draw takes new ones only inside the frame's dirty rect; outside it nothing under the material can have changed, since whatever changes adds its bounds to that rect (inside the clips of its ancestors: GlassMaterialKeptBackdropReviewTests, d2f00a530, pins a piece scrolled out of a clipping viewport and back, and passes). That covers what the material READS; what it DRAWS outside the rect was not redrawn, though a change inside reaches it through the blur and the refraction: see item 15. The dirty rect is read from the handler's host (`_host`, ServerCompositionVisual.Root, ServerCompositionTarget.DirtyRects, CombinedRect: private and internal members of the pinned package, Directory.Packages.props; GlassMaterial.Frame, was DirtyRect). The kept pixels are used only on the same surface (its handle and size); with no rect known (a member not found, another tracker kind: none is configured, CompositionOptions are not set) or another surface, the material takes the surface whole, as before. What it kept is given up when the material leaves its parent (a Released message) and disposed at the next render, where the GPU context is current. Tests: GlassMaterialPartialRedrawReviewTests 2 of 2 pass unchanged (8 levels with the kept pixels turned off); GlassMaterialPartialRedrawTests.A_change_under_the_glass_that_only_it_redraws_shows_through_the_glass_as_in_a_whole_drawing (a block under the glass turns from black to white: 19 levels from a whole drawing with the kept pixels turned off). CORRECTION (review of 2ea2cc674): that test measured only the pixels over the block, and so did not show that the change under the glass was drawn as a whole drawing draws it: the frost around the block, within the material's reach, kept the last frame's look (86 levels at scale 1, 90 at 1.5). It now measures the whole piece; item 15 is the fix. Not measured: a real Win32 window (its swap chain may not retain the previous frame, then every frame is drawn whole and the kept pixels are not used).
12. THE MATERIAL'S RENDER BOUNDS REACH AS FAR AS IT SAMPLES (ENGINEERING DECISION, from the review of 98acdd51e item 1). GetRenderBounds adds SampledMargin (66: the blur's 3 sigma, 36, the refraction's largest displacement, 28.6, and the antialiased edge) to the shape, so that when the material appears, moves or changes, Avalonia redraws all it reads and item 11's kept pixels are taken whole. The review found no test needing it, and that was right at 98acdd51e: a custom visual clips to its Size by default, and that clip (FinalizeSubtreeBounds intersects the subtree bounds with the own clip rect) cut the margin back to the owner's box. The material is now made with ClipToBounds = false; it draws only inside its shapes (the shader's coverage), so nothing else changes. Test: GlassMaterialPartialRedrawTests.A_piece_that_appears_beside_content_drawn_over_it_does_not_frost_that_content (a white bar drawn over the material 4 px right of a piece that appears: without SampledMargin the frost near that edge took the bar in, 62 levels from a whole drawing; with the margin but the clip left on, the same 62).
13. THE REPAINT OF 7b WHEN A TURNING PIECE LEAVES (ENGINEERING DECISION, from the review of 98acdd51e item 2). For each rect that meets a material's output grown by its reach, it adds that growth, inside the output, straight to the tracker (its AddRect, through reflection): what it adds does not pass through the events again, so it is never answered, nothing asks for another frame, and a scene that does not change draws nothing. A rect that meets several materials is grown for each, and what one adds is grown for the others (each once a rect). Each material tells the window's Reach its output and reach at each draw and leaves it on Released. ## ED-321

[SKILLS][STORE][TEST] SK-5 / DL-5 (OD-0099 amendments, OD-0103), cloud worker on codex/f-sk-5. Plan facts: ONDEMAND 3.1, 3.3-3.5, 3.7-3.8 and section 7 DL-5; skills-PLAN 2.1 and WU-4. Engineering decisions where those plans leave API or internal representation open:

1. Scope: Services store machinery, one type per file in Port/Skills/Store. SK-9 owns building/filtering/claiming per-chat generations, stable paths, spares and the measured launch budget; SK-8 owns shim switching, removal dependency policy and Reset orchestration; SK-13 owns Program's uninstall callback and UI. SK-5 exposes generation verification/leases, retirement, collection and unlock-all teardown for those callers. No ledger status changes. The missing-original gap is CLOSED: after the lead added it at staging commit 3d3068124, read skills-ORIGINALS-PLAN.md from that commit (git show), section 3.3, W0-2/W0-4 and their acceptance context. The adapted store requirements (lock, full verification after extraction/update, binary seal every launch, planted .pyc/changed .dll/extra files, GC and unlock/delete) are covered here. ONDEMAND section 8 supersedes bundled payload deletion and marrow-run; archive extraction is SK-4, shims/PATH/environment/tree-kill are SK-6, uninstall callback registration is SK-13, and actual LibreOffice timings remain DL-20. No omitted SK-5 behavior was found in the newly available original; no bundled-runtime behavior is restored.
2. The caller supplies an absolute Marrow Code data root and installed-pin descriptors. No service here resolves a real user folder or environment default. Tests require MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR and create independent child folders with spaces. The actual Windows ACL/stream seam throws on an unsupported platform; portable tests explicitly inject protection only, keeping real file IO. Native tests carry Feature=SK-5 and WINDOWS-ONLY in their source/category and skip with a visible NTFS/Windows reason on non-Windows. The Windows one*.sh wrappers are unavailable to this worker: run dotnet test directly on Linux, record skips separately, and leave native acceptance unverified.
3. A trusted, immutable per-file inventory is passed in memory. Skillset/plugin inventories must equal the embedded catalogue Files, including the licence file. Tools/package sets have archive hashes, not installed-file hashes in SK-1; SK-4 must supply the installed-tree inventory derived from hash-verified artifacts and deterministic installation, and reconstruct it from those verified artifacts after restart. Never use a manifest read from an installed writable folder as a trust root. A missing/invalid inventory or an unpinned descriptor is refused. For sets whose files have different per-skill pins (SK-1 O3), the caller supplies the installed pin key explicitly; the frozen per-skill pins are passed unchanged to the downloader. Windows-insensitive duplicate paths, unsafe relative paths and file/directory collisions are refused on every platform.
4. Full verification compares every file and directory (including hidden/system entries) to that inventory and its implied parent directories, refuses reparse points and named streams, checks read-only files and the Marrow deny entry. The launch seal enumerates the same tree and checks locks, streams, presence and sizes, but hashes only .exe/.dll/.pyd/.node (case-insensitive). AcquireForViewBuild checks the source store whole on every build (PLAN 2.1); Acquire checks the seal per launch. No LibreOffice sampling fallback is adopted without DL-20's measurement. Verification IO/platform failures return an invalid result, so no lease is issued; the SK-7 Damaged state is saved before returning.
5. Repair receives the frozen installed catalogue pin, never the current catalogue's newer pin. IStoreRepairDownloader is the narrow SK-3 boundary: fetch pinned artifact names / catalogue-relative skill files into the given scratch folder, verify bytes, and never install or execute. Archive materialization is the separate IStoreRepairInstaller boundary for SK-4; missing boundaries fail closed. A plain-file skill installer copies only the pinned file set. Repair builds tmp- folders beside the old item, locks and verifies before promotion, and waits for leases/sharing failures through pending repair + next GC, never by blocking or changing a live tree. Duplicate repairs are refused. Downloaded/prepared files are independently checked; a corrupt repair stays unusable. Internal exceptions are not new UI wording; the checksum failure uses ONDEMAND 3.9's exact message. Cancellation returns to Damaged and keeps the old pin; no silent install.
6. One service instance owns a data root during an app run (matching PLAN's in-memory lease design). Synchronous coordination serializes lease/verification/GC and promotion; downloads run outside that coordination with scratch-folder reservations. Leases dispose idempotently. condemned.json is an atomically written sorted array of absolute paths under this data root, strictly confined to managed trees, never a trust root; malformed/outside entries fail closed and remain untouched. Retired/damaged folders stay condemned across restart and are not reused. Active installed pins and reserved builds survive GC; unleased old versions, tmp builds and ended/spare/list generations are eligible. An IO/access deletion failure leaves the folder unlocked and condemned for the next immediate GC pass (no retry delays).
7. Unlock walks without following links, removes Marrow's exact deny entry throughout the tree, then clears read-only attributes, then deletion starts. Teardown unlocks all addons/store/views before any delete; enabled.json and accepted terms are retained. Held residual trees remain ordinary deletable folders and are retried at the next collection. Windows ACL changes and stream enumeration use .NET/Win32 directly, never a shell or elevation. Portable tests inject a sharing failure because POSIX open handles do not prevent unlink; separate WINDOWS-ONLY tests hold a real no-delete-sharing handle. Every locked test tree uses one fixture; teardown checks that no Marrow deny entry or fixture remains.

8. Review repairs: condemnation applies to overlapping paths, but GC preserves every descendant of a currently retained item; a condemned descendant blocks use and marks the registered parent damaged. Teardown collects unrelated unleased trees even if one live lease remains, and saves the SK-7 non-item metadata (accepted terms, declined chats and found-on-PC records) in a recreated ordinary addons/state.json. These close the added adversarial tests without changing any original expectation. Condemnation tests compare decoded JSON paths, so the same absolute-path assertion works with Windows JSON backslash escaping. Native junction and current-directory fixtures use Win32/.NET only; no real CLI is run.

9. Final failure-path checks: a lock/verification/state failure after the repair rename removes the stale pending descriptor, leaves the replacement condemned and unusable, and permits a fresh same-pin repair. Successful teardown removes condemned.json and does not recreate empty addons metadata; non-item metadata is written only when there is something to retain. Later teardown GC also retries unlocked bin/work/downloads residuals, not only versioned tools. The teardown-during-download assertion was strengthened from an empty tmp list to absence of the whole tools folder. The test sharing-failure seam also refuses ancestor deletion while a descendant handle is held, matching Windows rather than POSIX unlink.

## ED-322

2026-10-04. ENGINEERING DECISIONS for first-release SK-4 / ONDEMAND DL-4 only; owner-authorized feature work on `codex/f-sk-4`, based on `cloud/f-sk-3` and staging `3d3068124`. No ledger status changes.

1. **Authority and boundaries.** The owner's current worker instructions override the historical no-commit/no-push worker rules, the prohibition on edits under `porting/`, and the blanket no-skips rule for the explicitly WINDOWS-ONLY tests. Only this branch is pushed. SK-3 remains unchanged. SK-5 owns store lifecycle/GC/leases, SK-6 owns shims, SK-9 owns provider selection/progressive disclosure, and SK-8/SK-16 own orchestration and state persistence. SK-4 returns SK-7's immutable Installed record only after successful verification; it never writes state.json itself.
2. **Explicit installer input.** SK-1's present schema has artifact/file pins but no installer-parameter record, npm integrity field, dependency tree or extracted per-file manifest. `InstallPlan` supplies those internal parameters explicitly, without guessing them from ids. Its item and Checking record must name the same pin; unpinned items are refused. Inputs are local SK-3 outputs, keyed by catalogue artifact name or file path, and rehashed before use. Supplemental wheels/tarballs must also match a catalogue artifact and its local-file mapping. `WithDownloads` refuses unsuccessful/incomplete downloader outcomes. Licences require an explicit catalogue file path, length and SHA-256, and stay byte-identical at that path beside each installed item. No licence name, content or missing-file substitute is invented.
3. **Crash-safe publication.** ONDEMAND 3.4 says both "rename, lock, verify" and "a crash at any point leaves only a tmp folder." An immediate final-name rename cannot satisfy the latter under abrupt termination during lock. Therefore build in `tmp-<random>`, rename provisionally to `tmp-<random>-ready`, lock, whole-tree verify, then atomically publish the final name. Before publication an abruptly stopped process leaves only tmp names. A completed final rename exposes an already verified item, never an incomplete one. Injected faults at every step, including after publication, quarantine owned folders back to tmp names before unlock. Existing installed folders are never overwritten/deleted. Spares use the same transaction; rollback covers every owned view and store folder. Publication of several independent folders is not a multi-folder filesystem transaction: an abrupt stop between publications can retain completed, independently verified spares. Uncommitted store work still has a tmp name; recovery/GC is SK-5's scope.
4. **Trust and verification handoff.** Skillset verification uses the catalogue's exact file set (including licence), not a snapshot that could bless planted files. Extracted tool files derive a manifest from checked archives or an explicitly bound checked extractor's output; SK-1 does not currently pin extracted trees. File size/hash, missing/extra files, extra directories, reparse points, Windows named streams and missing locks are refused. Returned manifests include expected directories so SK-5 can verify legitimate archive-created empty directories. Directory names and file paths obey Windows confinement on Linux too: no rooted/drive/UNC path, dot traversal, ADS syntax, reserved device name, trailing dot/space, archive link or case-colliding file. Files are copies, never links. Hashing uses streams. This is the post-install verification handoff, not SK-5's future per-launch seal or repair implementation.
5. **Process and lock bindings.** Both seams fail closed when unbound; no CLI, PATH search or shell is an implicit fallback. The opt-in Windows runner accepts only explicit absolute executables pinned by path, size and SHA-256, uses ArgumentList, hides the window, and kills the child tree on cancellation. Windows lock binding applies the exact current-user inheritable deny `(OI)(CI)(WD,AD,WEA,WA,DE,DC)` plus read-only files; unlock removes only that exact explicit rule and then clears file read-only attributes. Linux tests use visibly named fakes, never a Linux approximation reported as a Windows ACL pass.
6. **Extractor outcomes.** `msiexec /a <artifact> /qn TARGETDIR=<tmp>` is one argument per element. Accept 0 and Windows Installer's 3010 (completed, reboot required); refuse all others, including 1641 (reboot initiated, contrary to a quiet administrative-image build), retaining the numeric exit code. The plan gives no user-facing exit-code wording, so none is added. SFX executes the pinned artifact itself with `-o<tmp>` and `-y`; only 0 succeeds. Both must yield payload files. Whether LibreOffice's real administrative extraction needs elevation, its interactive-installer fallback and real image performance remain DL-20/live integration checks; no silent normal installation or elevation is introduced.
7. **Python and Node.** Python requires a pinned pip wheel. The explicit pth filename and stdlib zip avoid an invented version default; write UTF-8 without BOM with LF and final newline: stdlib zip, `.`, `Lib\site-packages`, absolute `addons\work\python-agent\<version>`, `import site`. Pip wheel contents go into `Lib\site-packages`. Pyset stages only checked local .whl files in a tmp directory, writes exact pinned `name==version --hash=sha256:<digest>` requirements, runs only the plan's offline `--no-index --find-links --require-hashes --no-deps --target -r` argv and unchecked-hash compileall, then seals. Its local requirement/wheel staging stays tmp-prefixed for lifecycle cleanup by SK-5. Nodeset checks both catalogue SHA-256 and explicit SHA-512 integrity and copies regular tar entries from `package/` into explicit lock-tree node_modules paths without npm or any script execution. No package resolver or network fallback is invented.
8. **Spare/layout ownership.** Skill stores are `skills\store\<explicit source>@<pin8>` with catalogue paths preserved below them. Caller-supplied SK-9 projections provide every required provider, content key, selected file set, optional layout prefix and generated metadata; SK-4 copies, locks and verifies each projection and returns its spare path. Claude/Grok plugin prefix/metadata can thus be supplied without putting provider filtering or plugin policy into the installer. Unknown projection files are refused and every copied file remains bound to its catalogue pin. Browser zips support explicit multi-archive prefix projections; Playwright marker filenames and whether that runtime accepts the layout are still ONDEMAND 3.4's DL-20 uncertainty, not invented here.
9. **Evidence limits.** Tests are offline Marrow-made fixtures. Five Windows-only tests explicitly skip on Linux with a reason: NTFS junction/archive reparse refusal, tiny test-built PE execution after Python extraction (never Python), fake msiexec executable outcomes (never system msiexec), real ACL lock/unlock, and ADS refusal. Fake process/argv and all portable logic run on Linux. Windows execution remains unverified until those tests run on Windows; neither Linux skips nor fake processes are a Windows acceptance claim.

## ED-323

[SKILLS][INSTALL][STORE][TEST] Windows verification and adversarial review of SK-4 (DL-4) and SK-5 (DL-5) on `unit/integ-sk4-sk5`, 2026-10-04. Every WINDOWS-ONLY test both units declared ran here on Windows 11 (standard user, no Developer Mode) and passed; the items below are the defects found and the decisions taken to fix them.
1. **msiexec property quoting.** SOURCE FACT (Windows Installer documentation, "Setting Public Property Values on the Command Line"): a property value with spaces is written `PROPERTY="value"`. Read from the running test-built stand-in, `ArgumentList` handed msiexec `"TARGETDIR=C:\...\Marrow Code\..."` (whole-argument quoting), and the production data root `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Marrow Code` always contains a space. ENGINEERING DECISION: `InstallCommand.QuotePropertyValues` (set only by msi-admin) makes `WindowsInstallProcess` write `NAME="value"` for a public-property argument and MSVC quoting for every other argument; a value containing `"` or ending in `\` is refused rather than quoted ambiguously. Whether real `msiexec /a` runs without elevation stays DL-20.
2. **Pyset staging.** ED-322 (7) left the `addons\downloads\tmp-<random>` wheel staging "for lifecycle cleanup by SK-5", but SK-5's GC sweeps only `addons\tools`, `skills\store` and `skills\views` (SK-3's resumable partials must not be swept). ENGINEERING DECISION: the pyset installer removes its own staging after pip and compileall, on success and on failure; a held file or an abrupt stop leaves only that tmp- folder.
3. **Empty folders across the handoff.** ED-322 (4) returns `InstallResult.Directories` so archive-created empty folders verify, but `StoreManifest` derived folders only from file paths, so such a folder (PortableGit ships empty ones) was an extra folder and the item would be damaged on every launch. ENGINEERING DECISION: `StoreManifest(files, directories)` adds the listed folders and their parents, with the same path rules; a folder that is also a file is refused; any unlisted empty folder is still damage (PLAN WU-4).
4. **Link fixtures.** Symbolic links need SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege, so four SK-5 tests failed on a standard Windows account before reaching the code. The SK-5 fixtures fall back to the same reparse point made without privilege (an NTFS junction for a directory, a third-party reparse tag for a file); the code under test inspects only the reparse attribute. The fixture teardown unlinks planted links before its recursive delete, which .NET refuses on a junction for a standard user.
5. **Not fixed here (cross-unit, recorded for SK-8/SK-9/SK-16).** (a) `SkillsStore.Collect` deletes every unleased folder under `skills\views`, including the ready spares SK-4 just built, and every `tmp-` folder under `addons\tools` and `skills\store`, including one an SK-4 install is building at that moment; the store has no reservation API for an outside build or a spare pool. (b) Repair of an archive tool needs an `IStoreRepairInstaller` adapter over `ItemInstaller`; none exists, and `ItemInstaller` publishes to a final name the damaged folder still occupies, so the adapter needs a build-into-prepared-folder mode and the installer parameters (`InstallPlan`) that only the orchestrator holds. Repair of plain-file skill sets works now (`PinnedSkillRepairInstaller`).

No ledger statuses are changed. SK-5 production code and its tests remain untouched.

1. **Plugin activation.** Adopt BUILD-PLAN's proposal: downloaded plugin hooks and MCP servers

   activation is source-qualified (`itemId/pluginRoot`). A deliberate item-level activation
   can select the set, with folder switches overriding it. `PluginFolders` returns additional
   absolute roots; SK-11 must pass each separately with its documented plugin-loading flag.
   Vendor plugin manifests and every copied vendor byte remain unmodified. Live compatibility
   of each vendor plugin format is SK-11/DL-20's check, not established by folder tests.
2. **Reviewed metadata, defaults and budgets.** SK-1's current catalogue schema does not yet
   hold descriptions, group membership, priorities, external-access defaults or provider
   budget measurements. Services accepts explicit reviewed `GenerationSkill` metadata tied
   to the installed pin's catalogue names/paths. Name and description must also match its
   hash-verified frontmatter. Group membership, priority and whether a key/login/internet is
   required are mandatory inputs, never inferred from names or from a missing dependency.
   Q-SKILLS-1 A's six groups are on unless external access is required; A3/A4/O5 are off.
   Missing runtime tools do not disable an otherwise enabled skill. The caller supplies
   measured character budgets for all offered models; `ForModels` selects the minimum.
   Unknown/zero budgets and absent reliable clash snapshots fail closed. SK-2/SK-13 supplies
   the reviewed metadata; SK-11/DL-20 supplies live budget measurements and resolved config
   paths. No provider context size or YAML metadata is invented.
3. **Persistent switches and identity.** `enabled.json` contains a release version and two
   source-qualified switch maps, for skills and plugin folders; new skills use their reviewed
   defaults, removed entries are dropped by reconciliation, existing switches carry over.
   Plugins default off. Equal names from different vendors do not share a switch. PLAN 1.4
   chooses Anthropic's skill-creator for Claude/Grok, OpenAI's for other providers, and neither
   for Codex. Remaining same-name vendor candidates are selected deterministically by
   default-on rank, manifest priority, then source-qualified id. Content keys hash the release,
   selected source/skill ids and installed pins, and activated plugin-folder ids and pins.
   They do not include chat, project or selected model. `generation.json` is generated internal
   inventory metadata, not a disk trust root; it permits an empty generation to be verified
   by SK-5 without loosening StoreManifest's nonempty-inventory invariant. `chat-paths.json`
   records moved chat folder names; strict provider/chat/nonce validation keeps it from
   becoming authority to access or delete outside the managed views.
4. **Atomic publication with the frozen SK-5 API.** Before publishing, acquire a SK-5 lease on
   a locked, trusted one-file bootstrap at the final pathname, and another at `tmp-<nonce>`.
   Populate tmp while its lease prevents GC; remove only the owned final bootstrap while its
   pathname lease remains held; atomically rename the complete tmp to that pathname, lock,
   then whole-tree verify before returning the final lease. Thus direct SkillsStore.Collect
   also cannot remove the target in the rename-to-acquire window. Initial bootstrap creation
   races fail closed; a bootstrap is never handed to a session. Sources are whole-tree
   verified and leased during composition, and copied bytes are rehashed before use. A live
   generation stays frozen until disposal; current switches apply to new/resumed chats.
   Spares are leased, claimed by rename, repaired when damaged, replenished in background
   work outside the coordinator gate (below-normal priority on Windows), and bounded to the
   global key and keys of the five recent chats, plus the current composer preparation.
   Dispose waits for pending copies outside the gate. Read-only listing probes share one
   leased generation with reference counting; sessions get their own paths. Generation
   invocation checks the whole tree and the returned file bytes again. SK-5 handles removal
   and unlock ordering; platform protection defaults to real Windows protection and refuses
   operation on Linux unless an explicit test double is injected.
5. **Unmodified explicit-only skills.** ONDEMAND 1 supersedes the earlier vendor patches in
   PLAN 1.2. Native/Marrow-side invocation can keep explicit-only text out of its catalogue.
   A file-loading provider may receive an explicit-only skill only if its pinned frontmatter
   already says `disable-model-invocation: true`; otherwise the skill is omitted and reported
   in `LeftOut`. No patch is synthesized and no implicit invocation is silently enabled.
   Grok, Command Code, Copilot and OpenCode still receive no explicit-only skill until the
   plan's live checks authorize them. Codex's own review-agent is not republished.
6. **Read-only scans and closed seams.** Every scan gets explicit home/project/repository
   roots; there is no ambient home lookup, network, process or auth-file access. Native own
   skills are not even enumerated until Q17's switch is on. Provider config resolution and
   registered/plugin/runtime folders not documented enough to discover safely are supplied
   as resolved extra roots/reported entries by SK-11. Grok's documented paths arrays are read
   directly, with comments handled. Unsupported TOML/YAML, substitutions and reparse points
   refuse the scan rather than masquerading as no clash. Repeated folder/report entries are
   conservatively counted in the budget: without source/path identity, collapsing same-name
   user skills could undercount distinct copies. The user's description is never shortened.
7. **Test evidence and scope.** All fixtures are Marrow-authored; no vendor text, CLI or user
   data is used. Native ACL/junction/held-handle tests are WINDOWS-ONLY with explicit Linux
   skip reasons and the shared SK-5 unlock teardown. The initial budget fixture was corrected
   from 1700 to 1720 *before a behavioral implementation failure*: its 1507-character user
   entry plus 10% margin left 23 characters at 1700, too little for either 25-character entry;
   1720 leaves 41 and tests exactly one kept/one dropped. No assertion was weakened. Per-method
   Feature/Rule traits were made explicit and xUnit's required collection assertion form was
   used. Provider launch wiring, Settings integration, actual install-event registry refresh,
   and the Windows 150 ms / first-read timings belong to the following units/live run and are
   not claimed by this cloud component's offline tests. In particular SK-5 freezes its installed
   descriptor inventory at construction; SK-13 must refresh that inventory under its single-owner
   lifecycle when an installation adds a new id. SK-9 never treats an unregistered id as installed.
8. **Launch diagnostics.** PLAN 2.1's spare-miss log is `skills/generation-launches.jsonl`,
   containing provider, chat id, content key and an internal reason enum (existing chat, ready
   spare, missing spare or damaged spare). It contains no skill bodies or user files. Persistence
   failure refuses launch and disposes the unreturned lease. Item-level plugin activation
   clears previous folder overrides; a subsequent folder switch can override that activation.
   The user budget reserves 10% of the whole provider budget, a conservative reading of 2.7.

## ED-325

ENGINEERING DECISIONS, 2026-10-04. Scope: SK-8 / DL-8 only; ONDEMAND-PLAN 3.7/3.8 and section 7 DL-8, skills-PLAN 2.1, OD-0099 amendments and OD-0100. No ledger status changes.

- **One publication point:** prepare immutable per-id/per-pin routing under `addons/routes/<SHA256(id + LF + pin)>.json`, then select all targets with SK-7's atomic `addons/state.json` installed-pin write. The existing static SK-6 sidecar gains optional internal `RoutingStateFile`/`RoutingName`; its BCL-only reader is compiled into the existing NativeAOT launcher. Each invocation reads state once. Future generation builders read the same snapshot. `PipelineShimFiles.Write` binds the fixed wrappers at installation/composition time. No vendor latest request, product string or default is added. Unselected routing may be replaced on retry; selected routing is immutable. No post-commit observer exception rolls back a committed version.
- **Own the whole root:** SK-5's `SkillsStore` fixes its item registry at construction and cannot register replacements. Rather than change SK-4/SK-5, `SkillsPipeline` is the single root owner and reuses SK-5's lease type, tree unlock order, protection and deletion primitives. Do not run a second `SkillsStore` GC on the same root. Generation leases carry the exact selected source pins and hold source-version leases; sources are checked whole before view builds. GC skips builds in flight, removes individual provider children, retains live versions, and retries handle failures. SK-9/SK-19 must bind this owner; their provider/app composition is outside SK-8.
- **Restart trust:** the caller supplies frozen trusted installed descriptors (including old pins). Routing files select paths; they never supply trusted hashes. The pipeline cross-checks selected routes against those descriptors before GC. SK-4 exposes trusted empty-directory inventories, whereas SK-5's `StoreManifest` derives directories from file parents. SK-8's `PipelineVerifier` extends the same whole-tree rule with explicitly supplied trusted directories; restart callers must supply those too. Neither hashes nor empty-directory expectations are inferred from disk.
- **Multi-pin sets:** SK-7's composed `folder=pin;...` key remains the installed/latest pin. For SK-4's single safe path component only, hash that composed key to SHA-256. The original catalogue files and their hashes remain authoritative; no upstream pin is invented.
- **Rollback/recovery:** leave the persisted usable old record selected throughout download/install/route preparation. Only verified installation commits. Exceptions and cancellation remove prospective folders with SK-5's unlock order; abrupt exits leave unselected tmp/completed folders for GC. UE-2 reports failed updates and Retry without hiding the still-usable old version behind an unusable in-flight record. No new user-visible error wording is added. Downloads and installer parameters are explicit seams; missing seams fail closed.
- **Removal/reset:** remove the item and transitive package-set dependents from one atomic selected snapshot; keep skill/plugin sets installed with missing needs. A running lease keeps its folder until later GC. Reset keeps enabled.json and all accepted terms (also SK-7's declined/found metadata); a confined `skills/reset-pending` marker lets later GC/restart retry all addons residue except the retained state file. Unlock every reset target before deleting any. The marker is removed after residue and leases are gone.
- **Verification boundaries:** injected IOException tests prove caught rollback; a separate Marrow-made subprocess uses Environment.Exit at all six installer steps, four precommit pipeline steps and immediately after commit to prove recovery without catch/finally. No real CLI, user folder, vendor fixture or non-loopback network is used. Windows ACL/delete-sharing checks are explicitly WINDOWS-ONLY and skip elsewhere. The native AOT launcher's routed JSON reader is source-generated.

## ED-326

[SKILLS][INSTALL][STORE][GENERATIONS][TEST] Windows verification and adversarial review of SK-8 (DL-8, `origin/codex/f-sk-8` 751f0a2da) and SK-9 (DL-9, `origin/codex/f-sk-9` 06e2ebb83) on `unit/integ-sk8-sk9`, built on `unit/integ-sk4-sk5` 4c9d408a2, 2026-10-04. Every WINDOWS-ONLY test both units declared ran here on Windows 11 (standard user, no Developer Mode) and passed. The two cross-unit gaps ED-323 (5) recorded are closed below.
1. **Two owners on one root (defect).** SK-8's `SkillsPipeline` owns the whole root and its GC ("do not run a separate SkillsStore owner on this root"), while SK-9's `SkillGenerations` took a concrete `SkillsStore`. With both on one root each GC deletes the other's trees: the pipeline's GC deletes every chat generation SK-9 leased in the store, and the store's GC deletes every pin the pipeline installs (its inventory is frozen at construction). ENGINEERING DECISION: `IGenerationStore` (AcquireForViewBuild, AcquireGeneration(folder, manifest), Retire, Collect) is what SK-9 needs; `SkillsStore` and `SkillsPipeline` both implement it, SK-9 takes the interface. The pipeline's generation lease holds no source lease (a generation is a copy); its `Retire` refuses a selected pin's spare, marks the folder retired (never handed out again) and deletes it at once when unleased, else at a later GC. Tests bind SK-9 to the pipeline: an update during a chat keeps the chat's frozen generation (its old source pin is collected), the resumed chat gets the new pin at the same `chat-<id>` path; removal during a chat keeps that chat and new chats no longer list the set; the pipeline's GC keeps live generations and SK-4's route spares and deletes an ended chat.
2. **Gap (5)(a), GC versus builds in flight and fresh spares.** ENGINEERING DECISION: `SkillsStore.Reserve(folder)` is a reference-counted GC exclusion (equal, descendant or ancestor paths), not a use lease (AcquireGeneration is unaffected). `ItemInstaller` takes an optional `reserve` seam: every transaction reserves each name before it occupies it (`tmp-<guid>`, `tmp-<guid>-ready`, the final name, the rollback name); on success the intermediate reservations end and the published folder's and every spare's reservation is handed to the owner as `InstallResult.Reservation`, which it disposes once it registered or claimed them; on failure all reservations end, so the tmp- residue is ordinary GC work. Real-NTFS tests (WindowsInstallLock, WindowsStoreProtection): a store GC at every install step leaves the build and its spare intact and, after the reservation ends, the unregistered trees are collected; a failed build's residue is collected. The pipeline itself needs no reservation: its GC never runs while an operation (install) is in flight.
3. **Gap (5)(b), archive Repair.** ENGINEERING DECISION: `SkillsPipeline.RepairAsync(id, progress)` (the pipeline holds the orchestrator's download seam, which is where SK-4's installer parameters, `InstallPlan`, come from): refuse unless Damaged; return false, changing nothing, while a lease holds the damaged folder or a handle blocks its rename; rename it aside to `tmp-<guid>` (a locked folder renames: its parent grants delete-child, PLAN 2.1 r3, confirmed here on NTFS) and collect; download the INSTALLED pin's item from the trusted descriptor (never latest); install it with SK-4's installer at its own path; verify against the trusted descriptor and its trusted directories; commit Installed (then `UpdateCheck`, so a newer catalogue pin shows Update available again). Nothing transitional is persisted, so a failure or an abrupt exit leaves the item Damaged (its damaged tree, like any damaged tree, is GC work) or, after the commit, Installed; Repair runs again. A new `PipelineStep.SetAside` checkpoint. Spares SK-4 rebuilds for a repaired skill set are deleted (the pin's routing is immutable and keeps its own). Tests: zip and msi-admin (fake msiexec writing the image into TARGETDIR; LibreOffice's case) repairs; injected failure at SetAside/Downloaded/Installed/BeforeCommit and at every installer step, then retry/restart; a leased damaged folder defers; a held handle defers on NTFS; abrupt `Environment.Exit` in the Marrow-made worker at all 11 Repair steps on real ACLs, then a restarted pipeline finishes with one folder left. `SkillsStore.RepairAsync` keeps refusing archive kinds.
4. **Test fixes (no expectation changed).** (a) SK-9's 41 tests carried `Rule` traits such as `DL-9-enabled-json`, which the Traceability check refuses (`R-[A-Z]+-[0-9]+`); they now name R-TEST-4 with the plan rule kept as a trailing comment. (b) SK-8's `Tampered_routing_cannot_make_GC_delete_the_trusted_active_tree` replaced the raw path in the route JSON, which escapes every backslash on Windows, so nothing was tampered and the test failed; it now replaces the JSON-encoded path and asserts the file changed. (c) `InstallRig.Zip` writes a fixed entry time, so a fixture archive and its pinned digest are the same in a worker process and in the test that reattaches to its root. The PipelineRig gained Repair, msi, two-item and frontmatter options.
5. **DL-8/DL-9 review additions.** UE-2's group with two items: each row its own progress and result, one at a time, a failed item keeps its usable old pin and Retry updates it. PLAN 2.7's "never more than half of the budget" had no test (a hand mutation dropping it survived); `GenerationBudgetTests` pins it with the 10% margin. Hand mutations (each reverted byte-exact, then the tree rebuilt): SK-8: removal keeps package sets (killed), deletion ignores leases (killed), Repair downloads the latest pin (killed); a GC-only lease mutation was equivalent (TryDelete checks leases again). SK-9: no equivalence groups (killed), no half cap (survived, then killed by the new test), resume reuses a stale chat folder (killed). Gap fixes: Collect ignores reservations (killed), the installer drops the published folder's reservation (killed).
6. **UNRESOLVED / not done here.** (a) The app does not construct either owner yet (SK-13): it must make one `SkillsPipeline` per root and bind `SkillGenerations` to it; first installs are not in SK-8's pipeline. (b) SK-9 does not claim SK-4's install-time spares (it builds its own); the route keeps them. (c) PLAN 2.1's 150 ms ready-spare launch budget was not measured (DL-20). (d) A Reset whose residue is held keeps `skills\reset-pending`; until it clears, a GC with nothing installed deletes all of `addons\` except `state.json`, which would include a later first download's `.part` (SK-3) if one were in flight; not changed here. (e) Explicit-only skills cost no budget for every provider that receives them, though 2.7 states that only for Claude and Codex (Pi's listing behaviour is WU-11's live check).

## ED-327

[UI][SHADOW][SIDEBAR][TEST] Unit rec-shadow (branch `unit/rec-shadow` from `claude/verify-terminal-20261001` 066508ffb), 2026-10-05. Records UI-SIDEBAR-060 and UI-SIDEBAR-017; the lead's E rulings (`work/scratch/lead/E_rulings.md`), finding B and the two records' sections. The lead numbers this at merge.
1. **SwiftUI's `.shadow(radius: r)` is a Gaussian of standard deviation r** (SOURCE FACT by the video: the lead's least-squares fit on the radius-28 panel scrim of `2-chat-use.mov`, 118.0 s against 126.5 s, gives sigma 24-28; the "radius = 2 sigma" reading fits 6x and 25x worse; the CALayer shadowRadius convention agrees). The port draws sigma = r for every Swift `.shadow(radius:)`.
2. **Avalonia's blur value to sigma, measured.** Avalonia.Skia 12.1.2 (`DrawingContextImpl`, read with ilspycmd): `BoxShadowFilter.Create` blurs a box shadow with `SKImageFilter.CreateBlur(SkBlurRadiusToSigma(shadow.Blur))`, and `CreateEffect` uses the same function for `BlurEffect.Radius` and `DropShadowEffect.BlurRadius`; `SkBlurRadiusToSigma(b) = 0.288675 b + 0.5` (0 for b <= 0), in the drawing units of the pushed transform (DIPs). So the blur for sigma r is `(r - 0.5) / 0.288675`: r 1.5 -> 3.464, r 10 -> 32.908, r 28 -> 95.266. Not CSS's `b / 2`. Measured two ways:
   - Headless (Skia's CPU raster): the raster blur is the W3C three-box approximation (box d = floor(sigma * 3 sqrt(2 pi) / 4 + 0.5); d, d, d for odd d, and d, d, d + 1 for even d). Fitting Phi to a rendered straight edge, b = 3.5, 5, 10, 20, 32.9, 60, 95.3, 150 draw 1.431, 2.176, 3.209, 6.310, 9.710, 17.593, 27.198, 42.263 px, each the simulated three-box draw of the nominal sigma (`GaussianEdge.RasterSigma`) to 0.001 px; BoxShadow and DropShadowEffect are identical; under a 2x transform the device sigma doubles. The raster draws 0.94-0.97 of a nominal sigma, in window steps of about 0.5 px (r 1.5, 10, 28 -> 1.431, 9.710, 27.198 px: within 5 % of r).
   - Native, one real window under native.lock (OAK-BLACK, display scale 1, Avalonia's default Win32 GPU path; the composed screen read with BitBlt/CAPTUREBLT): r 28 drew sigma 28.062 DIP, r 10 drew 10.035 DIP. ENGINEERING DECISION: the helper targets the nominal sigma and does not compensate the raster's under-blur, since the real windows draw the nominal sigma exactly and a compensation would over-blur the screen.
3. **The helper**, `src/Marrow.UI/Port/SwiftShadow.cs` (namespace `Marrow.UI.Port`, beside SwiftShapes): `const double Slope = 0.288675, Floor = 0.5`; `double Blur(double radius)` (0 at or below 0.5: an unblurred shadow); `BoxShadow BoxShadow(Color color, double radius, double x = 0, double y = 0)`; `BoxShadows BoxShadows(Color color, double radius, double x = 0, double y = 0)`; `DropShadowEffect DropShadowEffect(Color color, double opacity, double radius, double x = 0, double y = 0)` for a view whose drawn content casts the shadow. Colours and offsets are passed as the Swift states them.

## ED-329

Unit rec-sidebar (records PR-SIDEBAR-091, UI-SIDEBAR-001, -008, -020, -022, -024, -028, -029, -030, -031, -032, -036, -044). The lead numbers these at merge.

1. UI-SIDEBAR-008, the title room of SidebarRow (Chrome.cs TitleLine). ENGINEERING DECISION (the lead's reading, SwiftUI HStack documented behaviour; not measurable without a Mac): `HStack(spacing: 8) { icon; Text; Spacer(minLength: 4) }` (Chrome.swift:711-720) puts its spacing between every adjacent pair of subviews, the Spacer included. The title therefore has the row's inner width less the icon (20), the icon gap (8), the gap before the Spacer (8) and the Spacer's minimum (4). TitleLine reserved 8 + 4 before and now reserves 8 + 8 + 4. A long title ends 8 pt further left than before (a SidebarRow is shared: the Settings sidebar follows). SidebarViewTests.A_project_row_keeps_the_recorded_geometry... asserts the exact edge (the largest whole-character fit, less than one glyph short of row width - 8 - 40 - 8 - 4) on a row made 17 glyphs + 92 wide, where the old room let a 17th character in and the new does not (red before the change: title ended at 257, past 253).

2. UI-SIDEBAR-020, the settle check's glyph colour (SettleCheck, SidebarView.cs). The foreground change of :2128 happens inside the hover's `withAnimation(Chrome.hover)` (:2135-2137), so an unchanged symbol keeps its glyph and its colour eases (AnimatedColor) from the old colour to the new on the transaction the change is written in; Reduce Motion (the view's environment or the platform setting, as AnimatedScalar reads it) takes it at once. A changed symbol is still a new glyph crossfaded by SymbolReplace, each glyph in its own colour. The settle bounce is CLOSED by OD-0105 (owner, 2026-10-05: the Swift source is proof enough): SidebarSettleBounceTests asserts the exact transactions of the settle path, `isSettling = true` inside `.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.45)` (SidebarView.swift:1909) and then `model.settle` inside Chrome.panelSlide (:1910), also from a real click on the open row's check. The older reflection-based test stays as the proof that the open row's check is kept and pops.

3. UI-SIDEBAR-036, the glide of surviving head glyphs (HeadCardsRow.Rebuild). SOURCE FACT (SidebarView.swift:1466-1467): a glyph's identity is its row's id (`\.first?.id`) and its own, so a glyph that moves to another row has another identity and leaves and joins (UI-SIDEBAR-038's fade, already built) rather than gliding; a glyph that keeps its row and head id, a row that keeps its first head, and the chevron that keeps its symbol keep their identity and move on the animation in force (:1535 snappy for a change of cardRows, :1541 panelSlide for a change of the head ids, otherwise the change's transaction; none for the first build). ENGINEERING DECISION: a card-level shift (FLIP), not a change to the shared ForEach foundation: each survivor is put back at the place it was drawn (the old slot, plus what was left of an earlier glide) and its shift eases to nothing. The slots are the card's own arithmetic (x = padding + column * (14 + rowGap), y = padding + row * (14 + 6)), so no layout pass is waited for; layout rounds to whole pixels, so frame 0 sits within half a pixel of the old place. The lead's wording "a glyph that crosses rows travels on snappy" is not what the source says (see above); the test for a vertical move is a surviving whole row moving up on snappy when the row above it goes.

4. UI-SIDEBAR-031 and -032, native test of the archive question popover (GlassWindowNativeTests). The test opens the question from a real thread row as the shortcut does (AppModel.AppModelArchiveRequest) in a real popup window and reads screen pixels. The glass material draws a rim light and an inner shade at the edge of its shape and tints the prominent one, so the ring just inside each capsule differs from the flat card where the material is drawn; the band just outside the focused Archive button must be the card (no focus ring). The material is composed some time after IsOpen turns true, so the test READS UNTIL both buttons show it (up to 5 s) instead of one read after a fixed sleep (which failed in 4 of 26 runs when the material was not drawn yet), and writes the time it took ("TIME TO MATERIAL", in the child's runner.stdout.log). MEASURED, 17 runs on a machine other agents were also using: 295 to 408 ms in 14 of them (295, 297, 334, 362, 375, 376, 392, 396, 406, 408 among them), 457, 597 and 1847 ms in three busier ones; the quiet figure is about 300 to 400 ms, at or over the 300 ms line in all but two. That is a PRODUCT QUESTION, not hidden by the wait: glass that arrives 0.4 s or more after the popover is up breaks the owner's no-pop-in bar; it is reported for the glass owner (is it the popover's appear animation, or the material waiting for its first composition update?). The rig's full-screen backdrop is a topmost window and on some runs stood over the popup, so the pixels read were the backdrop's (card 167,170,171): the test now takes the backdrop to the bottom (SetWindowPos HWND_BOTTOM), and fails with NATIVE_PRECONDITION, naming both windows, if the popup is not the window on top at the Delete button.

5. UI-SIDEBAR-044, native test of the folder chooser (OpenPanelNativeTests). WindowsOpenPanelRunner.Options(current, panel) holds the option set that RunModal hands to SetOptions; behaviour is unchanged. What the test calls is that PURE function with `default` as the dialog's own options: it does not read what the live dialog received (IFileDialog::GetOptions after SetOptions is not hooked), so by itself it proves the mapping from the panel's properties, not what the dialog got. The live dialog is proven by its behaviour instead: the title and OK label on the real window and two folders typed into the name box coming back (multi-select works); mutants on the title, the label and the multi-select flag turn the test red. The test shows the real dialog on an STA thread and drives it with window messages sent to that thread's own windows only: the title is the message, the OK button (IDOK) is the prompt, two quoted folders typed into the name box come back as two URLs, and IDCANCEL returns null (the sidebar adds nothing).
