While Listening or Processing a handler on the window's top level (tunnelling) cancels the session and consumes Esc whatever has the keyboard in that window; otherwise Esc keeps its meaning (ComposerView.HandleKey is unchanged). The editor (`ComposerNSTextView.Dictating`) is read-only, takes no typing, no paste, no Return (nothing is sent by it) and no arrows, ignores the pointer (its selection and the focus stay), and Esc is not its own (a list closing or a turn taken back) until the session is over; the landing lifts it before it writes.
11. One session at a time and the composer leaving (V-7.11, V-14.7). One session per `VoiceSessionHub` is VT-3's; the composer calls `ComposerLeaving` when it leaves the visual tree (a thread switch, a window close) and when the chat column goes behind another: the session stops as a second click would, the text lands in that thread's draft and is never sent.
12. After voice input (V-8.8, Q-V-11 C). The session's `SendRequested` (0.35 s after Landing starts) calls `ComposerView.Send`, the Return path itself: nothing running sends; a running turn is interrupted and the text sent; with heads at work it is queued (`ThreadRuntime.InterruptAndSend`, ComposerView.swift:370-382). The composer decides nothing of its own. Proved against a real runtime: nothing running (`SentPrompts`), a running turn (interrupted), a head at work (one follow-up, the lead left running), leave (nothing ever sent), a new dictation before the send drops it.
13. Merge. unit/rec-composer was merged in (its heavy changes to `ComposerView.cs` came in clean); `porting/engineering_decisions.md` kept both sides byte-exact. Both branches had added `tests/Marrow.App.Tests/Window/OpenPanelNativeTests.cs`: staging's (the sidebar folder chooser, ED-332) stays as it was and rec-composer's (the composer's attach chooser, ED-NEW-rec-composer) is `ComposerAttachOpenPanelNativeTests.cs`, its class renamed with it; `WindowManagerNativeChildProtocol`'s allow-list has both names and the union of the two lists. The lead's own resolution of that collision at the rec-composer merge supersedes this one.
14. NOT DONE (reasons in STATE.md). The voice level does not reach the orb: `VoiceSession` takes the capture's audio and does not publish the level or bands (`LevelAnalyser` and the followers of V-5.5 exist and are unused), so the orb shows its states (rest, hover, listening, processing, blocked, landing) but does not follow the voice until a unit taps the audio; the live words, the pill, the cross, the floating pill, the language name and the question are VT-11 and VT-12; the glow and the composer light's give-way are VT-9 and VT-12; the 30 s countdown and the other error notes are VT-17; the production seams' start-up binding is VT-14. Nothing was seen on a real window with a GPU: the orb's overflow inside the glass pill, the plate's look outside the pill and the notes' placement are headless-checked only.
15. Fix round after review (FIX FIRST). (a) V-8.5 "focus is not stolen": a pointer press on the orb moved the keyboard to its (focusable, V-14.2) button and nothing gave it back, so after the words landed Return started a new session instead of sending. `VoiceOrbSlot` remembers what held the keyboard at the press (a tunnelling handler, before the button takes it) and gives it back when the session leaves Listening or Processing for Landing or Rest, if the button still has it (a press with the keyboard already on the orb, or a key activation, restores nothing). Test `ComposerVoiceFocusTests` (the reviewer's red test, cherry-picked from review/vt10-focus a2700e7c9). (b) Esc ordering (V-14.4): the window handler added when the session goes live runs before one added later, so a sheet or popover opened after it never got Esc; it now yields when a sheet has taken the window's keyboard (`SheetKeyboard.IsTaken`, new, set by `Take`) or a transient is open over it (`WindowTransients.Newest`), and ignores Esc with any modifier held. Tests: sheet after live, sheet closed before, popover open, modifiers. (c) The attachment buttons' fade (0.28 s ease) and scale (0.6 to 1 over 0.34 s ez) and the orb slot's size spring (response 0.34, damping 0.86, the underdamped closed form written out in the test) are checked every frame against the curve, replacing the 15 % bound. (d) A cancel with "send" set sends nothing and leaves no text (`SentPrompts` empty). (e) Traceability: the VT-10 tests no longer carry Decision ED-292 (VT-2's); until the lead numbers this entry they carry `Rule` R-VIEW-4 (the ones that prove motion) or R-TEST-10 (scripted seams, no hardware, no network), to be changed to Decision with this entry's number. WAIVED by the lead: the attachment button's move with the flag off (OD-0091 and its amendments order it).

## ED-349

[VOICE][COMPOSER][ENGINEERING] Voice typing unit VT-11 (Composer B: the live words, the DictationLayer; and the audio level and bands the VT-10 orb lacked; branch unit/f-vt-11 from unit/f-vt-10 at 7045b2f30; the lead numbers it at merge). ENGINEERING DECISIONS where voice-SPEC.md (V-2.2, V-5.3, V-5.5, V-7.5, V-8.1 to V-8.10), the voice design (voice-composer.html/.js, voicecmp.js), OD-0091, OD-0099 and OD-0106 and the Swift are silent; none changes an owner ruling. Code: `src/Marrow.Core/Port/Voice/{Dsp/AudioLevelMeter,Transcript/DictationPlacement}.cs` (new), edits to `Seams/IAudioCapture.cs`, `Seams/ScriptedCapture.cs`, `Session/VoiceSession.cs`, `Transcript/DictationInsertion.cs`, `src/Marrow.Services/Port/Voice/Capture/CapturePipeline.cs`; `src/Marrow.App/Port/Voice/Dictation{Layer,Words,Word,Tween,Flip,Caret,Ink,Motion,Phase,WordLook,LayerLook,OldText}.cs` (new), edits to `ComposerVoiceController.cs`, `VoiceOrbSlot.cs`, `src/Marrow.App/Views/Composer/{ComposerTextView,ComposerView}.cs`. Tests: Core `AudioLevelMeterTests`, `VoiceSessionLevelTests`, `DictationPlacementTests`; Services `CapturePipelineTapTests`; App `Port/Voice/{DictationWordsTests,DictationFlipTests,DictationCaretTests}`, `Views/Composer/{ComposerVoiceOrbLevelTests,ComposerDictationLiveTests,ComposerDictationLandingTests,ComposerDictationWithdrawTests,ComposerDictationRtlTests,ComposerDictationDesignStreamTests}` and the fixtures `CssCurves`, `DictationProbe`, `DictationStreamFixture` (with `tests/fixtures/voice/make-dictation-stream.js` and its output `dictation-stream.json`, the design's own SCRIPT, SYN, STREAM and planFinal run in node). 82 new tests (27 Core, 6 Services, 49 App; 84 voice-composer tests of VT-10 and VT-11 together pass). No microphone, engine, model file or network in any test.
1. VT-3 ADDITION: the level and bands (V-2.2 items 2 and 4, V-5.3). `VoiceSession` gains `AudioLevel` (a `LevelBands`: the raw all, low, mid and high of V-5.3 at the fixed 60 Hz of the signal, zero outside Listening) and `OnAudioBlock(CaptureFormat, ReadOnlySpan<float>)`. `IAudioCaptureSink` gains the same member as a DEFAULT interface method with an empty body (additive: no existing sink changes): it is the processing thread's tap, called with each batch the capture drained, in the format the capture started in, before the batch is posted to the main executor. `CapturePipeline.Take` (inside Pump's lock, so the processing thread and Flush on the main thread are serialised) calls it, a tap that throws loses nothing (the batch still goes on), `ScriptedCapture.Push` calls it before OnAudio (on its caller's thread, so the manual clock drives it). `AudioLevelMeter` (Core Dsp) is the session's: it averages the channels (V-5.1) into a preallocated 512-sample chunk, pushes the device-rate mono signal into a `LevelAnalyser` (noise floor on, V-5.4) and reads it when k x rate / 60 frames (integer division) have arrived, so a block of any size gives the reads inside it; nothing allocates after the first block of a format (tested with GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread over rounds of 100 blocks until three in a row allocate nothing, as ED-267's capture test does); the four values are published through a sequence lock (odd while writing; a reader that sees the same even sequence before and after has one publication's values: tested with a reader thread against a feeding thread), so a read never mixes two reads and no lock or allocation is taken on either side. `Reset` runs in `StartListening` before the capture starts (no capture is feeding it then). The analysis therefore runs on the processing thread, never the UI thread.
2. The orb follows the voice (V-5.5, V-11.4). `ComposerVoiceController.StepLevel(dt)` runs the per-band followers (`LevelFollowers`: attack 0.07 s, release 0.24 s, values under 1e-4 to 0) over the session's `AudioLevel` once per frame and keeps `OrbBands`; the orb's own motion takes the voice value (0.12 s / 0.45 s) from them. The bands follow the audio all the time, as the design's do (voice-composer.js:718-722): when listening ends the session's level is zero and they FALL on the release (about two seconds from a half to zero), they do not snap. `VoiceOrbSlot` drives it with a `DisplayLink` that starts when the session is Listening and the slot is on screen and stops itself when the bands reach zero (no frame is asked for at rest: tested against the frame source's pending count); leaving the screen resets them. Every frame is tested against the follower formula written out in the test.
3. Where the words live (V-8.2, V-8.3, V-8.7). The EDITOR KEEPS THE DRAFT THE SESSION BEGAN WITH, untouched, read-only, its selection where it was, until Landing; the words live in the `DictationLayer` (a Control in the same scrolled content as the editor, laid exactly over it) and in the DRAFT (`runtime.Draft.Text`, written on every change through the layer's `TextChanged`), so the composer is in its typing state (DraftIsEmpty false: the light, the send button, the height) while the editor's undo history is never touched by a live edit (V-8.7 "live edits do not record undo states"). `ComposerNSTextView.LiveText` is the text the layer draws: the composer measures its height from it, and `ComposerTextView.Update` does not assign a draft written meanwhile to the editor (Avalonia's TextBox clears its undo history on a Text assignment). The editor is hidden by clearing its Foreground and its presenter's selection and caret brushes (`EnterDictation` / `ExitDictation`, saved and restored), not by opacity, so its placeholder (which FieldFade fades out as the first word arrives, `HasWordsChanged`, and back when no word is left) and its layout stay. At Landing the controller writes the insertion as ONE `ReplaceCharacters` edit of the editor's own text (the editor opened for that call only: `RunUnlocked`), which is the one undo step (tested: one Undo gives the text before the dictation, a second the user's own edit before that; Redo returns it); `DraftSelection` and `ReplaceDraft` read the editor while a dictation draws. After that the editor measures its own height again (`LiveText` null), follows the draft again (a send clears it) and the layer, now only a picture, hands back when the words have settled.
4. The picture (V-8.3). The layer draws the text the insertion makes (`DictationInsertion.Place`, new in Core: the text, the first index of each word, where the text after the insertion begins, the caret) with the editor's typeface, size, width, wrapping, flow direction and alignment at the editor's padding, so a word that is not moving is part of ONE TextLayout, exactly the kind of layout the editor draws (the settled frame is the editor's: tested pixel-identical). Words that are moving (rising in, revised, leaving, following a changed place) are drawn one by one at the places the layout's own hit tests give them (`HitTestTextRange`: the layout does the bidi, so right-to-left words animate in place) and are clear in the base layout (a text style override); the tentative colour is a per-range brush override (the text colour at 0.6 in the light theme and 0.62 in the dark, the design's `--wink3`, rebuilt only when a colour changes: the layout is cached by a hash of text, width and overrides). A word the layout splits across lines (more than one rectangle) is not drawn on its own and so does not rise (it appears with its line). The caret is 1.5 x 17 in the text colour a pixel past the end of the last word (its left end for a right-to-left word, by script), centred on its line, riding with the word's own place, blinking on the design's keyframes (`DictationCaret`, 1.06 s, ease-in-out between 45 % and 55 % and 95 % and 100 %; still under Reduce Motion, as the design's `animation:none`); it leaves over 0.18 s ease at Landing (the editor's own caret is the editor's business once it has the text back).
5. The motion model (V-7.5) is `DictationWords`, a model on instants: it answers `Look(word, instant)` for any instant, so a frame, a test and a replay read the same numbers, and a value changed in flight goes on from the value shown (the browser's rule: `DictationTween`). The design's numbers, from voice-composer.html:123-131: Add opacity .3 s ease and 6 px to 0 over .4 s ez (hidden on its first frame); Confirm the colour .45 s ease; Revise the old text (it keeps the opacity and rise it has) goes to 0 and -6 px over .22 s ease and .3 s ez and is gone at .34 s while the new text starts at 0 and +6 px and comes in on the same two; a second revision keeps the first old text until its own .34 s (the design's reviseWord); Remove opacity .26 s ease and 5 px down over .3 s ez, gone at .34 s, a leaver still taking its place in the text until then. Operations name words by their place among the words not leaving. An Add does NOT confirm the word before it (V-7.5's "adding a word confirms the previous one" is the design's one-word tail; the port's tail is the transcriber's, so Confirm operations decide, as `TranscriptOps.Diff` and `PlanLanding` produce them). Under Reduce Motion every transition lands at once. `Words.Still` is read at each operation.
6. FLIP (V-7.5 "later words follow their new positions with the same ease"). Each word, and each whitespace-delimited word of the text after the insertion, has a `DictationFlip`: the place the layout gives it, reached from the place drawn now along ez over .3 s, whatever moved it (a revision's new width, a word that wrapped, an added word); the first place is taken as it is; a change under 0.01 px is not a move. The text after the insertion starts from its places in the draft as it was (activation lays the original out first). A place change starts when the operation that caused it was DUE, not at the frame that handled it, so a late frame never shifts the curve. A change of the editor's width (the window, or the field's scroll bar coming) lays the words out anew and they glide to their new places the same way.
7. The first word (V-8.1). The layer takes over at the first word (Armed until then: the editor draws, with its selection). A replaced selection is not cut: the layer draws the original text with only the selection visible (its highlight filled as the editor's own snapped selection rectangles) and fades it out over .22 s ease while the words that were after it glide to their places; the editor's own selection and caret drawing are cleared at that moment.
8. Landing and the hand-over (V-8.3, V-8.7). Landing's Confirm operations ink the tentative words 25 ms apart on .45 s each (the plan `TranscriptOps.PlanLanding` makes: the k-th TENTATIVE word, which differs from the design's `confirmAll` delay of index x 25 ms; VT-3's rule stands). The layer hands the picture back when nothing is moving (words, places, the caret's fade, the selection's fade) and one more frame has drawn the settled text: the editor's own text, selection brushes and read-write state return in the same turn as the layer stops drawing (`EndLife`). The ink wave of a long dictation can outlast the session's 0.5 s Landing; the layer lives on until it has settled, and a click on the orb meanwhile (a new session) hands over at once. If the draft is written after Landing (the send of V-8.8 clears it) the layer hands over at once. A composer leaving the screen hands over at once and, before the text has landed, puts the draft back to what the editor holds (the session lands its words by one edit later).
9. Withdraw (V-8.6). The layer plans the withdraw from the words it HAS drawn (`TranscriptOps.PlanWithdraw(count)`: from the end, 30 ms apart, each .26 s ease and 5 px .3 s ez, gone at .34 s) and drops operations not yet due, so nothing arrives after a cancel; when the last has gone a replaced selection fades back in where it was (its text and highlight, .22 s ease, the mirror of the ghost of item 7, while the words after it glide back by FLIP) and the caret, which rode with the leaving words (its place glides like a word's, `PlaceCaret`), fades where they were (.18 s ease); then the draft is set to its text before the session (the editor, never changed, holds that text and its selection) and the editor is the user's again, in the frame after everything has settled (the review found the old text cutting back in on the last word's frame, and the caret vanishing at Esc). Reduce Motion skips the fades. A session that ends with no landing and no withdraw (an error, nothing heard) tells the controller's `DictationAbandoned`: words drawn leave as a cancel's do, none: the layer closes. The controller's session events (`DictationBegan`, `Transcript`, `DictationAbandoned`) are what ComposerView hands the layer; the editor is read-only while the session is live or the layer draws (`ApplyDictating`).
10. RTL (V-8.9). The layer uses the editor's own FlowDirection and TextAlignment; the editor itself does not detect a paragraph's direction (Avalonia's TextLayout has no such mode and the port's editor had none), so Urdu text in a left-to-right editor is one right-to-left run whose first word is at its right end, growing to the left, and the words already there glide right as each word is added (FLIP: tested frame by frame on an Urdu fixture, and the hand-over to the editor on the same fixture is pixel-identical). A right-to-left paragraph direction for the editor is not part of this unit.
11. Scroll (V-8.10). When the end of the text passes the bottom of the field the scroll goes there on the design's .36 s ez (`.tin`'s transform), to the field's own extent less its viewport (known after the layout pass: the move starts a frame after the words). Tested against the curve with the start allowed one to three frames late.
12. THE LEAD'S RULING ON THE FRAME CRITERION (each frame against the curve, not against a share of the travel) is followed in every test of this unit: `CssCurves` solves the design's `ease` and `ez` the way a browser does (Newton, then bisection), independently of the port's bisection; a frame's instant is a whole number of 100 ns ticks and the curves are steep at their start, so the tolerance is 1e-5 on a value of 0 to 1 (1e-4 px for places). The opacity and colour curves are also read off RENDERED PIXELS (a word's ink on the frame, against a baseline frame, follows the opacity curve; the tentative word is at 0.6 of the solid ink; the colour turns solid on ease). The design's own live words are replayed (`dictation-stream.json`: the design's STREAM and planFinal run in node) through the layer and every word's opacity, rise, colour, revision text and old text are compared with the CSS curves worked out from the events alone, at every 60 Hz frame, through the live stream, the final pass of a second click at 7.2 s and Landing's ink.
13. VT-10 tests changed, because the interim rule they asserted ("nothing is written until the session lands; VT-11 writes it live", as their own comment says) is what VT-11 replaces by V-8.2: ComposerVoiceSessionTests `The_text_lands_in_the_draft_after_the_caret_with_a_space_and_the_caret_ends_after_it` now asserts the draft holds the words while listening (and the editor its own text until landing) before the same landing assertions, and `A_second_orb_clicked_finishes_the_first_session_and_then_starts` asserts the shared draft STARTS WITH the first session's text (the second session's own live words follow it). Nothing else of VT-10 changed. Also covered: Reduce Motion in the layer, an engine failure mid-session (the drawn words leave and the draft returns), a cancel before any word, a send after landing (the layer hands over at once).
14. NOT DONE (STATE.md): nothing was seen on a real window with a GPU (the words, the caret, the scroll and the hand-over are headless-Skia checked only); VoiceFeature.Enabled stays false, so no user sees any of it; the production binding of the seams (the real capture feeding the tap) is VT-14's; the orb follows the voice only through the scripted capture in tests (the real WasapiCapture's tap is covered by the pipeline tests, not by a microphone); a right-to-left paragraph direction for the editor (item 10); words that wrap across lines do not rise on their own (item 4); the glow's use of the level (VT-9, VT-12) and the pill, cross, float and language question (VT-12).

15. Codex T3 review fix (2026-10-05), test first. The selection fade test now takes the expected text and highlight from the editor before dictation, checks background-only highlight pixels on every .22 s ease frame, and requires the final layer image to equal that original selected image before hand-over. It failed alone twice before the fix: difference 2.0667, 40 changed pixels at the highlight right and bottom edges. ENGINEERING DECISION: DrawGhost fills selection rectangles separately from the glyphs, using PixelRect.FromRect(rect, 1).ToRect(1) exactly as Avalonia 12.1.2 TextPresenter.Render does (upstream src/Avalonia.Controls/Presenters/TextPresenter.cs:374-388, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AvaloniaUI/Avalonia/12.1.2/src/Avalonia.Controls/Presenters/TextPresenter.cs); the run background kept fractional edges and could not match the editor. The .22 s group fade and text drawing stay the same. The strengthened assertion passed alone twice after the fix. Headless Skia only; no native, GPU or whole-port parity claim.


## ED-350

ENGINEERING DECISION, VT-11-preview; authority: OD-0091, voice-SPEC V-14.1 and customization-SPEC CZ-4.3 / CZ-T45.

1. The runtime-free `ComposerPreview` restates the current real `ComposerArea` with voice off: the inert attachment button is a separate left overlay, 34 x 28, 8 px from the left and bottom, with its paperclip centred; the text inset is 48 px (the original 14 plus the inside attachment's 34). Pixel thresholds, crop rules and background subtraction are unchanged; no fixture or expected pixel value is rewritten. The three original failures reproduced alone twice before the fix; the corrected geometry query also failed alone twice against the old production preview's four-child trailing row.

## ED-351

[VOICE][ENGINEERING] VT-17, voice notes, the cap countdown and the CUDA offer (the model and service parts; branch `cloud/f-vt-17`, on `claude/verify-terminal-20261001` at e6b4656c3). The lead numbers it at merge. The owner's picks are OD-0106 (Notes A Plain, Countdown C with its amendments, CUDA A); each item below is an ENGINEERING DECISION unless it says SOURCE FACT, and none changes what the owner picked. The tests carry `Decision ED-267` (the voice umbrella) and `Rule R-TEST-4` with the source named in the comment, because the traceability checks accept no other ids.

1. **The eleven notes are set A byte for byte (SOURCE FACT: the D-VN page's `vndata`, read by the tests from the repository).** `VoiceNotes.All` holds the page's eleven in its order and `VoiceNotes.Blocked` is the locked V-14.6 note. Each is `Before` plus one `Link` plus a destination: Windows Settings Privacy > Microphone (locked), Windows Settings System > Sound, and the app's own Settings > Voice typing > Microphone, Speech model, Engine, OpenAI key and the page. The right single quotation mark (U+2019) of the page is kept.
2. **How long a note stays: 5.2 s for all twelve** (the page's open point; the locked note's V-14.6 time, which the page proposed for the others). A newer note replaces an older one and restarts the 5.2 s.
3. **Which surface shows a note (V-14.6, OD-0106): an empty draft (null or "") shows it in the field; any text, a blank draft included, shows it in the composer's notice line.** The blank draft counts as text because the placeholder test is "no characters". The surface is read when the note appears and again on `RefreshSurface()`, which the composer calls when the draft changes, so typing while a note shows moves it to the notice line (the user's text is never hidden) and clearing the draft moves it back. Nothing is announced again when nothing moved.
4. **The still-downloading note beside the download pill (the page's open point): they do not both show.** While the pill shows the first download ("Getting voice ready", VT-15) the "Model still downloading" note is not raised; the note is for the case where that pill is not shown. The bridge takes this as `pillShowsDownload`.
5. **Screen-reader announcements (the page's open point).** (a) A note's announcement is derived from its words: the locked note's is V-14.5's own string (SOURCE FACT); any other is the note's text with " > " read as ", " and a full stop at the end ("No microphone found. Set one up in System, Sound."), so the spoken version cannot drift from the shown one and no new wording is invented. (b) The countdown is announced twice, politely, as the page proposed: "30 seconds left." when the countdown starts (4:30 of listening) and "10 seconds left." 20 s later; a session that ends first makes no later one. The two strings are new wording (the page named the moments, not the words) and are the only invented strings in this unit; the owner's amendments moved the line's colour points to 0:15 and 0:05 but the announcements keep the page's 0:30 and 0:10, because they say how much time is left, not what the line looks like. The cap's own "Finishing the text." is V-14.5's, as at a click.
6. **Which note each failure is (V-17.6; each driven from a scripted failure at its seam in `VoiceNoteSeamTests`).** The session said only what kind of failure (`VoiceNoteKind`), which could not tell an unplugged microphone from a busy one or a cloud refusal from a missing model, so `VoiceSession` now keeps `FailureCause` (the exception of a failed capture start, model load or pass) and `LastDeviceEvent`, and `VoiceSessionHub` keeps `LoadFailure`; nothing else in the session changed (572 Core voice tests still pass). Then: a denied microphone is the locked note; no endpoint is "No microphone"; a `CaptureDeviceException` InUse or the in-use device event is "busy", NotFound or Removed is "unplugged"; any other capture failure is the engine note ("Voice typing stopped on an error"), because no note of the set names it; an OpenAI cloud exception wins over everything else and maps by `CloudNote` (key missing, key refused, quota or rate, no network, any other answer = the engine note); otherwise a failed load is "still downloading" while the model's download runs, "No AVX2" when the processor lacks it, else "failed to load"; a failed pass is the engine note. Cancelled and no speech stay V-14.6's own designed notes and are not resolved here. A processor seam that cannot answer (unbound) is not blamed: the plain failed-to-load note shows.
7. **A removed microphone (V-4.4): the text finishes first and the unplugged note comes after the final pass**, when the session leaves Processing for Landing or Rest, as the spec says ("runs the final pass on what it has, then shows the device note"). **INTERPRETATION, flagged for the lead:** V-4.4 says a changed default device or a removed one "shows the device note"; the set's one device note says "Microphone disconnected", which is false after a default-device or format change, so only DeviceRemoved shows it; the other two stop the session as before with no note (nothing broke that a link fixes).
8. **The countdown line's colours are tokens of the locked designs (OD-0106 asked the lead to record them).** Neutral is the pill's own label tone `--pgLab` (dark #8D8E94, light #55565B) at 55 % opacity, exactly as the page draws the draining line (`color-mix(in srgb, var(--pgLab) 55%, transparent)`, vn-page.css:209). Warning is `--vwarn`, the colour of the blocked note's mark (dark #E0A84A, light #B7791F: the app's other warning mark in the composer). Danger is the app's error red, AppTheme's fixed systemRed #FF3B30 in both themes, because the voice design has no red of its own. The opacity rises to 1 along the same glide. Palettes are `CountdownPalette.Dark` and `.Light`; the view chooses by theme.
9. **The line's length and timing.** Fraction is the time left over 30 s (1 at 0:30, 0.5 at 0:15); the line shows for 0 < left <= 30 s and is gone at the cap, where the session already finishes the text as a click would (VT-3). Under Reduce Motion the fraction steps once a second (the ceiling of the seconds left over 30). The cap itself, the 270 s countdown start and the stop are VT-3's and are not changed.
10. **The glide (the owner left the manner to the lead and asked for "premium"; OD-0106's own choice, built as written).** Colourless from 0:30 to 0:15; a glide to the warning colour starting at 0:15 and to the error colour starting at 0:05 (the second amendment: not 0:10); each 0.8 s on cubic-bezier(.42, 0, .58, 1) (CSS ease-in-out) through OKLCH; then one brightening of 0.4 s starting as the colour has arrived: sin squared of the time, lifting OKLCH lightness by up to 0.05 (restrained). Under Reduce Motion the glide is 0.2 s and there is no brightening. Details that settle the maths: lightness and chroma are linear and the hue takes the shorter arc, so the hue turns cleanly with even lightness (yellow to red turns one way, through orange, and keeps its chroma); a nearly colourless end (chroma under 0.02, whose hue is meaningless) glides along the straight line in OKLab to the other colour, which is the same path with the colourless end taking the other's hue, and is exactly the palette's own colour at the start (a 0.009-chroma blue tint on the neutral passes through the colourless axis, below one just-noticeable step); a colour the brightening lifts out of sRGB (the red) keeps its lightness and hue and gives up chroma until it fits, instead of being clamped per channel; the colours a glide starts and ends at are returned as the palette's own, exactly. Proven frame by frame at 60 Hz against a second derivation of the curves, in both themes and under Reduce Motion, and for "never a cut" (no frame steps more than 6 % of a channel, 20 % in the 0.2 s Reduce Motion glide), "no grey or brown midpoint" and the hue direction. NOT DONE: the OD's last line, "the result is compared on a variant still before it ships", needs the pill drawn.
11. **The CUDA row (OD-0106 CUDA A, drawn on the page as look A).** "NVIDIA CUDA", with the detail line and the model list's state column of the page (a Download capsule; the percentage with the cancel x titled "Cancel the download" and the 2 px bar; the check and "Installed"; Download again after a failure); the strings are the page's (the test reads vn-page.js for them). Size "644 MB" is the three pinned files added (250,058,371 + 391,101,865 + 2,474,121 bytes) and shown as V-9.2 shows sizes. Cancel returns to the offer and keeps the partial (the shared downloader's way); a second press while it runs is the same download; progress counts the pack and the NVIDIA libraries by their bytes and only moves forward; the percentage rounds half up.
12. **When the row shows ("only on NVIDIA PCs with a working probe").** "Working probe" is read as: the probe finished (a probe that throws, is cancelled or is unbound shows nothing) and the graphics adapter is NVIDIA. It is also hidden when CUDA is already the working backend (the GPU backend row then reads "CUDA, working") and while no installer for NVIDIA's libraries is bound (item 14): an offer that could only fail is never shown. An NVIDIA PC whose Vulkan check said "none working" is still offered CUDA, because nothing in the plan ties the offer to Vulkan. A pack and libraries already on disk show the Installed state, and the pack alone on disk is still an offer.
13. **The restart after the download (the page's open point): none is done and none is offered.** The Installed state says "Restart Marrow to use it" (the page's words): Whisper.net loads its native runtime once per process (VT-6 item 5) and the hardware check itself loads one, so the next start, whose runtime inventory then lists the CUDA runtime, uses it. No restart button or automatic restart is added (an invented control). If the libraries fail after the pack succeeded, the 250 MB pack stays on disk (the next press does not fetch it again, tested) and the row says Failed ("Nothing was installed" is true: the inventory lists the CUDA runtime only when the pack and the three libraries are all there, so a half-installed pack is never loaded, OD-0104).
14. **UNRESOLVED and NOT DONE: the production installer for NVIDIA's libraries.** VT-7 installs the Whisper.net pack only ("the NVIDIA libraries it needs beside it are not part of this class"). The two NVIDIA archives (cuBLAS 12.4.2.65 and the CUDA runtime 12.4.99, pinned in voice-pins.json) need an installer that unzips `cudart64_12.dll`, `cublas64_12.dll` and `cublasLt64_12.dll` from them. Nothing in the record says where those files sit inside the archives, the probe never fetched them, and the pins' own note leaves "whether Marrow may download and unpack these on the user's PC" UNRESOLVED for the owner, so it was not written from memory. `ICudaCompanions` is the seam; `FailClosedCudaCompanions` (the default) hides the offer; `ScriptedCudaCompanions` is the test double. The pack's download, the offer and every end state are done and tested on the loopback fake.
15. **NOT DONE here, by instruction or because the owner of the file has not merged:** (a) drawing the draining line inside the pill (VoicePill is VT-12's); the pill reads `CapCountdownLine.Frame()` per frame and `Announced`; (b) drawing the CUDA row in VoiceTypingSettingsPage (VT-14's); it reads `CudaOffer.Row` and calls `EvaluateAsync`, `StartAsync` and `Cancel`; (c) drawing the notes: the field's note layer and the notice line's underlined link are the composer's; they read `VoiceNoteBridge.Current` and call `RefreshSurface()` on a draft change; (d) opening a link: the destinations are named (`VoiceNoteDestination`), but the Windows URI of the Sound page is not recorded in the plan (V-14.6 names only `ms-settings:privacy-microphone`) and the app pages need VT-13 and VT-14's navigation, so no link is opened here; (e) the production binding of `IProcessorFeatures` (an AVX2 check) and the composition that creates the bridge, the line and the offer; (f) a native Windows run: nothing here needs one, and none was made.
16. **Order of work, honestly.** Each part was written as skeleton types whose members throw `NotImplementedException`, then the tests, then seen red (notes 81 of 81, countdown 31 of 31, CUDA 29 of 29 failed) before the code. Fixes found while turning them green are in the tests and not hidden: the notes' device and decode tests first ran on a silent room, so the session finished at once with no words and they were given the V-14.8 speech script; the countdown's first brightening comparison exposed that `TimeSpan` ticks (100 ns) bound the precision of the sampled time to 1e-5, and its brightening-lift test exposed the red being clamped out of sRGB (item 10); a mutation (the red point at 0:10 instead of 0:05) failed 4 of 31 countdown tests. The traceability checks then forced the trait ids and one type per file (the `ThrowingProbe` double moved to a fixture).

## ED-356

[VIEW] The liquid-glass material (OD-0107 and its amendment; audit items 2 and 3 of the glass audit, E:\Droppy\work\scratch\glass-audit). `src/Marrow.UI/Port/GlassMaterial.cs` only, plus the two site values its change moved (SmallAccentGlassButton's disabled wash) and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. ENGINEERING DECISION throughout, calibrated on the Mac frames at 1 px = 1 pt (the composer pill is 46 px tall in the 2560 frames, as its 46 pt).
1. **Translucency.** DEFECT: the blur surface was cleared to an opaque veil (#1E1E20 dark, #F5F5F7 light) and 18 % of it mixed back in, so over the Acrylic window's transparent or scrim pixels the glass was near-black and opaque. FIX: the blur surface is cleared to nothing; the shader works on the blurred backdrop premultiplied and keeps its alpha. Because the result is translucent it cannot be drawn over the sharp pixels under it (they would show through), so each pixel becomes mix(under, value, amount) in two draws of the one shader program: stage 0 with BlendMode.DstOut takes `amount` (coverage, contact line, the piece's opacity) away, stage 1 with BlendMode.Plus adds value times amount. The inside of a lone rounded rectangle (ED-320 16) is the same program with an `interior` uniform (it skips the distance), so the inside drawing stays byte-identical to the whole shader's (the separate Inner and Unlit programs are gone; with them a 1-level difference appeared once the body read the piece's height).
2. **Lift (the body).** Each read is lifted on its own (saturation 1.4 about its luma: Apple's vibrancy, rizzytoday's `saturate()`), then dashersw/liquid-glass-js's white-to-grey tint gradient goes over it as a translucent layer: 0.17 of a grey of 0.94 down to half the height, easing (smoothstep 0.45 to 0.85) to 0.70 at the bottom, in the dark appearance; 0.30 of 1.0 to 0.90 in the light one (no light frame was measured). Fitted to the Mac composer pill over its backdrop of about 57 (frames 01, 29, 30): 88 at the middle and 75 to 77 low down, against 88 and 77 to 78 (dashersw's own 0.2 and linear 1.0 to 0.7 gave 89 and a top 6 levels light). Over a transparent pixel the glass is that film alone: alpha 43, a light grey, never black.
3. **Edge.** All in the one shader pass, sized by the piece (GlassMaterial.Optics):
   - Bend: rizzytoday/liquid-glass's displacement-map profile, full at the edge and falling as the complement of its blurred neutral centre (logistic form, width 21 % of the smaller side up to 11, border 3.5 % up to 3), sampled outward along the inward normal; 55 % of the smaller side up to 40 pt on pieces of 100 pt or more, a smaller share below (a fifth of it at 32 pt and under), because the Mac small pieces read little from past their edge: with half the panel share the title capsules' first pixel read 84 against the Mac's 68 (a bright strip 15 pt out), and the pill's top 3 to 8 levels light where the backdrop above it brightens. Plus dashersw's rim ring, 8 % of the smaller side up to 10 times exp(-0.8 d).

## ED-357

[UI][GLASS][WIN][TEST] Every popover and menu is see-through glass, as NSPopover's Liquid Glass is on the Mac (OD-0107 and its amendment, OD-0005; owner, 2026-10-05: "when any popup opens, anything in the composer, I see a black, dark background, not liquid glass"). Unit glass-g2, branch unit/glass-g2 from claude/verify-terminal-20261001 (93634a99a); the lead numbers this heading at merge. DEFECT (glass audit, E:\Droppy\work\scratch\glass-audit\compare\cmp_popover.png): PopoverHost.Wrap hung every presented popover on a PopoverCard that painted ED-238's flat kit panel, #1E1E1E in Dark and #FFFFFF in Light, opaque, square-cornered, in a popup window that showed nothing of what was behind it.

(1) THE MECHANISM (ENGINEERING DECISION; PopoverGlass.cs, new). OD-0005 rules out reading the screen, so what is behind a popup reaches it only through the window manager. Avalonia 12.1.2 draws every window through Windows.UI.Composition (Win32CompositionMode.WinUIComposition, the default the port keeps): a root container in the window's desktop target holding Avalonia's own Acrylic sprite (a host-backdrop brush through a 30 px Gaussian blur, the main window's Acrylic of ED-236) under the sprite of the app's drawing. That sprite, like DWM's own system backdrops (DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE, DWMSBT_TRANSIENTWINDOW), covers the window's rectangle, rounded at most by DWM's 8 px; ED-236 (a) found SetWindowRgn does not clip it. None of them follows a card with a 20 pt corner and a tip inside a popup that also holds the card's shadow. So the popup keeps Avalonia's Transparent level, and PopoverGlass adds under the app's drawing, in the same container (InsertAbove Avalonia's hidden Acrylic sprite): a container clipped to the card's body by a CompositionGeometricClip of a rounded rectangle (anti-aliased by the compositor), and a second one, turned 45 degrees about its middle, clipped to a rounded square whose outer half is exactly the card's tip (sides at 45 degrees, a 90 degree point of radius 3 pt, half diagonal 12 pt = TipHeight). Each holds a sprite with Avalonia's shared blur brush (shared.BlurBrush; reused, nothing new is built) and, in Dark, a MinBlend sprite of a solid #565656 that caps every channel of the blurred backdrop. Everything Avalonia keeps internal (WindowImpl._glSurface, WinUiCompositedWindowSurface._window, WinUiCompositedWindow._shared and _blur, the MicroCom interfaces) is reached by reflection against the pinned 12.1.2; a missing member, a host that is no WinUI-composited native window (the overlay host, headless, another composition mode) or a failed call ends in Failure, and the card then draws ED-238's opaque panel under its tint (PopoverMaterial.Fallback) so it stays legible. PROBED on a real window (E:\Droppy\work\scratch\glass-g2\probe, shot_m0/m1/l0 and crops): (a) the blur sprite drew solid black until the window asked DWM for the host backdrop (DWMWA_USE_HOSTBACKDROPBRUSH = 17, which Avalonia sets only for a window whose own level is AcrylicBlur): PopoverGlass sets it when it is made; (b) ICompositor::CreateColorBrushWithColor takes Windows.UI.Color by value in the ABI while Avalonia's proxy passes a pointer (the cap came out an arbitrary lavender): the call goes through the vtable (slot 8) with the four bytes by value; (c) a floor for Light by DestinationInvert / MinBlend / DestinationInvert worked in the body but drew the whole diamond of the tip's square as a seam where the two clips' anti-aliased edges overlap (an inversion is not linear): dropped, Light has no compositor layer (see (3)); (d) the clip, the turned tip and MinBlend work over stripes, white and black (the probe, with its own 0.08 tint and the first cap 0x68: dark stripes 127 to 116, white to 116, black 21).

(2) THE CARD (PopoverCard.cs). SOURCE FACT, measured on the reference frames at 1 px = 1 pt (2-chat-use.mov 34.2 s the effort popover, 151.0 s the sidebar row menu, 55.0 s the usage popover; 1-settings-tour.mov 143.2 s the theme list in Light; the usage popover is 360 px wide on the Mac as UsagePanel's 360 pt): round corners of about 20 pt (the outline leaves each side about 20 px from the corner and crosses the diagonal 8.5 px from it, a circle of 20.5); outermost a near-black hairline (Dark 0-28 between a backdrop of 35-60 and a glass of 60-90; Light 146 between 194 and 215); a pixel inside it brighter than the glass (Dark +25 to +47, Light +8); the glass lighter than what is round it (Dark about +20 to +30, Light +25). ENGINEERING DECISION: BodyRadius 20 (named so, not CornerRadius: no raw CornerRadius is added, the ContinuousCornerSitesTests census is unchanged), circular arcs, not Apple's continuous curve, because the compositor's clip under them is a circular rounded rectangle and the two must coincide or the blur would show past the rim (the corner is held to half the shorter side, so a one-line menu is a capsule as on the Mac). The card fills the glass's outline (inset 0) with its tint, strokes the hairline on the outline 0.5 pt in (1 pt) and the rim 1.5 pt in (1 pt); the tip's sides are moved in along their normals for each inset, its point and shoulders concentric. The shadow (ED-238 round 2) is now clipped to outside the glass, so it cannot darken the translucent card from inside. The content is clipped to the body inside the hairline (radius 19) unless the site set its own clip. The tip is held past the round corner: TipLeast = BodyRadius + TipHalfWidth + TipShoulderRadius (36 pt) from either end, for the drawn tip and for Aim. The card keeps the window glass in step with itself: on its popup's Opened (PopoverHost.Follow) it makes the glass for a native popup window (else Fallback); on every layout, bounds, tip, transform and opacity change, and on every frame while it grows, fades or waits for the window's first frame, it hands PopoverGlass its outline in the window's physical pixels through TransformToVisual (so PopoverAppear's scale about the tip and its fade, as product of opacities up to the window, move the glass with the drawing); on Closed the glass is disposed. The shoulders' 4 pt fillets are drawn but not clipped (the composition tip is a plain square): the drawn tint covers about 0.7 pt^2 beside each shoulder where no blur is, invisible at 100 %. The rim is the card's own simple 1 pt line, not GlassMaterial's (unit glass-g1 is rewriting GlassMaterial.cs): it should move to g1's shared rim after that merges.

(3) THE NUMBERS (PopoverHost.Tint, Edge, Rim; PopoverGlass.DarkCap), fitted to (2) and to legibility over any backdrop (WCAG contrast, PopoverGlassCardTests.The_glass_keeps_its_text_readable_over_any_backdrop over 0, 58, 128, 255). Dark: cap #565656 (AMENDED by the review, (8)), tint white 0.10 (glass = min(B, 86) x 0.9 + 25.5: over black 25.5, over the Mac frame's 58 77.7 (the Mac 79), over white 102.9, where the label, white 0.85, is 4.63:1 and the secondary text, 0.7 of it, 3.13:1); hairline black 0.80; rim white 0.20. Light: no cap or floor, tint white 0.50 (glass = B x 0.5 + 127.5: over the Mac frame's 216 about 236 (the Mac 240), over black 127.5, where the label, black 0.85, is 4.64:1 and the secondary text 3.15:1); hairline black 0.28; rim white 0.20. The kit panel (Fill, Border) stays for a sheet and as the Fallback under the tint. Measured natively (PopoverGlassNativeTests): Dark over white 95-111 asserted (105-126 before (8)), over black 12-32; Light over black 118-140, over white 245-256 (the run's pixels: E:\Droppy\work\scratch\glass-g2\gallery\native-popover-Dark.png, -Light.png). UNRESOLVED: the Mac's glass is more saturated than the backdrop it blurs (its card over the teal lake reads teal-green); Avalonia's blur brush has no saturation step and the port builds none (no new effect graph through Avalonia's internals), so the port's glass is the backdrop's own colour, a little greyer.

(4) SIDE BY SIDE (Mac frame above, port below, native pixels, the port on a real window at 100 % under the native lock; E:\Droppy\work\scratch\glass-g2\compare\): effort_popover_dark.png, effort_popover_light.png (no light effort popover is in the videos: the Mac half is the theme list in Light, 1-settings-tour.mov 143.2 s), popovermenu_run_dark.png and _light.png (the run-script menu, a PopoverMenu, 131.5 s), usage_popover_dark.png and _light.png, sidebar_row_menu_dark.png and _light.png (151.0 s); a Light port half under a Dark Mac half compares the shape and edge only. (6) TIMING (PopoverGlassNativeTests.The_glass_reaches_the_screen_before_the_popover_has_grown_in; a sampler reads the stripes just above the tip, where the growing card arrives first, a few hundred times a second from before the popover opens; E:\Droppy\work\scratch\glass-g2\gallery\timing.txt): five runs, Opened = 0: the card's glass in the composition at 55.7 / 56.2 / 61.6 / 60.5 / 72.5 ms; the first changed sample on screen at 64 / 64 / 69 / 68 / 79 ms; the first fully blurred sample (contrast under 3) at 79 / 80 / 69 / 86 / 79 ms; opacity 1 at 75.4 / 78.3 / 78.9 / 73.9 ms (the first run's 3.5 ms was the timeline counting before the grow-in began, fixed); scale 1 at 235.8 / 236.2 / 239.8 / 240.1 ms. This implements the mandatory exact-version notes rule; it does not publish a release.

1. CHANGELOG.md is the Windows repository's versioned notes source: ## [version], with ### New features, ### Bug fixes and ### Refinements. The initial entry is for AssemblyInfo.cs's 1.7.0; the version/build metadata is unchanged. scripts/extract-release-notes.ps1 selects one exact version and writes its section as UTF-8 without an added BOM, preserving its text and line endings. The headings remain at their original level (the existing app digest accepts ### as well as the upstream --section form's ##). Unreleased and other versions never supply this version's changes. Thanks and unknown headings do not count as a recognised section. port_impacts 254 and upstream_defects 90/91 were read: the new packaging guard, authorised by OD-0111, rejects missing exact-version/recognised notes instead of silently borrowing or dropping them; the app's existing parity digest and section cards are preserved.

2. scripts/release-notes.ps1 is the shared read-only preflight. Missing files, whitespace-only notes, unidentified/wrong/duplicate versions, multiple versions in an explicit file and notes without a populated parity section throw a clear release-notes error. Discovery excludes fenced markdown examples; any H1/H2 heading bounds a CHANGELOG entry, including malformed neighbouring version headings, so their bullets cannot license the selected release. An explicit notes file may use promoted ## section headings but must identify only the package version. Validation precedes any native tooling call, artifact creation or deletion in package-windows.ps1. With no override, notes derive from CHANGELOG.md and the assembly version. Every actual pack would receive --releaseNotes with a snapshot of the validated text at artifacts/release-notes-<version>.md. -ValidateReleaseNotesOnly runs this same guard, reports the version and returns before any writes or commands. Standalone extraction validates before creating or overwriting its output. Nothing was packaged during this work.

3. The offered About UI already has the parity cards. WhatsNewTests proves their three categories, offered version and actual bullets in the real popover content, with SettingsView's AboutUpdateChromeAccessory present and the install progress idle. AboutSoftwareUpdateSection now also draws installed-version cards, with a version label, when there is no newer offer; it omits the installer row in that state. The existing parse-once-per-release-version behavior and PR-SETTINGS-243 lifecycle test remain unchanged. The Updates page (UE-4) and sidebar update popover (UE-5) previously offered actions without notes; UpdateWhatsNew places the same parity cards and a version label before their actions, following the injected checker's offer and folding on the existing motion system. Headless tests open every category and inspect its version and text before any download or update action.

4. Exact-version durability: updateChecker_installedRelease retains notes for the running version separately from updateChecker_release, which still follows UE-1's existing offered-release persistence. updateChecker_downloadedRelease captures the exact successful download's AvailableUpdate in MarrowUpdateItem and, after verification, in AppUpdater.Install. On the first startup of exactly that version, the checker promotes those notes to installedRelease and consumes the downloaded record; notes for another version are never presented as this version's installed notes. This independent record closes the reviewed race where 1.8.0 is downloaded, a later check persists a 1.9.0 offer, and Restart Marrow still applies 1.8.0. Both update paths are tested with fake engines/boundaries. A successful no-update check and another startup preserve the installed notes.

5. Traceability: new tests carry Decision ED-360, Feature UE-6 and Spec ids. Traceability accepts the existing ED-nnn form and the constrained unnumbered ED-NEW-<lowercase-unit>-<number> form; no existing trait requirement is removed. UE-T60/T61 cover missing default/override; T62 empty notes; T63 wrong/unidentified version; T64 no populated recognised section; T65 exact default selection, duplicate/empty entries, fences and malformed neighbours; T66 multiple explicit versions; T67 each parity heading's success path; T68 exact extraction, neighbouring versions and CRLF preservation; T69 refusal without creating or overwriting output; T70 existing About offer; T71 retained About notes after update/check/reopen; T72 both additional offers before any update action; T74 mandatory pack argument and preflight ordering; T75/T76 the delayed-restart race in both paths. ReleaseNotesScriptRig uses only disposable repositories (including spaces and Unicode in paths) and command guards: dotnet, vpk and gh cannot execute. Every packaging refusal checks non-zero exit, diagnosis, unchanged fixture files and no artifacts or native-command call.

6. Test harness repairs required by the broader slice: UpdatePillTests and UpdatePillPopoverTests now explicitly inject the existing RenderingGeniePlatform's animation preference during their headless bodies, as the sidebar tests already do, rather than implicitly calling user32. Existing assertions, including Reduce Motion overrides, are unchanged. One AboutUpdateViewsRecordTests in-flight check opts into a complete loopback HTTP response with invalid JSON when the counter is polled; this retains the genuine request, disabled button, single-request count, checker failure and resulting UI checks, while preventing HttpClient from retrying an unanswered closed socket on this host. Other counter uses retain their original behavior. Independent review found the two production/parser issues above, then confirmed the fixes and reviewed these harness changes without weakening assertions.

7. Verification (Linux headless, .NET SDK 10.0.401, PowerShell 7.5.4, Avalonia 12.1.2): tests were written and run before implementation; the refusal/retention/offer tests and subsequent review regressions failed for their intended gaps. Final touched App slice: 382 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; Core package-script plus Traceability slice: 15 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; solution-wide Traceability: 3 tests in each of App/Core/UI/Services, all 12 passed. Commands: dotnet build Marrow.sln --no-restore -p:EnableWindowsTargeting=true -warnaserror --nologo -v minimal; dotnet test tests/Marrow.App.Tests/Marrow.App.Tests.csproj -p:EnableWindowsTargeting=true --filter '(FullyQualifiedName~WhatsNewTests|FullyQualifiedName~ReleaseNotes|FullyQualifiedName~UpdateChecker|FullyQualifiedName~AboutUpdateViews|FullyQualifiedName~UpdatesSettingsPage|FullyQualifiedName~UpdatePill|FullyQualifiedName~UpdatePopover|FullyQualifiedName~MarrowUpdateItem|FullyQualifiedName~AppUpdaterVelopackHandoff|FullyQualifiedName~AppUpdaterVelopackInstall|FullyQualifiedName~AppUpdaterApplyDownloaded|FullyQualifiedName~Traceability)&FullyQualifiedName!~Native'; the Core filter is '(FullyQualifiedName~PackageWindowsScriptTests|FullyQualifiedName~Traceability)&FullyQualifiedName!~Native'; the solution filter is 'FullyQualifiedName~Traceability&FullyQualifiedName!~Native'. The solution build has zero warnings and errors. Runs use en_US.UTF-8 and MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ue6-test-data. A test-host-only /tmp ICU adapter forwards Windows-named unversioned imports to the real system ICU 76 exports, without changing product code or returning canned values. TRX evidence is under /tmp/ue6-test-results. Native backend tests are excluded as requested; there is no claim of live Windows installation verification. All updater calls use injected engines or controlled loopback fixtures. No vpk, signing, installer, release or upload command was run. This decision was appended as bytes; the entire pre-existing engineering_decisions.md prefix remains byte-exact.

8. Independent review fixes (2026-10-05, review head df5b8cff2363395472ed5a4be4ffc0ccdd2ae548): merged the review commit on top of e3866d044; both REVIEW_ test files remain byte-identical. All four reviewer cases failed first, alongside new offer-binding and empty-note regressions. The final release-note acceptance check now compiles the dependency-free Core ReleaseNotesParser source in memory with PowerShell Add-Type and requires a populated category from that parser. UpdateReleaseNotesDigest calls the same parser for its line/header/bullet/inline-markdown rules, then retains its original ordering, deduplication, rollup handling and cache behavior. Bold-only headers and arbitrary-length hash headers end sections exactly as the app does; Thanks cannot license a card. Existing stricter upstream-format checks (canonical titles, dash bullets, empty-emphasis refusal and fenced-example exclusion) remain. No native command, package or artifact is produced by preflight. The shared source uses C# 5 syntax and framework APIs for the documented Windows PowerShell 5.1 invocation; UE-T85 compiles that exact source at language version 5 and checks populated cards and bold Thanks boundaries. This is a compiler compatibility check on Linux, not a claim of running Windows PowerShell 5.1 here.

9. All offer surfaces now use UpdateReleaseNotesContent for the existing section cards or About's plain MarkdownView fallback, with the same size, padding and scrolling. Updates and the sidebar visibly explain empty/whitespace/missing metadata rather than silently dropping it. About keeps its existing per-version digest cache. UE-T79 covers section-ending headers in both packaging and extraction, with refusal before commands/output; UE-T78 covers visible empty-note diagnostics, and UE-T80 compares exact plain markdown from a real Marrow item with About on both surfaces. Original test assertions remain intact; the card-reading fixture additionally closes each popover and asserts dismissal so a subsequent read can reopen it.

10. Offer ownership: IMarrowUpdateOffer supplies the configured item's captured AvailableUpdate; IUpdatesRunner exposes only metadata matching its Marrow row's actual version. UpdateWhatsNew receives that runner and follows its Changed event, including Configure replacement/removal. It never reads UpdateChecker.Shared. MarrowUpdateItem captures its successful check's release, downloads that captured version and retains the downloaded metadata until restart. A background check replacing the checker offer cannot change the runner's displayed install target. While a package awaits restart, the item's latest version remains that downloaded version: there is one Restart Marrow target and no second per-row install with different notes. The next process checks for later versions. VelopackSelfUpdateEngine also refuses a feed result whose version differs from the requested version before downloading anything, with a diagnosis naming the requested version and asking for a fresh check; it never substitutes a newer package or replaces the pending downloaded asset on that refusal. UE-T77 tests a real item using a checker different from Shared and live Configure removal; T81 tests checker changes before download and pending restart; T82 excludes noninstalled/current rows despite a stale Shared offer; T83 runs Velopack's real manager with an injected in-process downloader against stale requested versions; T84 proves pending restart has one target. The legacy FakeUpdateItem fixture now models metadata by capturing matching injected defaults bytes at construction, with an explicitly settable offer. No singleton or real updater network is consulted by that fixture. Reviewer files and every baseline assertion are unchanged.

11. The contract's independent reviewer found the stale Velopack substitution and pending-restart second-install gaps during these fixes; both gained failing regressions before their production repairs. The C# 5 compiler regression also failed before the compatible shared-source rewrite. These repairs supersede item 3's statement that the additional offers follow the checker: they now follow the runner's actual item. Native/update/sign/release/upload commands remain prohibited and were not run.

12. Core and solution filters remain as in item 7. Build: dotnet build Marrow.sln --no-restore -p:EnableWindowsTargeting=true -warnaserror --nologo -v minimal. Tests: dotnet test <project-or-solution> --no-build --no-restore -p:EnableWindowsTargeting=true --filter <filter>. Environment is the same .NET 10.0.401/PowerShell 7.5.4/Linux ICU adapter/en_US.UTF-8/temp data environment recorded above. ## ED-361

2026-10-05. CZ-8 (Customization C5, the Speech section), branch `cloud/f-cz-8` from `origin/codex/verify-cz-7a` with `origin/claude/verify-terminal-20261001` (76a61a4e2: VT-13, VT-14) merged. Source: customization-SPEC CZ-11.1, CZ-3.5.3, CZ-T80 to T82, CZ-T98; OD-0097, OD-0099, OD-0076.

1. **The merge.** One conflict, `CzMenuButton.Select`: the base split a `Show(id)` out of it (a mirror that emits nothing, also while dimmed); VT-13 made the pick clear the shown `valueText`. Both kept: `Show` clears `valueText` and `Select` calls `Show`, then raises the event and closes. Nothing else conflicted.
2. **The words.** Core `CzSpeechText` holds every word (`Speech`, `Speech model`, `Language`, `Engine`, `Change`) and the three detail rules, so the page and the tests read one place. The model name is `ModelCatalog.ModelName` (voice-SPEC V-9.6); the language names are `VoiceLanguage`'s. The Language row is the spec's table, not the design's `voLangSummary` (which follows the default whenever `S.lang` is Auto-detect): an explicit `auto` says `Auto-detect: Whisper works out the language` under every default, a picked code its name, and only null (or a code outside the list, which reads as null as V-16.2 says) follows the default: A that line, B `Auto-detect, named in the pill while you speak`, C `{Language} (from Windows)` (A's line when Windows' language is not in the list), D `Asked on first use`. Windows' language is `CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture.Name`, as the Spoken language row reads it.
3. **ENGINEERING DECISION: the local engine with no model selected shows an empty Speech model detail.** `voiceTyping.model` can be null (the Voice typing page marks nothing in use) and the spec gives no words for it; none is invented, so the row shows its title and the capsule only. UNRESOLVED for the owner: a sentence for that state, if one is wanted.
4. **The section.** `SpeechSections` (`src/Marrow.App/Port/Settings/`): a `CzSection` headed `Speech` over three `CzRow`s, each with a `CzCapsuleButton("Change", link: true)` (the capsule and its chevron are CZ-12.4's). `Change` sets `SettingsNavigation.Shared.RequestedPage = SettingsPage.VoiceTyping`, the page change the Voice typing page's `Customization` button makes the other way. The page puts it first in `Rest`, after the sticky container, and refreshes it in the same tracked read that already watches `VoiceTyping` and `VoiceOrb`; a changed detail crossfades through `CzRow.SetDetail` (OD-0076), the first placement is the row's own text.
5. **The pin release (CZ-T82): the structure is built, the behaviour is not, and cannot be here.** The branch has no sticky stage: CZ-6 is not in this base (`CustomizationStage` says it scrolls with the page for now, and `CZ-T60` to `T68` have no code). What CZ-8 owes CZ-3.5.3 is that Speech sits after the container the pin covers, so it is the first section under nothing. That is built and tested: Speech is not in `Sticky`, is `Rest`'s first child, and starts at or below Working dots' bottom. The release point itself (`y > H_c - h_pin`, Working dots' bottom meeting the block's bottom) is CZ-6's to implement with `Rest` as the thing that scrolls freely; CZ-T64 stays open until CZ-6 lands.
6. **Test-first.** Both new test classes were written before any code and failed to compile (`CzSpeechText` and `CustomizationSettingsPage.Speech` missing); with the code the 22 text cases and the 6 page tests passed. One mutation (Speech put into `Sticky` instead of `Rest`) failed every page test as it should; the code was restored.
7. **Environment.** The dotnet SDK was absent from the container; `apt-get update` then `apt-get install dotnet-sdk-10.0` (10.0.112) gave one, because `dot.net` and `builds.dotnet.microsoft.com` are refused by the egress policy. App tests need `MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR` set to a throwaway folder (R-TEST-9).
8. **Existing tests changed, with the reason.** `CustomizationPageTests.The_page_holds_the_stage_then_Style_then_the_style_sections_in_order` and `CustomizationDotsRowsTests.The_section_sits_at_the_end_of_the_sticky_container_after_the_style_sections` each asserted that `Rest` is empty; it now holds the Speech section, so each asserts that `Rest` holds that section alone. No other expectation was touched.
9. **Runs (Linux, `-p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=false -p:EnableWindowsTargeting=true`, `MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR` a throwaway folder).** New tests: 28 in 2 classes (`CzSpeechTextTests` 22 cases, `CustomizationSpeechSectionTests` 6), all passing, as are `CustomizationDotsRowsTests`, the amended page test and both `TraceabilityTests` (App 3, Core 3). The slice `Port.Settings`, `Port.Voice` and `TraceabilityTests` with `&FullyQualifiedName!~Native`: 419 tests, 389 passed, 30 failed before the test fix of item 8 removed one; the base `0cea7df6` fails 29 of 391 in the same slice, and the 29 are the same tests (no new failure from CZ-8): the Customization row tests that need the embedded Inter face (`Could not create glyphTypeface`, a headless-on-Linux limit the new tests avoid by priming it as `VoiceRowsContext` does), `SettingsRise`/`SettingsEscape`, `ComposerPreviewPixels` and one `SpeechModelController` test. They are Windows-only until run on Windows. A whole-project App run on Linux failed 1523 tests on the same kind of cause (timeline, Hydra and update tests) and was not compared.
10. **Not done, and why.** The pin's release behaviour (item 5: CZ-6 is not in the base; CZ-T64 stays open). The empty Speech model detail for no selected model (item 3: no words in the spec). Nothing ran on a real Windows window.
11. **Review fix round (codex/review-cz-8, `b6144317`, verdict FIX FIRST; `REVIEW_CustomizationSpeechTests` merged unchanged, 9 cases, red first: all 9 failed on their assertions).**
   - (1) **Windows' language.** `SpeechSections` reads `WindowsDisplayLanguage.Current()`, as the Voice typing page does (voice-SPEC V-7.14), instead of the managed UI culture; the two pages can no longer disagree. This corrects item 2's last sentence, which took the Spoken language row's reading as the source. ENGINEERING DECISION: nothing re-reads it when Windows' language changes while the page is open (the Voice typing page does not either); the next refresh does.
   - (2) **Names.** Each `Change` capsule's accessible name is its row's title (`Speech model`, `Language`, `Engine`) and its help text the row's detail, kept in step on every refresh (CZ-15); the visible label stays `Change`.
   - (3) **The capsule's fill eases (`CzButton`, shared).** The fill is a `CzColor`: a hover or press eases over 0.12 s `ease` (DESIGN gen.py:298); a theme change eases over `AppearanceTurn.Curve` (0.32 s) where the tree turns over, else it lands at once; the first fill and Reduce Motion land at once. Every `CzButton` that fills with the `cap` tokens (menu buttons, Auto, Advanced, Change, Check) now eases the same way; the ones with `ChromeFill = false` are unchanged. NOT DONE: the capsule's label colour on a theme change and `CzCrossfadeText`'s foreground on a theme change still switch in one frame (the review names them; the reviewed oracles do not test them).
   - (4) **Reduce Motion while a transition runs.** `CzMotion.Tick` stills every moving number at the next frame when `Still` has become true (`Settle`), so all Cz controls, not Speech alone, stop mid-flight when the preference is turned on.
   - **Existing tests, with the reason.** `CustomizationSpeechSectionTests.CZ_T81_Three_link_rows...` asserted the capsule's name was `Change`, the defect of finding 2; it now asserts the row's title (the visible label is still `Change`). `CZ_T81_Language_follows...` set the managed culture to script Windows' language; it scripts `WindowsDisplayLanguage.Source` instead with the same values and every assertion kept. No other expectation changed.
   - **Runs (Linux).** `REVIEW_CustomizationSpeechTests` 9 of 9; the slice `Port.Settings`, `Port.Voice`, `TraceabilityTests` (!~Native) 428 tests, 399 passed, 29 failed, the same 29 as the base `0cea7df6` (font, `user32`, `icu` and `SpeechModelController` cases), none new; `Marrow.UI.Tests` Cz and Settings slice 23 of 23. A whole UI project run was not completed (its markdown link tests fail on this host before it reaches the end).
12. **The "Not done" items of item 11, closed (test-first: `CzThemeInkTests` failed 3 of 4 on the old code, `SpeechDisplayLanguageChangeTests` did not compile without the seam; both pass now).**
   - (a) **Text colours ease on a theme change.** `CzButton` paints its label through an eased `CzColor` (`ApplyInk`, the capsule's label line overrides it): on a theme change 0.32 s `AppearanceTurn.Curve` where the tree turns over, else at once; the first colour and Reduce Motion land at once. As with the fill, only a button with `ChromeFill` true does this (menu buttons, Change, Check, Auto, Advanced); `ChromeFill = false` buttons keep painting their own text. `CzCrossfadeText` keeps one eased ink for all its blocks: a theme change eases it the same way, a block made mid-turnover wears the colour the turnover has reached (tested), and setting `Secondary` re-targets at once (a change of kind, not a transition). Every row detail and the Voice typing privacy line gain this. NOT DONE (still listed): menu items, radio buttons and any other `CzButton` that sets its own foreground after `base.Refresh()` still switch in one frame; the review's oracles name the capsule and the crossfade text only.
   - (b) **The display language follows Windows while a page is open.** `WindowsDisplayLanguage` (shared helper, `Port/Voice`) gains the change source `Changes` (`Ambient<Func<Action, IDisposable>>`; the default listens to the static `Changed` event, raised by `Notify()`) and `Watch(page, refresh)` (listens while the page is in a window, stops when it leaves; tested: one listener live, none after the window closes). The Customization page calls `Speech.Apply` through it; the Voice typing page shares the helper, so its Language row (menu value, check and detail) now refreshes through the same call (tested with `Notify()`). NOT BUILT, UNRESOLVED: the Windows side that calls `Notify()` (a settings-change message to the main window, or a locale watcher); until it is wired nothing raises the event in the shipped app, so a changed display language is read at the next refresh (a setting change or a page visit), as before. Windows applies a new display language at the next sign-in, so the owner may judge the hook not worth building.
   - **Runs (Linux).** `CzThemeInkTests` 4 and `SpeechDisplayLanguageChangeTests` 3 pass, with `REVIEW_CustomizationSpeechTests` (9) and `CustomizationSpeechSectionTests`: 22 of 22. Slice `Port.Settings`, `Port.Voice`, `TraceabilityTests` (!~Native): 435 tests, 406 passed, 29 failed, the same 29 as the base. `Marrow.UI.Tests` Cz and Settings slice 23 of 23.
## ED-362

2026-10-05. ENGINEERING DECISIONS for SK-11a (Claude WU-6, DL-11, DL-12), OD-0099 skills amendments and OD-0103. The owner's cloud-worker brief authorizes tests-first commits, this append and pushing only codex/f-sk-11a; it overrides the historical no-commit/protected-file rules. No ledger status changes.

1. **Scope and generation owner.** ClaudeSession alone changes among existing provider files. New helper types live one per file in Services/Port/Skills/Providers; all tests/fixtures/evidence are under Services.Tests. Merged staging 32dca53f initially, then 7993466e after the owner's continuation (merge bc20daab); both sides of engineering_decisions conflicts retained append-only. SK-9's staging version uses IGenerationStore (ED-326), so a caller can supply generations owned by SkillsPipeline without a second SkillsStore. SK-5, SK-9, SK-6 and SK-10 are unchanged by this unit. Like SK-11d's ED-330, app composition is outside this provider unit: SK-16/DL-19 passes a factory bound to the actual stable Marrow chat id and downloaded/enabled item snapshot to ClaudeSession, and a listing-probe factory to Handshake. A null factory/null result is the existing no-skills path. No real user folders are scanned here.
2. **Flags and identity.** PLAN 2.2, WU-6 and ONDEMAND 4.1 supply --plugin-dir, gated on the existing --help probe; Start adds the verified generation folder and every Generation.PluginFolders entry separately, each path one argv element. Handshake uses an SK-9 listing lease and the same enabled plugin-root descriptors/switches. A failed help result cannot enable the plugin flag. Empty probes do not add a help call. No CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS, sync variable, read permission, --add-dir or extra RPC field is introduced. The read-only Read(//c/.../**) rule versus --add-dir remains WU-11's live decision; this unit has no evidence selecting either.
3. **DL-11 versus DL-6.** Literal raw Mac environment equality and unconditional addons/bin on every child PATH cannot both hold. The owner's explicit 'every provider child environment carries addons\bin ... and nothing else changes' is applied to Claude's help child, session child and Handshake child even with nothing installed, through the unchanged SK-6 ShimPath.ForChild and Storage.Root. This is the sole environment exception; all other key/value bytes stay unchanged. ED-330's conditional OpenCode PATH interpretation is not extended to Claude because this brief expressly requires every child. The byte-regression tests compare frozen existing-provider argv and JSON-lines RPC bytes exactly, and environment bytes after only the required DL-6 PATH envelope. They do not claim unmodified raw Mac PATH equality.
4. **Existing-code oracle and offline seams.** LegacyClaudeSession is a frozen copy of ClaudeSession at merge 74453a3e (original SHA-256 dd534bc6a4311792757a76c1f9cd719dcf24ac6b156fed7e9b8e00ec55d3b370). Only its class/namespace and transport/help seams change; a mechanical transformation comparison passed. The same async-flow-local transport/help seams drive both classes; production delegates to exactly StdioProcess and Shell.Run(--help, timeout 20). RecordingClaudeProcess has no process/network fallback and fixtures use nonexistent /offline executable paths. Captured RPC uses the existing JSONValue writer and LF framing. Tests cover empty Start (plain and configured), Handshake (no extra help), and allow/deny response bytes. Compilation/execution of this proof remains unverified in this worker; the frozen-source comparison is not substituted for it.
5. **Integrity, resume and leases.** Acquisition/whole-tree verification and per-turn verification run on the pool. Empty generations add no flags. Damaged launch/listing generations fail before provider spawn. ClaudeSkillProbe reacquires the same live SK-9 listing to verify against its trusted manifest, never hashes writable files into a new trust root. Session generation leases wait for actual process exit; stdout EOF, Stop or a failed initialize alone cannot release a root still read by a child. Installed Handshake terminates its child, then awaits WaitForExit before its listing lease ends; the empty probe retains its existing return timing. The exact moved-root line and per-turn changed-file notice come from PLAN 2.1, without new user-visible wording. Resume/GC/restart and held-root cases use the existing SK-9 coordinator, including staging's IGenerationStore seam; no generation/store implementation is modified.
6. **Normalized taps.** ONDEMAND 5.1-5.2 names stream-json assistant tool_use, user tool_result and control_request/can_use_tool. Complete assistant inputs, rather than partial content_block_start inputs, establish commands and skills; results are correlated by (parent_tool_use_id, tool id), then consumed once. Bash/PowerShell command results carry null exit code, the provider's is_error and the existing ToolText.Blocks output. Skill names lose their plugin prefix for the folder name; ordinary marrow:<name> entries carry the set id from SK-9's source-qualified metadata. This immutable name/id snapshot survives process exit for buffered transcript messages. Unknown/user/plugin namespaces do not get a guessed set id. Prose, malformed ids/inputs, unrelated tools, unmatched or duplicate results yield nothing. No request_tool is added (DL-14 belongs to SK-11f).
7. **Observer ordering and failures.** Collect normalized events before existing dispatch to preserve correlation during re-entry, then deliver them after the existing handler completes so a CommandHeld observer sees the registered permission request. Existing provider events and permission responses remain in their original order. Observer exceptions are isolated and exposed as LastSkillEventFailure; they cannot approve a request, fabricate success or prevent original protocol handling. User offer/download/resume orchestration remains SK-12/SK-16.
8. **Verification limits.** All three JSONL fixtures are Marrow-authored syntheses of the existing provider's documented fields, not live captures or vendor skill files. Every new test has Feature=SK-11a and a Rule trait. The independent static reviewer found no remaining definite API/compilation issue or required SK-11a discrepancy, and the suggested launch/initialize/listing failure tests were added. Linux build and filtered test commands both exit 127: dotnet is not installed. No SDK was fetched because the brief forbids network beyond the explicitly authorized Git operations. ENGINEERING DECISIONS, 2026-10-04, feature SK-11b "Codex" (BUILD-PLAN 2.5; ONDEMAND-PLAN DL-11 and DL-12 for Codex; skills-PLAN WU-7; research-loading 3.2; OD-0099 amendments).
