No ledger status is changed. Code: `src/Marrow.Services/Port/Skills/Providers/Codex*.cs` (one type per file) and the edit points marked PORT-ONLY (SK-11b) in `src/Marrow.Services/Providers/CodexSession.cs`; tests `tests/Marrow.Services.Tests/Port/Skills/Providers/` (Feature=SK-11b).

1. **Seam shape.** `CodexSession(SessionConfiguration, CodexSkillWiring? skills = null)`: the wiring (a chat's SK-9 `Generation`, SK-5 `StorePaths`, and the listing probe's `PublishedSkill`s) is an optional second constructor parameter, so `SessionConfiguration`/`ProviderSession.cs` (shared with SK-11a) stay untouched; null is the Mac's behaviour. The caller (SK-12 / DL-19, in `ThreadRuntime`) owns the generation's lease and disposes it at session end. `ListCommands` takes an optional `GenerationListing`; both new parameters are trailing and optional, so every existing call compiles unchanged.
2. **Connect (WU-7).** After `initialize` and the `initialized` notification, with wiring: `skills/list {cwds:[<session working directory>], forceReload:true}` then `skills/extraRoots/set {extraRoots:[<generation folder>]}`, on every connection (a reconnect or a second session sends its own). A `ListCommands` probe with a listing sends only `extraRoots/set` (it sends its own `skills/list` next). The `skills/list` reply is not used: the generation is built before the connection exists (SK-9's `Start` needs the clash snapshot first), so the call exists to follow WU-7's sequence and refresh Codex's cache. An RPC error reply to either call is ignored (Codex before 0.136.0 has no `extraRoots/set`); a failed transport is not swallowed and closes the connection like a failed `initialize`. A relative folder is refused before anything is sent (Codex answers -32600 to it). `skills/config/write` is never sent and `CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE` is never set (source-scan test); `clientInfo.name` stays "marrow".
3. **Listing path rewrite.** `CodexSkillPaths.Rewrite` is GenerationListing.ForChat's rule over the listing's skills as a snapshot (`PublishedSkill` records), because the listing lease is released after the probe while the slash list outlives it. A listed path of a skill the chat's generation no longer holds (switched off since the list was read) throws `InvalidOperationException` from the send, as `ForChat` does; no user-visible text is invented for it (UNRESOLVED: ThreadRuntime may want to turn it into a notice).
4. **Resume.** `thread/resume` parameters are the unchanged `ThreadParameters` plus `threadId`/`excludeTurns` (extracted into `ResumeParameters`, taking the already-built dictionary, so `ThreadParameters` is still read once). Only when `Generation.PreviousFolder` is set (the old chat folder was held, so the chat moved) the existing `developerInstructions` string gets `"\n\n"` + skills-PLAN 2.1's line appended; the key is `developerInstructions` because that is the key the existing code already sends (the plan's `developer_instructions` is the Rust field name). `thread/start` is never changed.
4a. **Always allow.** A command approval whose `acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment` decision holds, anywhere in its JSON, a string that contains `StorePaths.Views` (either slash, any case, and ending at a name boundary so `views-sibling` does not match) loses the "amend" option and its payload; Approve and Approve for session remain. The amendment's JSON shape is not assumed (all strings are scanned). Commands outside the root, and a session without wiring, are unchanged.
5. **PATH rule (DL-11).** `CodexChildEnvironment.Apply` is applied to the environment of every `codex app-server` launch in `Connect` (sessions and every static probe that connects): `ShimPath.ForChild(env, <data root>)`, so only `PATH` changes and `addons\bin` exists even when empty. The root comes from an `Ambient<CodexChildRoot>` whose default asks the bound `Storage.Root` (the app binds it at start-up, so production gets the rule with no App edit); an unbound `Storage` (tests, tools) is "not known" and returns the environment unchanged without a folder (fail closed, no exception). The registry's one-shot probes (`--version`, update, plan-limits reads through `Shell.Run`) are in `ProviderRegistry.cs`/`PlanLimits.cs`, shared files, and are not changed here (UNRESOLVED for the lead: SK-12 wiring or a later unit adds the same one-line `Apply` there if those children should carry `addons\bin`).
6. **Byte-identity method.** The hard rule (nothing installed means argv, environment and RPC bytes equal the Mac's) is proved on Linux against CodexSession's own members: `AppServerArguments` (`["app-server"]`), `InitializeParameters` (moved out of `Connect` verbatim; golden bytes in the original key order), `ThreadParameters` and the resume parameters byte-compared with and without wiring, `ResolveSkill` returning the same command object, approval options compared with and without wiring, and `Apply` returning the same dictionary when no root is known. The remaining proof, that `Start` really writes the same stdin lines and the same environment (initialize, initialized, thread/start, and PATH as the only changed variable), needs a process: the Windows-only stand-in tests (`CodexSessionUnchangedTests`, WindowsOnlyFact) record the real lines and a new `env-<n>.txt` dump (an additive line in `tests/fixtures/codex-cli/CodexStandIn.cs`, plus `CodexScript.LaunchEnvironment`). The only deliberate difference with nothing installed is the PATH insertion DL-11 itself requires.
7. **Taps (DL-12).** `CodexToolTaps` turns Codex JSON into SK-10's `ToolEvent`s: `item/commandExecution/requestApproval` gives `CommandHeld(command)`; `item/started` of a `userMessage` gives `SkillUsed(name, itemId)` for each content part `{type:"skill", name, path}` (the shape the port itself sends; ItemId is the SK-9 `PublishedSkill.Id` prefix when the path is a Marrow generation path, null for a user's own skill); `item/completed` of a `commandExecution` gives `CommandFinished(command, exitCode, IsError, aggregatedOutput)` with `IsError` true for status `failed` or `interrupted`; a `declined` command never ran and gives nothing. The command is the text the approval card shows (`ToolTitles.UnwrapShell`), nothing more is unwrapped, so a PowerShell wrapper such as `powershell -Command "..."` reaches the detector as written (UNRESOLVED: whether SK-10's tokenizer should look inside such a wrapper; no live Windows Codex transcript was available). An exit code outside int range wraps unchecked. `CodexSession.OnToolEvent` is the sink; a listener that throws is logged and ignored, and the existing `ProviderEvent`s are identical with and without a listener (test). Model-initiated skill use is not tapped: no Codex item type for it is documented in the formats this unit read (UNRESOLVED; ONDEMAND S1 names only `{type:"skill"}` items).
8. **Fixtures and trait ids.** The transcript is `tests/Marrow.Services.Tests/Port/Skills/Providers/Fixtures/codex-app-server-skills.jsonl`, hand-synthesized from the shapes CodexSession already parses; no live CLI was run. The traceability checker accepts only `Req`/`Rule`/`Decision`/`Spec`/`Feature` traits with fixed id patterns, so the tests carry `Feature=SK-11b`, `Rule=R-TEST-9|R-TEST-10` and `Spec=SK-T7` (WU-7), `SK-T11` (DL-11) or `SK-T12` (DL-12). (The SK-9 tests' `Rule` ids such as `DL-9-installed-enabled` already fail that checker's id test on this branch; not touched here.)
9. **Verification limits.** Linux (apt SDK 10.0.112, fresh /tmp MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR): see the report for the filtered run. `CodexSession` cannot start a process on Linux (`ProcessLauncher` is CreateProcessW) and `SlashCommand.CodexInput` needs the ICU shim (`icu.dll`), so three tests are Windows-only and were not run here: the two stand-in `Start` line/environment tests and the composed `CodexInput` skill part. No live Codex, no real model turn, no check of Codex's elevated Windows sandbox reading the generation (WU-11 / DL-20).

ENGINEERING DECISIONS, 2026-10-04, feature SK-11f "API providers" (WU-12 and DL-14). Authority: BUILD-PLAN 2.5 SK-11f; ONDEMAND 3.6, 4.1, 4.2, 5.1 S4, 5.2, 5.5 R4, DL-11, DL-12,
DL-14; skills-PLAN 2.7, 3.3 (native row), Q17, WU-12; research-loading 3.10 and 5; OD-0099 amendments (progressive disclosure; Invoke A). Only
`src/Marrow.Services/Providers/OpenAICompatibleSession.cs` and new files under `src/Marrow.Services/Port/Skills/Providers/` changed. SK-5 and SK-9 are untouched. No ledger status changed.

1. **Seam, default off.** `OpenAICompatibleSession` gains two public settable members, `SkillTools` (a `NativeSkillTools`) and `OnToolEvent` (an `Action<ToolEvent>`), both null by default.
   With both null, and with a `SkillTools` that has nothing to offer, every byte the session sends equals the Mac's (see 10). Building the `Generation` (SK-9), the offer flow, and the
   user's own-skills switch, and setting these two members when a session is created, is the wiring of SK-12 and SK-16 (ProviderRegistry and the app are not this unit's files):
   NOT DONE here, so the feature is inert in the running app until that wiring exists. The caller keeps the `Generation` alive for the session and disposes it after.
2. **Catalogue block.** Words (mine; the plan gives none): one header line `Skills (call use_skill with a skill's name to read its instructions):`, then one line `<name>: <description>` per
   skill, exactly SK-9's `PublishedSkill.Listing`, so the block costs what SK-9's budget counts (name + description + 3). The header sits inside the 10% margin `GenerationBudget.Room`
   keeps back. The block goes between the policy (Hydra, anti-slop) and the project's own guidelines, so the guidelines stay last as `SystemPrompt()` already says. It is null (and
   the prompt unchanged) when there is nothing to list. Explicit-only skills are never listed (`screenshot`, `yeet`, `review-agent`). The user's own skills come first and shadow a
   Marrow skill of the same name (compared with `GenerationFilters.Normalize`), even if the caller forgot to pass them to SK-9 as the existing set. The block is rebuilt from an
   immutable generation, so every turn's system prompt is identical (`RefreshSystemPrompt` runs each turn). WU-12 says Marrow's descriptions are "shortened or dropped first" at the cap:
   SK-9 drops and never shortens; nothing here shortens either (UNRESOLVED, SK-9's call).
3. **use_skill.** Offered only while the block has at least one line. Schema: `name` (string, required), `file` (string, optional); description text is mine. `file` absent or `SKILL.md` returns
   `Skill folder: <absolute folder>\n\n<SKILL.md text>` (research-loading section 5 step 3: the body and the folder path, because run_command, not the file tools, runs a skill's scripts);
   any other `file` returns that file's text alone and is not a skill use. Confinement is SK-9's `Generation.ReadReference` (relative slash path, `..` and drive and absolute forms refused, the
   file must be pinned in the generation, bytes re-hashed on every read) and, for the user's own skills, `RequireRelative` plus `DiskUserSkillFiles` (no link at any step, under the skill's
   root, strict UTF-8). Error texts (mine, in the `Error: ` style of the built-in tools): `Error: a skill name is required.`, `Error: unknown skill <name>.` (also for a skill that is off,
   explicit-only or not installed, so nothing is revealed), `Error: the file path must be a relative path inside the skill's folder.`, and `Error: <SK-9 message>` for a file that is not pinned,
   not text or changed on disk. The tool needs no approval (it only reads Marrow's own pinned copy) and its row is `ToolCall.Kind.Other`, titled `Skill · <name>` (U+00B7, as the MCP rows;
   `Skill` alone for a missing name). The row's output is capped at 4000 characters as read_file's is; the model gets the full text. Who invoked a skill (the model here, the user by a slash
   pick) is the Invoke A row's business in the UI unit; this tool only produces the model's.
4. **request_tool.** Schema `name` and `reason`, both required strings; description text is mine. It is offered only while `IToolRequestOffer.Available` (something from the catalogue is
   installed): that is how the DL-11 hard rule ("with nothing installed, every argv, environment variable and RPC message equals today's") holds for this tool too, at the price that a
   user with nothing installed gets the offer from the failed-command and held-command signals (S2, S3) and not from the model's own request (S4) until something is. If the lead prefers
   the tool always present, the single change is `Available`, and the request bytes then differ from the Mac's by one tool definition. The name must be a catalogue item id or a program a
   catalogue item provides (`ToolRequestCatalogue.Contains`, the detector's own lookup, tested on the embedded catalogue); anything else is `Error: <name> is not in the catalogue.` and
   the user is never asked. A blank name is `Error: a tool name is required.`; a missing reason is passed on as empty. The tool awaits `IToolRequestOffer.Ask` (the offer flow, SK-12, which
   shows the card and downloads only on the user's yes; this unit has no downloader and no reference to one) and returns `installed at <path>` or `declined`, the plan's words. The wait is
   cancelled by the turn's own cancellation (a stopped turn ends Interrupted and the model is not called again). No approval request: the offer's yes is the consent, in every mode,
   Plan included (no project file changes). A request still in flight when the last item is removed reaches its offer; a new call after that is the unknown tool again.
5. **The user's own skills (Q17).** `NativeUserSkills(root, enabled, files)` reads only `<root>` (the caller passes `~/.agents/skills`; the plan names that folder and no other for this
   provider). With `enabled` false (the plan's default) it never lists or reads anything, and `List`, `Existing` and `Read` answer empty or null; a fake file system records no access in the
   test. With it on, the folder is listed once per session and kept; an entry whose frontmatter is unusable or whose name breaks the Agent Skills name rule is skipped, the first of two same names
   wins, and a folder that cannot be read lists nothing instead of failing the session. `Existing()` is the snapshot SK-9 takes for clashes and for the budget (user entries counted first, whole).
   Deciding the switch's value belongs to the Skills page and the wiring.
6. **Taps (DL-12, native).** The session emits SK-10's own types through `OnToolEvent`: `CommandHeld(command)` when run_command is about to wait for the user (non-empty command,
   not interrupted, `RequiresApproval`), before the approval event; `CommandFinished(command, exitCode, exitCode != 0, output)` when the command ran and the turn was not stopped (output as the

   CLI, fail closed; `ED-309` for the PATH rule); the plan row and WU names are in the test names and comments. `TraceabilityTests.Every_test_names_...` already fails at the base commit

## ED-367

2026-10-05. Unit SK-12, BUILD-PLAN 2.5; ONDEMAND DL-13, 5.3-5.5 and S1; OD-0099 and OD-0103. Owner-authorized first-release deviation from the pinned Mac: optional-download offers, provider approval denial reason, request_tool completion, and a Marrow timeline notice sent as a user message. No upstream parity status is promoted by this unit.

1. One main-actor SkillsOfferFlow belongs to a ThreadRuntime. Normalized provider taps and command approvals feed the SK-10 detector; both approval/event orders are supported. Requested items merge into the current card in catalogue dependency order. Offered items are remembered for the chat; declines are written through the injected SK-7 state boundary before provider replies. TermsRequired keeps the card Asked without fetching bytes; the terms UI and host registration remain SK-13/SK-14.
2. R1 releases only a current session epoch's still-held approval, using its actual Approve/Decline option. Claude's optional three-argument ResolveApproval carries S1's denial byte-equal; other protocols retain their existing two-argument shape when no reason field exists. Done requires every requested absolute verified path, followed by routing publication. The continuation slots are declared catalogue title, pin and executable; missing slots fail closed. S1 words are never paraphrased. Internal boundary exceptions are diagnostics, not new product copy.
3. R2 appends one generated prompt to the existing queue, without dispatching a Hydra head or interrupting the current turn. It drains after completion, failure or interruption; ordinary user prompts retain their existing failure behavior. R3 uses the same next-turn path when idle and does not touch the draft. A task-local marker identifies the generated timeline Notice, so an identical user-authored message remains a User item. R4 waits on the offer and returns the existing installed-at/declined tool result in the same turn; model requests never also enqueue a continuation, including canceled waiters.
4. The checked bridge prepares the entire card before SK-3 starts a combined download, preserving actual byte totals, then invokes SK-4 and the host's explicit publication callback while the install reservation is held. It refuses missing pins or incomplete catalogue inputs before any plan/download. Internal preparation methods cannot be called across assemblies. The host supplies installers, state/shim publication and the shared service lifetime; there is no implicit network fallback. Existing confirmed transfers may be attached without another download. Attached listener cancellation does not cancel the owner; owner cancellation returns the card to Asked. Failed transfers are removed for Retry, retaining SK-3's verified local files/.part behavior. Successful results remain cached for the shared service lifetime; removal/restart invalidation belongs to SK-16 wiring.
5. Cancel increments an operation revision before canceling the downloader; late progress/completion cannot resume a task. A new need during an active download joins the card but requires a subsequent Yes if that item was not in the confirmed set. Download failure preserves the backend's S1 reason and leaves Retry available. Continuation strings are validated before releasing held approvals or same-turn waiters.
6. Offline tests bind all HTTP to an in-memory handler that refuses unknown URLs, installer locking to a fixture, and publication to a fixture callback. ThreadRuntime's incidental Git probes use an async-local Shell test boundary; any unexpected command fails before process creation. The default production Shell path is unchanged. New fixture types live under each project's Fixtures directory. Tests' assertions were not weakened: merged SK-11a needed ValueList construction and main-actor pumping compile repairs; its invalid Rule citations became Feature plus Rule traits. SK-11e's unnumbered ED-NEW Decision citation remains a comment because Traceability accepts only numbered Decision IDs. The meta-tests themselves are unchanged.
7. Merge ledgers keep their existing byte sequences and mixed CRLF/LF endings. The cloud SK-5 decision entry displaced during the five-way ledger conflict resolution was restored byte-exact at the end before this entry. Evidence records original base-line preservation and merge-side added-line preservation. All five finished units are ancestry of codex/f-sk-12; no staging/base branch is pushed.
8. Verification is Linux/.NET 10 with filters ending &FullyQualifiedName!~Native. Windows-only native execution is excluded as requested. The local Windows tunnel is offline (not seen for 300 seconds), so Windows ICU-dependent continuation/draft assertions and legacy Ledger Windows-path cases cannot be verified here. No platform test expectation is changed to fit Linux. The pinned E:/Droppy reference checkout is absent, so Gate A cannot establish source parity here. SK-14 card rendering, SK-13 host/terms binding, SK-16 cross-surface/restart wiring and DL-20 live artifact/provider checks remain their own units; no packaging, signing, publishing or installer was run.

## ED-368

2026-10-05. Unit SK-16 (`cloud/f-sk-16`, from `claude/verify-terminal-20261001` 76a61a4e2 with `claude/review-sk-15` (SK-15, with SK-13) and `codex/f-sk-14` (SK-14, on SK-12 and the SK-11 provider units) merged). BUILD-PLAN row SK-16, skills-ONDEMAND-PLAN DL-19 (its list is the acceptance list: Settings and offers share one download per item, an offer attaches to a Settings download in progress and the reverse, progress in both places, an app restart during a download resumes from the `.part` on the next Download press and never on its own), OD-0099 (the amendments of 2026-10-04: the "Download it yourself" fallback, Cancel, Pause/Resume), OD-0100 (the Skills and tools rows), ED-326 (6)(a), ED-NEW-f-sk-13 items 4 and 8, ED-354 items 3 and 9, ED-367, ED-308 and ED-343 (the Updates hook). Nothing here downloaded from a real source, ran a CLI, an installer or Velopack, or packaged anything: every test uses a fresh folder under MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR, scripted seams or SK-0's loopback https fake with the guarded handler, and the fakes that fail closed.
1. **The pipeline's first install (`SkillsPipeline.InstallAsync(id, progress, ct)`, ED-326 (6)(a)).** SK-3's download seam, then SK-4's installer, then the binding seam, committed to state.json as Installed; it returns the folder. It mirrors `UpdateAsync` step for step (the same checkpoints, the same verification of the installed tree against the trusted descriptor, the same prepared route before the one commit). It refuses, before any byte is requested and with nothing written: an item not in the catalogue, one installed already (update or repair it), one with no complete pin, one whose terms are owed (`PipelineTermsRequiredException`), one that needs an item that is not installed, and unbound seams ("Pipeline seams are not bound."). A cancel or a failure leaves the item not installed, with the temporary trees collected; the download keeps what it fetched. ENGINEERING DECISION: nothing about a download in flight is written to state.json, so a restart finds the item not installed and the `.part` on disk, and nothing resumes by itself (DL-19). `FetchingBound` says whether both seams are bound, `InstalledFolder(id)` the folder an Installed or UpdateAvailable item is routed to, and `Changed` is raised after an install, update, repair (when it repaired), remove or reset has finished, outside the pipeline's locks (an observer's exception cannot undo a commit).
2. **One download per item (`SkillsDownloads`, `Marrow.Services.Port.Skills.Fetch`; `SkillsHost.Downloads`).** The one place a first download starts from. An item asked for while its download runs joins it, whoever asks, is told where it is at once (the last report is replayed) and sees every later report. ENGINEERING DECISIONS: (a) an asker that leaves (its token is cancelled) stops waiting and leaves the transfer to the others; when the last asker has left the transfer is cancelled and what it fetched stays for a later try (ONDEMAND 3.2). (b) The page's Cancel stops the download for everyone who asked (`Stop`): an offer's card that was waiting on it returns to Asked, which is SK-12's rule for an owner's cancel; Pause/Resume of Download all and a card's own cancel only leave. (c) An item that needs items not installed fetches them first, each its own shared download, and its progress is one bar across the need and the item weighted by their pinned bytes (an item with no size weighs one byte), never going back. (d) A failure reaches every asker and frees the item, so the next ask is a new download (Retry). (e) An item that is here is not downloaded again; its folder is given back. (f) `Available` is the seams being bound; `CanFetch(item)` also needs a complete pin for the item and every need not installed; an item that cannot be fetched fails with `FirstInstallUnavailableException`, whose message is SK-15's existing string (`LibraryWords.DownloadsUnavailable`): no new string. (g) `Running(id)` and `Watch(changed)` let any surface see a download another surface started.
3. **Settings and the offers over it.** `SkillsFirstInstall : IFirstInstall` (the Settings pages' seam; `HostLibraryBackend` uses it by default when the host's seams are bound, otherwise it keeps `FailClosedFirstInstall`, whose tests are unchanged) and `SkillsOfferInstalls : ISkillsOfferDownload` (`SkillsHost.OfferDownloads`): the card's items are shared downloads; the card's progress is the sum of the items' pinned bytes done (Downloading) until every item's bytes are in (Checking, the offer's "checking" state), and it returns each item's installed folder as the verified absolute path. `Attach` joins only an item whose download is running and otherwise fails closed with SK-12's own "No existing download is bound.". `IFirstInstall.IsAvailable` (a default member, true; false for the seam that fails closed), `ISkillsLibraryBackend.FetchingAvailable`, `Fetching(id)`, `WatchFetching(changed)` and `CancelFetching(id)` (default members, so every scripted backend still compiles), and `LibraryController.FetchingAvailable`. The controller shows a download another surface started as a Downloading row with the progress both share, redraws on its changes, and its Cancel stops it. ENGINEERING DECISION: SK-15's pages disable nothing when fetching is unavailable (their tests press Download with the seam that fails closed and expect the row to fail with the one message), so there was no disabled control to enable; the flag is exposed for the pages and nothing else reads it yet.
4. **Production seams (`SkillsProductionSeams.WithDownloads`, `CatalogueInstallPlans`, `DownloaderLicenceText`).** `SkillsStartup.Bind` now composes `SkillsHostOptions.Production().WithDownloads(dataRoot)` (`Production()` itself is unchanged: SkillsHostProductionTests still pin its null seams). The download seam is `PipelineDownloadSource` over the one `Downloader` (the catalogue's host list, part folder `addons\downloads`). ENGINEERING DECISIONS: (a) a skill set or plugin at one commit is fetched file by file from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<pin>/<path>` (ONDEMAND 3.2) with each path escaped, each file held to its pinned length and hash; the licence file comes from the item's own pinned licence URL; (b) the verified inputs wait under `addons\downloads\items\<id>` and are deleted when the binding is made; (c) the install gives no spare projections (SK-9 builds each chat's generation itself; a spare is only a speed-up and nothing supplies one yet); the store folder is `<id>@<pin8>`; (d) the route has no shims (a set provides no executable); (e) the licence text is fetched through the same downloader from the pinned licence URL, to a temporary file that is deleted after it is read, and the terms step checks it again. (f) UNRESOLVED, fail closed with the one unavailable message: an item the catalogue holds no install parameters for (a tool, a Python set or a Node set: Python embed options, wheels, node packages, msi layout; SK-1's schema has no field for them, ED-NEW-f-sk-13 item 8) and one at per-skill pins (no single commit). A file that is none of the pinned inputs is refused with `DownloadMessages.Mismatch` ("The file didn't match its checksum.") and nothing is written. ENGINEERING DECISION: a service that is running an update is left alone and reads the new set at the next change; before the launch has configured the service a change does nothing. The default of the hook stays empty (UE-4's test).

(c) No real download, pin, installer, provider chat or live look at the pages was run (DL-20). (d) The Minimize pill and popover (OD-0099 Minimize A) and the Add button with its sheet are not part of this row.
9. **Tests.** Services `Skills.Fetch` (43): PipelineFirstInstallTests 13 (the pipeline), SkillsDownloadsTests 9 (one download per item, leaving, failure, needs, availability), SkillsOfferInstallsTests 7 (both directions, Attach, cancel, the host's seam), HostLibraryBackendFetchTests 7 (the backend and controller over the shared downloads), ProductionSeamsTests 7 (the loopback fake: raw paths, restart and resume with Range, the manual file, the plans, the licence, the options). Fixtures `FetchRig` and `LoopbackRig` (Services). App: `SkillsUpdateRowsTests` 4 and `SkillsStartupDownloadsTests` 2 (the hook, the refresh, the composition, the order in `Program.Main` from its IL). Each new test was seen failing against a stub of what it proves before the code was written (the first-install and Fetch types were stubs that throw; the Updates refresh was also checked by removing its call). No existing test, expectation or trait was changed except the merge repair below.

Repair, not a weakening: where both sides counted the sidebar the derived form (`SettingsSidebar.Pages("").Count`, the titles taken from the pages) was kept; `SettingsNewPagesTests` now lists Plugins and Skills as ready with the other new pages (the IsReady table, the factory, the search finding both by title), and its helper for the old expected order was removed with its last use. 11. **Review of SK-16 (`codex/review-sk-16` 2698c9eed, FIX FIRST, ten findings, 17 failing REVIEW_ cases): merge.** The first delivery merged an older SK-15 line. `codex/f-sk-15` at c7526e100 (the reviewed SK-15 state) is merged in: its four review-test files (`LibraryPageReviewTests`, `LibraryReviewTests`, `SkillSwitchReviewTests`, `LibraryBackendReviewTests`) are back unchanged, with its reviewed wording, its round-up of a blocking space requirement and its `CanFetch` guards; the review branch's four `REVIEW_Sk16*Tests.cs` files and its report are merged unchanged. `SettingsNewPagesTests` takes SK-15's stricter reviewed form. ED item 3 above said SK-15 disabled nothing; that was wrong, and it is withdrawn: SK-15's controls are disabled while unbound, which is the reviewed requirement.
12. **Unbound downloads (finding 1).** `ISkillsLibraryBackend.CanFetch` (SK-15's) is the one flag: `HostLibraryBackend.CanFetch` is `Installs.IsAvailable`, `LibraryController.FetchingAvailable` reads it, and the duplicate flag on the interface is removed (`HostLibraryBackend.FetchingAvailable` stays as a name for it). While unbound Download, Retry and Download all are disabled, Download and Continue admit nothing (no row is queued, nothing is written as a failure) and the page says why; the reason now sits in the action's own line (the action's controls are the line's children). The first delivery's test `With_the_seams_unbound_a_press_fails_the_row_with_the_one_unavailable_message_and_nothing_is_fetched` asserted the opposite of the review's required behaviour and is replaced by `With_the_seams_unbound_a_press_changes_nothing_on_the_page_and_fetches_nothing` (the one existing assertion that had to change; everything else is kept).
13. **No lock is held across a callback (findings 2, 3 and 5).** `FetchFlight` calls no listener under its lock; every report carries a sequence number and each listener keeps what it has been given last, so a replay for a late joiner never arrives after a newer report and a callback may read the flight or `Downloads` from another thread. A flight also keeps the own progress of each item of its chain (`ReportPart`, passed up through the needs). `SkillsOfferInstalls` counts the card's bytes over the DISTINCT items (the card's items and the needs they share, each once; an item already here counts as done, so the card reaches Checking when every byte is in whether or not an item was installed before), follows each item's own part rather than its chain-wide fraction, calls the caller's callback outside its lock in order, and ends at the FIRST failure or cancel of any item (`Task.WhenAny`) with that exception: it then withdraws its interest in the others through a linked token, which stops a transfer only if no one else asked for it (a Settings page that did keeps it). `SkillsDownloads.Pending(item)` and an `Install` overload taking the part callback are public for this. NOTE: the pipeline runs one operation at a time, so an item that waits behind another's held download cannot fail before it starts; the tests order their holds accordingly.
14. **A catalogue update keeps an installed skill set (finding 4; closes ED-NEW-f-sk-13 item 6 for skill sets and plugins).** `SkillsPipeline` writes, with the route and before state.json selects the pin, `addons\manifests\<sha256 of id and pin>.json` (`PipelineManifests`, its own JSON context): the catalogue entry the install was verified against, as the catalogue file writes a one-item catalogue. `CatalogueTrust.Restore` uses the current entry when its pin is the installed pin (as before) and otherwise that kept entry, which must belong to the same id and pin, be fully pinned and hold a valid inventory; the descriptor is made from it, never from installed bytes, so the tree is still verified against exactly what was verified at install (a tampered tree is Damaged, tested). The pipeline then offers the update (`UpdateAvailable`, one update row). Anything off about the kept entry (absent, another pin, not parseable, an invalid inventory) leaves the item unrestored as before. ENGINEERING DECISION on the trust root: the kept entry lives in the `addons` folder only Marrow writes, like state.json and the route it already trusts; it is not read from an installed folder (ED-321 (3)). A tool or package set still has no persisted descriptor (UNRESOLVED, unchanged: its derived tree hashes are not kept). A Repair of a set at an older pin than the catalogue's re-fetches the catalogue's pin and fails closed against the kept inventory; the user's way forward is Update.
15. **Update everything reconciles when idle (finding 7).** A change of the installed set during a run is remembered: `UpdateEverythingProduction.Refresh` subscribes once to the service's `Changed` and gives the service its items again on the main actor as soon as it is not busy (`Forget` drops the subscription). Replaces item 7's "left alone until the next change".
16. **Words and space (findings 8, 9 and 10).** These came with `codex/f-sk-15` c7526e100: "Ready in new chats" on an installed skill set, the blocking requirement rounded up ("Needs 13 GB free on C:."), and the reviewed Hide and manual-recovery sentences. No SK-16 change.
17. **Tests added for the fixes (after the code; the REVIEW_ cases were seen red first).** `FetchReviewFixesTests` 6: an offer's failure keeps a transfer a Settings page also asked for and stops one only it asked for, a late joiner's replay precedes newer reports, a kept entry that does not hold up or belongs to another pin is not used, a tampered tree is Damaged against the kept inventory. Existing assertions are otherwise unchanged.

2. **Tools-only PATH without a skill generation.** SK-11e originally treated a null skill launch as an unchanged environment. ONDEMAND 3.6/4.2 and the merged SK-11c PATH exception require addons\bin on every bound child, including tools-only installs with no enabled skills. ProviderSkillEnvironment now uses the already-bound ProviderChildEnvironment when no generation exists; an unbound fixture still returns the same map without touching user folders. ## ED-372

T9 Windows SK-16 repair (2026-10-05), explicitly authorized by the lead. This supersedes only the whole-download operation-slot behavior described in ED-368; SK-16 stays integrated.

1. **Production defect, not only test ordering.** The existing offer-failure test fails twice alone at the train head and pre-flake head. The original fixed SK-16 input a9d2b2f8f also fails five of ten isolated executions. Task.Run start order decides whether failing S1 or held S3 first occupies SkillsPipeline's operation semaphore. The semaphore was held across the whole download, so S3 can prevent S1 from reaching its failure. AcceptTerms also synchronously waited for that same semaphore: the deterministic held-download regression times out before the fix, matching the SK-14 UI-freeze concern.
2. **Only the download releases the slot.** InstallAsync, UpdateCoreAsync and RepairCoreAsync call one DownloadOutsideOperation helper. It releases operation around the asynchronous download and reacquires it in finally, so every caller still owns exactly one slot on every exit. Installation, verification, route publication and GC remain serialized. The helper snapshots the item and its dependency records and rejects changed records before publishing; a reset serial also rejects a download that would otherwise reinstall an Available item after Reset. Cancellation and pinned-plan validation remain in force. No state of an in-flight download is persisted.
3. **Terms are a short state-only commit.** AcceptTerms builds its next state from the current state under gate, without operation.Wait, following the existing SK-14 SetDeclined pattern. Install/update/repair commits already preserve the current accepted-terms/declined/found lists under the same gate. SetDeclined exists on the held SK-14 branch and is not promoted here; its gate-only implementation is compatible with this change. Fledge W3 must preserve this AcceptTerms gate-only commit when merging its same-file correction, and must retain the three download-helper calls and reset invalidation guard.
4. **Deterministic test, unchanged failure assertion.** FetchReviewFixesTests starts S3, waits for its explicit entry signal, attaches the offer, then cancels the first asker's interest so only the offer wants S3. The original IOException/20-second assertion, S3-stop guard and absent-installed-folder assertion remain byte-exact; an extra assertion proves the initial asker detached. New FetchDownloadBlockingTests prove terms return during the held download and survive its commit, and reset returns during it and prevents a later install. All three regressions fail on unmodified production (three timeouts), then pass after the fix; the original offer method passes both exact isolated reruns. The complete Services skills scope passes 748/748. Full train gates and reviewer-suite retention are reported separately.

SK-18, import skills from other apps on the PC (OD-0118, with the owner's later rulings: no design review, your wording is fine; auto-detection). Branch cloud/sk-18 from claude/verify-terminal-20261001. ENGINEERING DECISION throughout; nothing here is a source fact, because the pinned source has no such feature. The lead retains ED numbering.

1. Scanner (src/Marrow.Services/Port/Skills/Import/ForeignSkillScanner.cs, ForeignFrontmatter.cs). It reads, and never writes, these places under the home folder: .claude/skills; .claude/plugins (every skills folder below it, labelled with the plugin folder, version-named folders skipped, the newest write per plugin and skill wins); .codex/skills and .agents/skills (Codex); .gemini/antigravity-cli/skills, .gemini/config/skills and .gemini/skills (Antigravity); .cursor/skills and .cursor/rules/*.mdc and *.md (Cursor; a rule becomes a skill named from the file, its description from the front matter or the first body line); and any folders the person picks. Name and one-line description come from the front matter through a tolerant reader (BOM, CRLF, quotes, folded and literal blocks, comments; flow and anchor values ignored; never throws). Broken items are left out and counted: no front matter, no description, no usable name, not text, too large (256 KB), an empty rule, the 1000-skill limit, depth 8. Links that are reparse points are reported, not followed. A relative home is refused.

2. Library (ImportedSkillsLibrary.cs). Under the skills root, imported/index.json (version 1, written atomically) and imported/copies/<id>/. Copy keeps Marrow's own copy of the whole skill folder (200 files, 5 MB at most). Link keeps only the path and reads the original each time it is handed out, so a change is picked up and a missing original shows "Original missing" and hands nothing out. A duplicate is the same app and source path, or the same name ignoring case; the answer is keep both (a unique "-<app>" name), replace (the new one is made first, the old removed after, and the old on/off setting kept) or skip. An unreadable index loads empty and is copied to index.json.unreadable before the first write; an index from a newer Marrow is shown and never changed. Each imported skill can be switched off and removed; removing deletes only Marrow's own copy. The duplicate question is asked with the library free (a regression test holds it), because the person may take a while and the page and the chats read the library meanwhile.

3. Handoff (SkillGenerations, IImportedSkillSource, ImportedGenerationSkill). Imported skills enter every generation of every provider after the catalogue's skills, at the provider's own place (skills/<name>/ for claude and grok, <name>/ for the others), under the same name, clash, description and budget rules as every skill; one that does not fit is left out as "import/<id>". A generation with no imports has exactly the key it had; with imports the key also covers each file's hash, so a changed link gives the next chat a new generation while a running chat keeps its own. Tested at generation level for claude, codex and agy. The launch wiring of SK-11 (--plugin-dir, extra roots) and SK-17 Antigravity are not in this branch, so nothing here changes how a provider process is started.

4. Sheet and page (src/Marrow.App/Port/Skills/Import, Pages/LibraryPage.cs, SkillsPageSeams.Imports). Skills page only, never Plugins. "Import skills" button with one plain line under the providers section; the sheet opens in the window like Download all (440 wide, glass, wash, Escape, Reduce Motion), grouped by app, the port's tick box per skill and per app, a Copy / Link choice with a crossfading plain note, "Choose a folder…" through the system folder chooser, a problems line, the duplicate panel with Keep both / Replace / Skip and a tick "Do this for the rest", "Import" (with the count) and "Import all", then Close with the result. Imported skills are listed under "Imported skills" with a switch, a quiet "from <app> · Copied/Linked" tag and a two-step Remove (trash, then "Remove?"). Everything that comes and goes folds or crossfades and the ticks ease (OD-0076); under Reduce Motion each lands at once. Escape during an import only hides the sheet (an open question is answered Skip for the rest); the sheet returns at the end.

5. Auto-detection (owner ruling, ImportDetector.cs). The Skills page asks the scanner, with no picked folder, when it opens and listens to the same places while it shows (a FileSystemWatcher per place that exists, deep; for a place that does not exist yet, the nearest folder that does, shallow and limited to the next name, so an app installed later is noticed). A change waits 800 ms of quiet, scans once and listens again. When something found is not yet imported and not dismissed, one quiet line shows: "Found 12 skills in Claude Code and Codex · Import", with a dismiss cross. Import opens the sheet, which scans the same way and so already lists every detected app, nothing ticked; choosing another folder stays an extra. Dismiss is kept in imported/dismissed.json (the keys it was dismissed for): the line stays away until a skill not seen before appears. The line goes when everything found is imported. Nothing is imported by detecting; nothing in the other apps is written (the watch only listens, tested with a before and after fingerprint). The listening stops when the page is left.

6. Words that the owner has now accepted (keep plain and short): Import skills; Imported skills; "Bring in skills that other AI apps keep on this PC. Nothing in those apps is changed."; the sheet's title, sub line, Copy / Link notes, Choose a folder…, Cancel, Import, Import all, Close, the duplicate question and its three answers; "from <app> · Copied/Linked"; Original missing; Remove, Remove?; Found N skills in A and B; Import; Dismiss. So these are MISSING from the design sources and are NOT written: (a) the card's asked sentence and the line saying why the item is needed (the step it blocks); (b) the decline control and its label; (c) the captions for done, continuing and declined (5.5 says only that the declined card "collapses to one line that says where the item can be downloaded later"); (d) the terms step's place inside the card; (e) the card's geometry, spacing and its place in a reply; (f) the shape of the "failed" fold's fallback inside the card. Everything below uses only words the design draws for the same states on the Settings page (`LibraryWords`), and the card is NOT MOUNTED in any thread.
2. **The card's states as a value (`OfferCardProjector`, `OfferCardView`, Services).** Asked: the item titles in dependency order, the combined size, each source host once (the host of the catalogue's source address), "Download · size" as the primary label (the design's), on unless a terms step is owed (5.4: it stays inside asked), a decline available, no cancel. Downloading: bytes and percent (rounded down, none without a total, never above 100), Cancel, no download button, no decline. Checking: "Checking…", no button. Failed: "Didn't download", the reason as the downloader gave it (S1, never paraphrased), "Retry" and a decline. Done, continuing and declined: no word, no button (see 1). ENGINEERING DECISION: Cancel is offered while the bytes come in and not while they are checked, as the Settings row does.
3. **The card (`OfferCardControl` over `IOfferCardSource`, App; `SkillsOfferFlow` implements the interface).** A panel in the reply's own layout (never an overlay, so it cannot cover the composer's text; tested above a text box, in every state, at 420 points wide). Titles, then the host line, then one action line per state in the Settings page's own controls (the primary glass capsule, the bar with its percent and a cancel glyph, the spinner with "Checking…", the warning glyph with the reason and Retry). Every change of state crossfades on the frame clock, the bar and percent only move forward, and Reduce Motion (the pages' own helper: the window's setting, the system's, or no frame source) lands it at once (OD-0076; tested frame by frame with the clock taken by hand). Done, continuing and declined collapse the card (`IsVisible` false). The decline control is not drawn (1b); the offer's `Decline()` is reachable by whoever mounts the card. Return is the primary action's only while the card itself has focus (the event's source is the card and it is focused) and the primary action is on; a focused button already clicks on Return, and Return in the composer never reaches the card (tested: composer focused, card focused, terms owed, mid-download).
4. **Wiring to the host (`SkillsOfferFlows.Create(runtime, host)`).** One offer for one chat over `SkillsHost`: the catalogue it was opened with (`SkillsHost.Catalogue`, new), the pipeline's state, the host's shared downloads (`SkillsHost.OfferDownloads`: an offer joins a download Settings has running, and the reverse, ED-NEW-cloud-sk-16) and the pipeline's new `SetDeclined(state)` (state.json; only the declined list is taken, so an offer cannot change an installed record; written before the provider is answered, ONDEMAND 5.4/5.5). Tested end to end through the real flow: accepting an item that cannot be fetched (every embedded catalogue item is still Unpinned) fails the card with the one unavailable message and leaves no download running; a decline lands in state.json for the chat. ENGINEERING DECISION, UNCHANGED: nothing in the app calls `Create`. A made offer holds a provider's command and answers a model's `request_tool` only when someone presses its card, and the card has no place in a reply (1e), so no thread gets one: the first one made without a card to answer it would hang the model's request. Mounting is the next step once the card's placement is in the repository.
5. **"Download it yourself": the words exist in the repository, so they are written.** `ManualFallbackWords` (Core) is `sd-page.js` fbBlock byte for byte: "Download it yourself"; "Get "; "Put it in "; "Open download page ↗"; "Open folder"; "Check again"; the two step-3 sentences ("Marrow checks its SHA-256 against the pinned one and installs it." for a tool, "Marrow checks every file against its pinned hash and installs it." for a set); the folder `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Marrow Code\addons\downloads\manual\` (the design marks it a proposal: "ED, UN until built"); "Checking…" and "Installed" are `LibraryWords`'. The design's own "ED" tag beside the folder is its marker, not a word of the page, and is not drawn. Step 1's two texts come from the catalogue by the rule the design's FB table follows (`ManualFallbacks`, tested against the design's own entries for every item it lists that the catalogue has: A1, A3 to A5, O1 to O4, T2 to T10, P1): a skill set or plugin at one commit is "the repository at commit <7 digits>, as a .zip" from "github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<7 digits>"; one at per-skill commits is "the <n> skill folders at their pinned commits (...)"; a tool is its artifacts' names joined by " and " from the directory of its first artifact's address without "www." (or, where the catalogue gives an artifact no address, its source page, the vendor's releases page); a Python package set is "the pinned wheels named in wheels.txt in that folder" from "pypi.org". DIVERGENCES from the design: Python's embedded package (T1) is two items here, so its text names only its own file (the design's one entry names the pip wheel too); a Node package set and an item with no pin (A6) have none (the design draws none). The block sits under a failed item's warning in the Settings detail's failure fold (`ManualBlock`, `DetailView`): the heading and three numbered steps, "Open download page ↗" (opens `https://<source>` through the workspace seam), "Open folder" (makes the folder, then opens it) and, beside step 3, "Check again", which gives way to "Checking…" while the item is fetched and checked and to "Installed" when that ends well; an item that never failed shows none of these words.
6. **"Check again" (`LibraryController.CheckAgain`, `ManualFiles.PlaceFolder`).** Only a failed item acts. Every file in the manual folder is checked against the item's pinned inputs by length and SHA-256, never by name; a file that is none of them is left out and never touched; the user's files stay. A skill set or plugin may come as the repository's .zip (the design's step 1): each entry of a zip in the folder is checked the same way whatever folder it sits in, so the zip's folder name never matters. Each match is kept in the part folder as `<8 hex digits>.part` (SK-16's `ManualFiles.Place`), so the normal download, which the controller then runs, finishes it from the whole `.part` with no request (tested against the fake server's log), and fetches whatever was not found. ENGINEERING DECISION: the design says Marrow "checks every file ... and installs it" and does not say what happens when the folder holds only some; the rest is fetched the normal way. ISkillsLibraryBackend gains default members (`ManualFolder`, `PlaceManualFiles`, `OpenManualPage`, `OpenManualFolder`), so every scripted backend compiles; both copies of `FakeLibraryBackend` record them.

(b) The terms step inside the card (its button stays off while terms are owed; there is nowhere to accept them from the card). (c) Constructing offers for threads (4). (d) The Minimize pill and the Add button (not this row). (e) No live look, no real download, no provider chat, no browser or folder opened (DL-20).

9. **Flights begin in the order asked (`SkillsDownloads`).** Starting each flight on the pool let an item asked second reach the pipeline first (its wait is first come first served), so a failing first item could wait behind a long one: the REVIEW_ case for an offer's failure, and my own test of it, depended on that order and failed once under a full-suite load. The short part of a flight that ends at its first real wait now runs on one exclusive scheduler, one flight at a time in the order queued; the transfer itself runs wherever it runs. Ten runs of the Fetch and Pages slices then passed with only the Windows-only drive test failing.

## ED-385
ENGINEERING DECISION (SK-14 W3 / H1, unified with T9 SK-16 ED-372): use the already reviewed SK-16 whole-download-slot repair, not a separate locking design. Install, update and repair all use DownloadOutsideOperation; unconditional slot reacquisition preserves ownership on every exit. A completed download revalidates resetSerial, the item record and dependency records and rechecks terms before publication. AcceptTerms commits from current state under gate, exactly like the retained SetDeclined path. Install, verification, routing and GC remain serialized. No whole download can block another item's failure or synchronous terms/decline path. The original inherited HostOfferTermsConcurrencyTests was preserved and committed before repair, with its 5-second red witness retained. Its acceptance remains recorded through eventual installation and host restart. Imported T9 ordering and reset regressions retain all original assertions. W3 green: 17/17 including those regressions, decline behavior and Traceability; build zero warnings/errors. Source provenance: T9 production commit 3287a4fba373959d65144ef6c973f5aa830d33d8. The same helper and all three call sites must survive integration; only SetDeclined is an additional SK-14 method.


ENGINEERING DECISION (SK-14 W3 / M1 and L1): offer detection reads an immutable snapshot of persisted facts plus the host's live flight IDs. The projection is never committed to state.json; installed/update/removing guards, accepted terms, declined offers and found-on-PC facts are retained. The real SkillsOfferFlows.Create path is covered with a held host download and the unchanged exact 4/18-byte progress expectations. Attachment captures a flight and increments its interest under the same downloads gate; a missing flight throws the existing No existing download is bound message and never falls through to Install. A two-item synchronous-replay regression removes the later flight between joins and proves there is no replacement download.

ENGINEERING DECISION (SK-14 W3 / M2): CheckAgain publishes the existing Checking state before starting a worker for synchronous manual-file verification/copy. It restores the original failed overlay before calling the original Download path, retaining terms, found-on-PC, busy/run guards and installed-item update/repair routing. A per-placement cancellation token uses the existing transfer registry and spans the queued first-install handoff; cancellation never starts installation after held verification ends. Non-OOM placement errors follow the controller's existing Failed/error.Message policy. No product strings, file pin checks, assertions or time bounds change. Tests-first: live factory, attach race, blocking placement, placement error, and cancellation each have a preserved red witness; test commit 44446fb50 precedes these production edits. Original interrupted H1 acceptance test is byte-exact.


ENGINEERING DECISION (W3 Windows manual-folder gate): the unchanged original OpenManualFolder regression failed twice because SwiftURL.FileURLWithPath deliberately accepts only POSIX absolute paths, whereas ManualFolder is a native Windows drive path. Keep that pinned Swift API unchanged; convert the native folder with System.Uri.AbsoluteUri, then SwiftURL.Create, at the Windows-only host backend. The original open/folder-exists assertions remain, with an additive exact native-URI assertion committed before repair (880e5cfc8, red retained). The method passes twice after the one-line production change. Final affected Services 241/241 and App 150/150 including Traceability; all five H1/M1/M2/atomic/cancel regressions pass twice (Services 5/5, App 1/1 each). Broad skills history is kept separately: 777 passed/4 failed of 781; three provider fixture failures fail twice on this old SK-14 base but their existing corrected fixtures are already on T9. No provider changes are copied into W3; integration must retain those T4 review fixes.


## ED-386
ENGINEERING DECISION (T9 batch 9 integration): join trial-H asynchronous developer inventory with the existing SK-16 refresh lifecycle instead of dropping either. Remember captures the current async source, Configure observes its task with the reviewed original error policy, and Refresh awaits it on the actor without blocking; recheck the captured factory and service busy state after the wait. Busy updates retain their rows and subscribe for reconciliation when idle. Forget releases the subscription and invalidates the captured factory. UE-6 keeps its retained item array for exact offered-release lookup while incoming Office pending-version polling remains. ACPSession keeps both SK-17 owned MCP/late-stop safeguards and T4 effective argv/PATH/tap cleanup. SkillsHost keeps both imported skills/generation wiring and shared downloads/offer terms. The pipeline keeps the already reviewed ED-372 helper byte-exact and SK-14 SetDeclined, with one current-state gate for both terms and decline. No assertion, test time bound, error wording, native policy or process recipe changes. All incoming tests and earlier review tests are retained and the combined non-native gate plus exact conflict-path regressions determines readiness.

## ED-NEW-skills-backend-5 - Owned provider launch composition (RR-15, 2026-10-07)

ENGINEERING DECISION under OD-0099: compose the existing SK-11a..f provider adapters through one Services factory and the host's trusted managed/imported generation builder. ThreadRuntime prepares new/resumed CLI and native sessions, verifies reuse, binds native use_skill/request_tool to the per-chat flow, and retains each generation until real child exit. JSONRPC exposes additive ChildExited; Claude/Codex/Copilot/Pi/Command Code lifetime seams retain readers through EOF, Stop and failed initialization, with all Command Code per-turn readers awaited. Cursor/Antigravity keep their existing seams. Respect effective provider homes, OpenCode config order and read-only Command Code path arrays; no original provider configuration is written. Additive fakes: 31 new Services tests and 60 selected App runtime tests pass, including source fingerprints, progressive disclosure, all family bindings, resume/reuse and delayed fake-child exit. Full Windows acceptance remains required; RR-13/14 remain separate blockers. No UI file or existing test/assertion/reference changed. Details: porting/first-release/reviews/skills-backend-t35/RR-15.md.

Move only that helper to its own file and add R-TEST-4 metadata; all assertions remain unchanged. Core traceability 3/3, Services additive-plus-traceability 34/34, App runtime-plus-traceability 63/63. Final Core skills 479/479; Services skills 891 passed with the same 16 failing and 48 skipped cases as the untouched base (860 passed). Full Core/Services Linux attempts do not prove Windows acceptance. Five row commits and the consolidated NOT READY report at porting/first-release/reviews/skills-backend-t35.md record the unresolved catalogue/installer contracts and Windows-run needs.


## ED-NEW-skills-backend-6 - Round 2 custom-source backend (RR-18, 2026-10-07)

Lead ruling: origin/claude/lead-rulings:R-gaps-round2.md, T35, assigns the Folder/ZIP/GitHub backend to T35 and requires an early push for T36. OD-0099 custom additions use a separate own-items registry, never the OD-0118 provider-import registry or fabricated catalogue licences. Check retains immutable validated bytes; Add publishes a copied tree then commits provenance and file pins atomically. Commands are registered by committed registry entries, verified before use, retained across reopen, and disabled/removed explicitly. Production input is anonymous public GitHub only, resolved to a full commit; no clone or scripts. Archive/folder resource bounds are 4096 files / 128 MiB with Windows-safe relative paths and no links. Reset of managed downloads preserves user-owned copies. CustomSourcesTests were written before the API and first failed for missing backend types; in-memory filesystem/GitHub fakes exercise all three sources, restart, frozen input, provenance, unsafe paths, failed commit rollback, command registration, duplicate/forged tokens and concurrent selected items. No existing guard/test is changed. Binding details: porting/first-release/reviews/skills-backend-t35/custom-source-api.md.


## ED-NEW-skills-backend-7 - Round 2 ordered service starts (RR-44, 2026-10-07)

The existing exclusive start scheduler did not reserve enqueue order under the flight-creation gate. Join first called listeners/Notify outside the gate, so a blocked first observer allowed a later request to enqueue first. OrderedServiceStartsTests forces this with a blocked first requesting-thread observer, then requests an independent item: unchanged service starts [S3,S1], expected [S1,S3]. Enqueue the short async Run entry under the same gate after incrementing its interest; callbacks stay outside the gate and the transfer does not hold it. Existing joins, cancellation, dependency sharing and offer/backend regressions remain unchanged and pass. RR-44 selection/in-flight UI presentation belongs to T36.


## ED-NEW-skills-backend-8 - Round 2 own-item provider bindings (RR-18, 2026-10-07)

Five added CustomHostBindingTests first failed against the early API: commands were absent from child PATH and plugin skills absent from generations. ProviderCustomCommands now applies committed/verified per-item command bins to every child environment without changing the parent or putting custom commands ahead of existing PC tools. Service composition stays outside the standalone BCL-only Marrow.Shim assembly. Own skill and plugin-skill snapshots join imported snapshots without fabricated catalogue records. Claude/Grok generations copy supported Claude plugin manifests, hooks and resources; Codex-only manifests contribute ordinary skills, without a claim of Claude-compatible hooks. Selection/clash/budget filtering removes excluded skill files. Generation file pins and leases preserve already launched copies after own-item Remove. CustomToolBundleTests additionally proved a primary executable must be selected by the entered command when helpers coexist; ambiguous bundles remain invalid. All input/network/filesystem effects for custom checks/adds use in-memory ports in tests; generation publication uses the existing disposable store with fake protection/locks, never an installer or provider process. No existing tests or wire assertions changed.


## ED-NEW-skills-backend-9 - Round 2 explicit own-skill priority (RR-18, 2026-10-07)

OD-0099/skills-PLAN 2.7 says the user's own skills are listed first and must not be crowded out. Four test-first CustomSkillPriorityTests found the new explicit additions inherited OD-0118's separate catalogue-first import policy, and lost source disable-model-invocation flags. They reserve names/budget first, list first, and preserve named-only invocation; providers without that flag support omit them. Existing provider imports retain their previous name/budget/key behavior and all nine ImportedHandoff cases pass unchanged. The actual source flag is part of the content identity. Custom checks fail closed on unreadable disclosure metadata. No original test, tolerance, reference, catalogue fact or assertion changed.


## ED-NEW-skills-backend-10 - Round 2 GitHub sub-folder sources and concurrent own copies (RR-18, 2026-10-07)

The locked T36 Add sheet already sends owner/repository[/sub-folder] in Location. The root-only Repository validator rejected its optional path; URI AbsolutePath also erased dot segments before validation. Test-first fake HTTP cases reproduced both. Validate the original URL path, normalize sub-folder backslashes to forward slashes, reject dot/empty/absolute/encoded/unsafe Windows paths, and reject repository components that become dot segments after stripping .git. Resolve HEAD once; subtree checks request only commit-pinned contents listings and raw files beneath the selected folder, never the whole repository archive. Reject links/submodules, non-child or duplicate paths, saturated/incomplete API listings, invalid sizes and byte-count mismatches. Persist normalized Provenance.SubPath, the exact commit, pinned contents URL and selected-tree fingerprint; installed file pins remain exact. Existing root requests retain their archive hash behavior.

ParallelCustomInstallTests separately reproduced the new API holding its registry gate during both file copies. Reserve names/commands under the gate, publish independent private trees concurrently, then serialize atomic registry commits; failure rolls back only that tree and preserves its check token. No UI, existing baseline test or catalogue fact changes. Custom plus ordered starts and traceability: 57/57 pass, entirely fake source files/HTTP. Red and green witnesses are in skills-backend-t35-evidence/round2-*.log. T36 can merge this branch without changing its five-field request adapter; binding documentation and T36-handoff-round2.md identify the source/provenance contract.


## ED-NEW-skills-backend-11 - Round 2 official-source pin generator (RR-13, 2026-10-07)

The lead's T35 ruling requires a checked-in generator and fake fixtures, leaving the real run to the owner's PC. pin-generator.mjs is transport-injected and import-side-effect free. A complete manifest must name all 29 source IDs exactly, with artifacts and official version/licence metadata selectors for each. Checked-in source policies constrain HTTPS origins and every manual redirect; only an official repository release may redirect to GitHub's release CDN. No credentials, old catalogue licence fallback, filename-derived version, empty/unknown licence or unsafe Windows output path is accepted. The source metadata's exact raw bytes, SHA-256, size, requested/final URL, selector and actual UTC read time accompany its own observed value. Artifact streaming hashes SHA-256 and counts/saves those same bytes, checking selected version and any published digest/size expectations. generate-pins.mjs is an explicit manual command with a real-fetch flag, new output folder and staged complete publication; no application catalogue or installer writes.

Fourteen generator fixture cases within the 19-case combined suite prove all 29 IDs, independent known-byte SHA-256/size, metadata provenance/body retention, empty/missing facts, strict UTF-8/base64, size/hash/version mismatches, rejected origins/redirects, Windows output collisions and a UTC date boundary. Tests first failed for the missing module and then for each recorded strictness gap. All tests inject bytes/transport; no real source network run or install was performed. The embedded catalogue and every SkillsCataloguePinsTests assertion remain byte-identical. This implements the Round 2 generator, not completion of the 29 real catalogue entries. Local source metadata selection/pin run/review and guarded catalogue publication remain required.
